title: Use adjective forms to describe how or when an action happens
goal: You'll be able to change い-adjectives and な-adjectives into forms that modify verbs.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe how an action happens
text: An adjective can describe the manner of an action. Here, 丁寧に tells us that father is washing the car carefully. The verb still tells us what he does.
Use ～く for い-adjectives and ～に for な-adjectives. The English translation may use an adverb such as “carefully,” or a phrase such as “in large letters.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Change the final い to く
text: Remove only the final い of an い-adjective and add く before the action: 早い → 早く. The verb carries tense and politeness; the adverb does not change for a past action.
いい is irregular: its adverb is よく. In よく聞いてください, よく means “carefully” or “well.” In other contexts it can mean “often,” so read it together with the action.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Use に after a な-adjective
text: Use the な-adjective stem plus に, without な or だ. 静かな → 静かに. Remember that きれい is a な-adjective even though it ends in い: use きれいに.

formation: い-adjective without final い + く + Verb
な-adjective stem + に + Verb

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{丁寧|ていねい}**に**{車|くるま}を{洗|あら}っています。
examples.romaji: chichi wa teinei ni kuruma o aratte imasu.
examples.en: My father is carefully washing the car.

examples.romaji: い → く
examples.en: early → early (modifying an action)

examples.ja: {静|しず}か → {静|しず}か**に**
examples.romaji: stem + に
examples.en: quiet → quietly

examples.romaji: いい → よく
examples.en: good → well; carefully

examples.romaji: hayai → hayaku

examples.ja: {静|しず}か → {静|しず}か**に**
examples.romaji: shizuka → shizuka ni
ii → yoku

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{早|はや}**く**{起|お}きます。
examples.romaji: ren wa hayaku okimasu.
examples.en: Ren gets up early.

examples.ja: {名前|なまえ}を{大|おお}き**く**{書|か}いてください。
examples.romaji: namae o ookiku kaite kudasai.
examples.en: Please write your name in large letters.

examples.ja: **よく**{聞|き}いてください。
examples.romaji: yoku kiite kudasai.
examples.en: Please listen carefully.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{静|しず}か**に**{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいます。
examples.romaji: mei wa shizuka ni hon o yonde imasu.
examples.en: Mei is reading a book quietly.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{字|じ}をきれい**に**{書|か}きます。
examples.romaji: mei wa ji o kirei ni kakimasu.
examples.en: Mei writes neatly.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{丁寧|ていねい}**に**{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.romaji: chichi wa teinei ni setsumei shimasu.
examples.en: My father explains carefully.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}は{道|みち}が{混|こ}むから、{早|はや}**く**{家|いえ}を{出|で}ます。
examples.romaji: asa wa michi ga komu kara, hayaku ie o demasu.
examples.en: The roads get crowded in the morning, so I leave home early.

examples.ja: {薬|くすり}の{説明|せつめい}を{丁寧|ていねい}**に**{読|よ}んでください。
examples.romaji: kusuri no setsumei o teinei ni yonde kudasai.
examples.en: Please read the medicine instructions carefully.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}だから、{静|しず}か**に**{話|はな}してね。
examples.romaji: toshokan da kara, shizuka ni hanashite ne.
examples.en: We're in the library, so talk quietly, okay?

examples.ja: ～く・～に (adverbs)
examples.romaji: Use adjective forms to describe how or when an action happens
examples.en: 7 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Turn an adjective into a noun naming a quality
goal: You'll be able to change adjectives into nouns for qualities such as height, strength, or convenience.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Name a quality
text: ～さ turns a description into the name of a quality. You can measure a height or discuss how convenient something is. The result behaves like a noun, so particles attach after さ.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～さ
text: Remove the final い from an い-adjective, or use the な-adjective stem. いい becomes よさ. Use this for a degree or property; do not assume every adjective produces an equally common noun.

formation: い-adjective without final い / な-adjective stem + さ

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{木|き}の{高|たか}**さ**を{測|はか}っています。
examples.romaji: mei wa ki no takasa o hakatte imasu.
examples.en: Mei is measuring the height of a tree.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}を{選|えら}ぶときは、{広|ひろ}**さ**が{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.romaji: heya o erabu toki wa, hirosa ga taisetsu desu.
examples.en: When you choose an apartment, its size is important.

examples.ja: この{荷物|にもつ}の{重|おも}**さ**は{三|さん}キロです。
examples.romaji: kono nimotsu no omosa wa sankiro desu.
examples.en: The weight of this luggage is three kilograms.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}の{便利|べんり}**さ**が{好|す}きです。
examples.romaji: kono machi no benrisa ga suki desu.
examples.en: I like the convenience of this town.

examples.ja: {飛行機|ひこうき}に{乗|の}る{前|まえ}に、かばんの{重|おも}**さ**を{調|しら}べました。
examples.romaji: hikouki ni noru mae ni, kaban no omosa o shirabemashita.
examples.en: Before getting on the plane, I checked the weight of my bag.

examples.ja: {富士山|ふじさん}の{高|たか}**さ**を{知|し}っていますか。
examples.romaji: fujisan no takasa o shitte imasu ka.
examples.en: Do you know the height of Mount Fuji?

examples.ja: このプールの{深|ふか}**さ**は{一|いち}メートルです。
examples.romaji: kono puuru no fukasa wa ichi meetoru desu.
examples.en: This pool is one meter deep.

examples.ja: ～さ
examples.romaji: Turn an adjective into a noun naming a quality
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Make someone or something become a certain way
goal: You'll be able to describe deliberately changing a quality, condition, or setting.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Deliberately change a condition
text: ～くする and ～にする describe making something become a certain way. Someone actively changes the condition; the thing being changed is commonly marked with を.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～くする・～にする
text: Use 小さくする for making something small and 静かにする for making it quiet. Conjugate する for tense and politeness. Noun + にする can also mean choosing or designating something.

formation: い-adjective without い + くする / な-adjective stem or Noun + にする

examples.ja: {父|ちち}はテレビの{音|おと}を{小|ちい}さ**くします**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa terebi no oto o chiisaku shimasu.
examples.en: My father turns down the television volume.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}をきれい**にしました**。
examples.romaji: heya o kirei ni shimashita.
examples.en: I made the room clean.

examples.ja: テレビの{音|おと}を{小|ちい}さ**くしてください**。
examples.romaji: terebi no oto o chiisaku shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please turn down the TV volume.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}では{静|しず}か**にしてください**。
examples.romaji: toshokan de wa shizuka ni shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please be quiet in the library.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}を{教室|きょうしつ}**にします**。
examples.romaji: kono heya o kyoushitsu ni shimasu.
examples.en: I will turn this room into a classroom.

examples.ja: {暑|あつ}いですね。エアコンを{少|すこ}し{強|つよ}**くしましょう**か。
examples.romaji: atsui desu ne. eakon o sukoshi tsuyoku shimashou ka.
examples.en: It's hot, isn't it? Shall I turn the air conditioner up a little?

examples.ja: お{客|きゃく}さんが{来|く}るので、{玄関|げんかん}をきれい**にしました**。
examples.romaji: okyakusan ga kuru node, genkan o kirei ni shimashita.
examples.en: Guests were coming, so I cleaned up the entrance.

examples.ja: {時間|じかん}がないので、{今日|きょう}の{話|はなし}は{短|みじか}**くします**。
examples.romaji: jikan ga nai node, kyou no hanashi wa mijikaku shimasu.
examples.en: We're short on time, so I'll keep today's talk short.

examples.ja: ～くする・～にする
examples.romaji: Make someone or something become a certain way
examples.en: 7 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: The way to do something
goal: You'll be able to turn an action into a phrase meaning how to do it or the way it is done.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Explain how to do something
text: Attach 方 to a verb stem to name the way of doing it. This is useful when asking how to use a machine or read an unfamiliar word. Here 方 is read かた.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～方
text: Remove ます and add 方: 読みます → 読み方. The result is a noun. A related object commonly uses の: この漢字の読み方. For する compounds, use noun + の + 仕方, such as 勉強の仕方.

formation: Verb ます-stem + 方

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{芽衣|めい}にカメラの{使|つか}い**{方|かた}**を{教|おし}えます。
examples.romaji: ren wa mei ni kamera no tsukaikata o oshiemasu.
examples.en: Ren teaches Mei how to use the camera.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}で{地下鉄|ちかてつ}の{乗|の}り**{方|かた}**を{聞|き}きました。
examples.romaji: eki de chikatetsu no norikata o kikimashita.
examples.en: At the station, I asked how to take the subway.

examples.ja: この{漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}み**{方|かた}**を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.romaji: kono kanji no yomikata o oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: Please tell me how to read this kanji.

examples.ja: {切符|きっぷ}の{買|か}い**{方|かた}**が{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: kippu no kaikata ga wakarimasen.
examples.en: I do not know how to buy a ticket.

examples.ja: この{洗濯機|せんたくき}の{使|つか}い**{方|かた}**が{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: kono sentakuki no tsukaikata ga wakarimasen.
examples.en: I don't know how to use this washing machine.

examples.ja: {子|こ}どもにお{箸|はし}の{持|も}ち**{方|かた}**を{教|おし}えています。
examples.romaji: kodomo ni ohashi no mochikata o oshiete imasu.
examples.en: I'm teaching my child how to hold chopsticks.

examples.ja: すみません、{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}への{行|い}き**{方|かた}**を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, yuubinkyoku e no ikikata o oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the post office?

examples.ja: ～方
examples.romaji: The way to do something
examples.en: Want extra conjugation drills for -masu Stem Conjugations across Group 1 (Godan), Group 2 (Ichidan), and Irregular verbs? Use our Interactive Verb Conjugation Practice Tool or review the 13-Form Japanese Verb Conjugation Chart.

pattern: ～でできている・～からできている
title: Say what something is made of or made from
goal: You'll be able to identify a visible material or an original ingredient that has been transformed.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Identify a material or source
text: ～でできている tells what material something consists of. ～からできている can highlight an original ingredient that has been transformed. The choice reflects how the speaker presents the material, rather than an absolute visible/invisible rule.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～でできている・～からできている
text: Use で for an ordinary material description. Use から when tracing a product back to its source. できています is a polite description of composition, not the potential meaning “can do.”

formation: Material + でできている / Source ingredient + からできている

examples.ja: この{椅子|いす}は{木|き}**でできています**。
examples.romaji: kono isu wa ki de dekite imasu.
examples.en: This chair is made of wood.

examples.ja: {日本酒|にほんしゅ}は{米|こめ}**からできています**。
examples.romaji: nihonshu wa kome kara dekite imasu.
examples.en: Sake is made from rice.

examples.ja: チーズは{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}**からできています**。
examples.romaji: chiizu wa gyuunyuu kara dekite imasu.
examples.en: Cheese is made from milk.

examples.ja: このコップはガラス**でできています**。
examples.romaji: kono koppu wa garasu de dekite imasu.
examples.en: This cup is made of glass.

examples.ja: このお{皿|さら}は{紙|かみ}**でできています**。とても{軽|かる}いですよ。
examples.romaji: kono osara wa kami de dekite imasu. totemo karui desu yo.
examples.en: This plate is made of paper. It's really light.

examples.ja: ワインはぶどう**からできています**。
examples.romaji: wain wa budou kara dekite imasu.
examples.en: Wine is made from grapes.

examples.ja: この{窓|まど}は{丈夫|じょうぶ}なガラス**でできています**。
examples.romaji: kono mado wa joubu na garasu de dekite imasu.
examples.en: This window is made of strong glass.

examples.ja: ～でできている・～からできている
examples.romaji: Say what something is made of or made from
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Like or in the same way as something
goal: You'll be able to compare nouns, descriptions, and ways of acting by pointing out a resemblance.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Compare by resemblance
text: Use ～のような before a noun and ～のように before an action or description. You compare something with a familiar model without claiming it actually belongs to that category.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ような・～ように (similarity)
text: A noun takes の before よう. A plain verb clause can connect directly. Choose な or に according to what follows. This lesson uses similarity; goal-oriented ように is taught separately.

formation: Noun + のような + Noun / のように + Verb or adjective

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{鳥|とり}**のように**{両手|りょうて}を{広|ひろ}げます。
examples.romaji: mei wa tori no you ni ryoute o hirogemasu.
examples.en: Mei spreads both arms like a bird.

examples.ja: おもちゃ**のような**{小|ちい}さい{車|くるま}を{買|か}いました。
examples.romaji: omocha no you na chiisai kuruma o kaimashita.
examples.en: I bought a tiny car that looks like a toy.

examples.ja: {雲|くも}**のような**パンです。
examples.romaji: kumo no you na pan desu.
examples.en: It is bread that resembles a cloud.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{父|ちち}**のように**{料理|りょうり}します。
examples.romaji: ren wa chichi no you ni ryouri shimasu.
examples.en: Ren cooks like his father.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{春|はる}**のように**{暖|あたた}かいですね。
examples.romaji: kyou wa haru no you ni atatakai desu ne.
examples.en: It's warm like spring today, isn't it?

examples.ja: マリアさんは{日本人|にほんじん}**のように**{日本語|にほんご}を{話|はな}します。
examples.romaji: maria-san wa nihonjin no you ni nihongo o hanashimasu.
examples.en: Maria speaks Japanese like a Japanese person.

examples.ja: このホテルはお{城|しろ}**のように**{大|おお}きくてきれいです。
examples.romaji: kono hoteru wa oshiro no you ni ookikute kirei desu.
examples.en: This hotel is big and beautiful, like a castle.

examples.ja: ～ような・～ように (similarity)
examples.romaji: Like or in the same way as something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

pattern: こんな・そんな・あんな
title: This kind, that kind, that kind over there
goal: You'll be able to point to a type of thing based on what is near the speaker, near the listener, distant from both, or already under discussion.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Point to a kind of thing
text: こんな, そんな, and あんな identify a type or quality. They can refer to something near the speaker, near the listener, or away from both, and also to something just described.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use こんな・そんな・あんな
text: Attach these words directly to a noun; do not add の. そんな often refers back to what the other person said. Unlike この, which picks out a particular item, こんな emphasizes “this kind of” item.

formation: こんな / そんな / あんな + Noun

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は**こんな**{大|おお}きい{葉|は}を{見|み}つけました。
examples.romaji: mei wa konna ookii ha o mitsukemashita.
examples.en: Mei found a leaf this big.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんが{会社|かいしゃ}をやめるんですか。**そんな**{話|はなし}は{初|はじ}めて{聞|き}きました。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san ga kaisha o yameru n desu ka. sonna hanashi wa hajimete kikimashita.
examples.en: Tanaka-san is quitting the company? This is the first I've heard of that.

examples.ja: **こんな**{時計|とけい}が{欲|ほ}しいです。
examples.romaji: konna tokei ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: I want this kind of watch.

examples.ja: **そんな**かばんが{欲|ほ}しいです。
examples.romaji: sonna kaban ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: I want that kind of bag.

examples.ja: **あんな**{家|いえ}に{住|す}みたいです。
examples.romaji: anna ie ni sumitai desu.
examples.en: I want to live in a house like that one over there.

examples.ja: {財布|さいふ}をなくしたんですか。**そんな**ときは、すぐ{交番|こうばん}に{行|い}ってください。
examples.romaji: saifu o nakushita n desu ka. sonna toki wa, sugu kouban ni itte kudasai.
examples.en: You lost your wallet? When that happens, go to a police box right away.

examples.ja: この{写真|しゃしん}を{見|み}てください。**こんな**{部屋|へや}に{住|す}みたいです。
examples.romaji: kono shashin o mite kudasai. konna heya ni sumitai desu.
examples.en: Look at this photo. I want to live in a room like this.

examples.ja: あそこに{大|おお}きい{犬|いぬ}がいるでしょう。**あんな**{犬|いぬ}がほしいです。
examples.romaji: asoko ni ookii inu ga iru deshou. anna inu ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: You see that big dog over there? I want a dog like that.

examples.ja: こんな・そんな・あんな
examples.romaji: This kind, that kind, that kind over there
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Refer to a person and their group
goal: You'll be able to use たち and ら to refer to groups of people or to a person together with others associated with them.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Refer to someone and their group
text: ～たち and ～ら can refer to several people or a person with associated companions. 蓮たち means Ren and his group, not several people all named Ren.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～たち・～ら
text: たち is widely useful with people. ら is common in forms such as 彼ら and 僕ら, but is not interchangeable with たち everywhere: あなたら can sound rough. Neither ending is a general plural marker for objects.

formation: Person or personal pronoun + たち / ら

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}**たち**は{公園|こうえん}でサッカーをしています。
examples.romaji: rentachi wa kouen de sakkaa o shite imasu.
examples.en: Ren and his friends are playing soccer in the park.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さん**たち**はもう{会議室|かいぎしつ}にいます。
examples.romaji: tanaka-santachi wa mou kaigishitsu ni imasu.
examples.en: Tanaka-san and the others are already in the meeting room.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}**たち**は{明日|あした}{出発|しゅっぱつ}します。
examples.romaji: watashitachi wa ashita shuppatsu shimasu.
examples.en: We leave tomorrow.

examples.ja: {彼|かれ}**ら**は{同|おな}じ{学校|がっこう}の{生徒|せいと}です。
examples.romaji: karera wa onaji gakkou no seito desu.
examples.en: They are students at the same school.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}**たち**は{来週|らいしゅう}、{京都|きょうと}へ{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: watashitachi wa raishuu, kyouto e ryokou ni ikimasu.
examples.en: We're going on a trip to Kyoto next week.

examples.ja: {子|こ}ども**たち**が{学校|がっこう}の{前|まえ}でバスを{待|ま}っています。
examples.romaji: kodomotachi ga gakkou no mae de basu o matte imasu.
examples.en: The children are waiting for the bus in front of the school.

examples.ja: {彼|かれ}**ら**は{毎週|まいしゅう}{土曜日|どようび}にサッカーをします。
examples.romaji: karera wa maishuu doyoubi ni sakkaa o shimasu.
examples.en: They play soccer every Saturday.

examples.ja: ～たち・～ら
examples.romaji: Refer to a person and their group
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Turn an action or statement into a noun-like idea
goal: You'll be able to use こと to discuss actions and facts as abstract ideas in neutral or formal contexts.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Turn an action into an idea
text: こと lets a whole action serve as the topic or object of a sentence. It is useful for discussing activities as ideas, rather than describing one visible event.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～こと (nominalizer)
text: Use a plain form before こと, such as 泳ぐこと. It then takes ordinary noun particles. の is also a nominalizer, but the two are not freely interchangeable, and some fixed patterns specifically require こと.

formation: Plain verb or い-adjective + こと / な-adjective stem + なこと

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{絵|え}を{描|か}く**こと**が{好|す}きです。
examples.romaji: mei wa e o kaku koto ga suki desu.
examples.en: Mei likes drawing pictures.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}の{夢|ゆめ}は{日本|にほん}で{働|はたら}く**こと**です。
examples.romaji: watashi no yume wa nihon de hataraku koto desu.
examples.en: My dream is to work in Japan.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{歩|ある}く**こと**は{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.romaji: mainichi aruku koto wa taisetsu desu.
examples.en: Walking every day is important.

examples.ja: {元気|げんき}**なこと**が{一番|いちばん}{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.romaji: genki na koto ga ichiban taisetsu desu.
examples.en: Being healthy is the most important thing.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}の{趣味|しゅみ}は{料理|りょうり}をする**こと**です。
examples.romaji: watashi no shumi wa ryouri o suru koto desu.
examples.en: My hobby is cooking.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}の{仕事|しごと}は{小学校|しょうがっこう}で{子|こ}どもに{英語|えいご}を{教|おし}える**こと**です。
examples.romaji: ani no shigoto wa shougakkou de kodomo ni eigo o oshieru koto desu.
examples.en: My older brother's job is teaching English to children at an elementary school.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}の{楽|たの}しみは、{近|ちか}くの{温泉|おんせん}に{行|い}く**こと**です。
examples.romaji: yasumi no hi no tanoshimi wa, chikaku no onsen ni iku koto desu.
examples.en: What I look forward to on my days off is going to a nearby hot spring.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}で{大切|たいせつ}なのは、パスポートをなくさない**こと**です。
examples.romaji: ryokou de taisetsu na no wa, pasupooto o nakusanai koto desu.
examples.en: What's important when traveling is not losing your passport.

examples.ja: ～こと (nominalizer)
examples.romaji: Turn an action or statement into a noun-like idea
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Highlight one part of a statement
goal: You'll be able to focus attention on who, what, when, or why something is the case.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Focus on the missing information
text: ～のは～です puts the part you want to identify after は. It can answer who did something, when it happened, or what was chosen. The first clause gives the background and the final phrase supplies the answer.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～のは～です
text: Use plain verbs and い-adjectives before の. Nouns and な-adjectives need な: 静かなのは. Do not put です inside the background clause.

formation: Plain clause + のは + Focused information + です

examples.ja: このケーキを{作|つく}った**のは**{芽衣|めい}**です**。
examples.romaji: kono keeki o tsukutta no wa mei desu.
examples.en: The person who made this cake is Mei.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}が{生|う}まれた**のは**{大阪|おおさか}**です**。
examples.romaji: watashi ga umareta no wa oosaka desu.
examples.en: Osaka is where I was born.

examples.ja: {出発|しゅっぱつ}する**のは**{明日|あした}**です**。
examples.romaji: shuppatsu suru no wa ashita desu.
examples.en: It is tomorrow that we leave.

examples.ja: {一番|いちばん}{静|しず}かな**のは**この{部屋|へや}**です**。
examples.romaji: ichiban shizuka na no wa kono heya desu.
examples.en: The quietest one is this room.

examples.ja: {次|つぎ}の{電車|でんしゃ}が{来|く}る**のは**{十時|じゅうじ}{五分|ごふん}です。
examples.romaji: tsugi no densha ga kuru no wa juuji gofun desu.
examples.en: The next train comes at 10:05.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}でいちばん{人気|にんき}がある**のは**このケーキです。
examples.romaji: kono mise de ichiban ninki ga aru no wa kono keeki desu.
examples.en: The most popular item at this shop is this cake.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}がある**のは**{明日|あした}じゃなくて、あさってです。
examples.romaji: kaigi ga aru no wa ashita ja nakute, asatte desu.
examples.en: The meeting isn't tomorrow. It's the day after tomorrow.

examples.romaji: Highlight one part of a statement

title: Give a name or identify what something is called
goal: You'll be able to introduce the name of a person, place, object, or idea before a noun.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Introduce a name
text: ～という links a name to the kind of person, place, or thing it names. It is especially useful when the listener may not know the name yet. Here いう is a naming link, not a literal act of speaking.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～という
text: Put the name before という and the category after it. In conversation, っていう is common. Keep this naming use distinct from quoting a whole statement.

formation: Name + という + Noun

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}はポチ**という**{犬|いぬ}と{遊|あそ}んでいます。
examples.romaji: mei wa pochi to iu inu to asonde imasu.
examples.en: Mei is playing with a dog called Pochi.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さん**という**{人|ひと}から{電話|でんわ}がありました。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san to iu hito kara denwa ga arimashita.
examples.en: There was a call from someone called Tanaka.

examples.ja: {京都|きょうと}**という**{町|まち}に{行|い}きました。
examples.romaji: kyouto to iu machi ni ikimashita.
examples.en: I went to a city called Kyoto.

examples.ja: これはもち**という**{食|た}べ{物|もの}です。
examples.romaji: kore wa mochi to iu tabemono desu.
examples.en: This is a food called mochi.

examples.ja: 『となりのトトロ』**という**{映画|えいが}を{見|み}たことがありますか。
examples.romaji: "tonari no totoro" to iu eiga o mita koto ga arimasu ka.
examples.en: Have you ever seen a movie called "My Neighbor Totoro"?

examples.ja: {駅|えき}の{近|ちか}くの「さくら」**という**ホテルに{泊|と}まりました。
examples.romaji: eki no chikaku no "sakura" to iu hoteru ni tomarimashita.
examples.en: I stayed at a hotel called Sakura near the station.

examples.ja: {日光|にっこう}**という**{所|ところ}へ{行|い}ったことがありますか。
examples.romaji: nikkou to iu tokoro e itta koto ga arimasu ka.
examples.en: Have you ever been to a place called Nikko?

examples.ja: ～という
examples.romaji: Give a name or identify what something is called

pattern: ～という意味・どういう意味
title: Ask or explain what a word means
goal: You'll be able to define unfamiliar language and ask what an expression means.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Explain what an expression means
text: ～という意味です explains the meaning of a word, sign, or phrase. The explanation comes before という意味, so you can give the meaning as a whole clause.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～という意味
text: Use ～という意味です to explain what a word or expression means. When the explanation is a full noun or な-adjective predicate, retain its だ before という. This pattern defines meaning rather than merely reporting someone's words.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Ask with どういう意味
text: Use どういう意味ですか to ask someone to explain a word or expression. An answer can use ～という意味です.

formation: Word or plain clause giving the meaning + という意味です
Word or expression + はどういう意味ですか

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{入|はい}ってはいけない**という{意味|いみ}**だと{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.romaji: ren wa haitte wa ikenai to iu imi da to setsumei shimasu.
examples.en: Ren explains that it means you must not enter.

examples.ja: 「{営業中|えいぎょうちゅう}」は{店|みせ}が{開|あ}いている**という{意味|いみ}**です。
examples.romaji: "eigyouchuu" wa mise ga aite iru to iu imi desu.
examples.en: "Eigyouchuu" means the shop is open.

examples.ja: 「{無料|むりょう}」は{お金|おかね}がいらない**という{意味|いみ}**です。
examples.romaji: “muryou” wa okane ga iranai to iu imi desu.
examples.en: The word “muryou” means that no payment is required.

examples.ja: 「{有料|ゆうりょう}」は{お金|おかね}が{必要|ひつよう}だ**という{意味|いみ}**です。
examples.romaji: “yuuryou” wa okane ga hitsuyou da to iu imi desu.
examples.en: The word “yuuryou” means that payment is required.

examples.ja: {無料|むりょう}は**どういう{意味|いみ}**ですか。
examples.romaji: muryou wa dou iu imi desu ka.
examples.en: What does “muryou” mean?

examples.ja: この{言葉|ことば}は**どういう{意味|いみ}**ですか。
examples.romaji: kono kotoba wa dou iu imi desu ka.
examples.en: What does this word mean?

examples.ja: すみません、それは**どういう{意味|いみ}**ですか。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, sore wa dou iu imi desu ka.
examples.en: Sorry, what do you mean by that?

examples.ja: 「{禁煙|きんえん}」はたばこを{吸|す}ってはいけない**という{意味|いみ}**です。
examples.romaji: "kin'en" wa tabako o sutte wa ikenai to iu imi desu.
examples.en: "Kin'en" means you must not smoke.

examples.ja: 「{売|う}り{切|き}れ」は{全部|ぜんぶ}{売|う}れて、もうない**という{意味|いみ}**です。
examples.romaji: "urikire" wa zenbu urete, mou nai to iu imi desu.
examples.en: "Urikire" means everything has been sold and there is none left.

examples.ja: ～という意味・どういう意味

title: Treat a whole statement as an idea or fact
goal: You'll be able to package a clause as a fact, message, or concept that can fit into a larger sentence.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Package the content of a statement
text: ～ということ treats a whole statement as a fact or message. You can then say you know, understand, or heard that information. It can also introduce a summary of what something implies.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ということ
text: Keep tense and negation inside the clause. Noun and な-adjective predicates retain だ: 休みだということ. The resulting phrase takes particles such as を or が; it is not a name followed by a category noun.

formation: Plain clause + ということ

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{明日|あした}が{休|やす}みだ**ということ**を{知|し}っています。
examples.romaji: ren wa ashita ga yasumi da to iu koto o shitte imasu.
examples.en: Ren knows that tomorrow is a day off.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{現金|げんきん}だけだ**ということ**を{知|し}っていますか。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa genkin dake da to iu koto o shitte imasu ka.
examples.en: Did you know that this shop only takes cash?

examples.ja: {店|みせ}が{閉|し}まった**ということ**を{聞|き}きました。
examples.romaji: mise ga shimatta to iu koto o kikimashita.
examples.en: I heard that the shop had closed.

examples.ja: もう{時間|じかん}がない**ということ**です。
examples.romaji: mou jikan ga nai to iu koto desu.
examples.en: It means that there is no time left.

examples.ja: {来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}が{祝日|しゅくじつ}だ**ということ**を{忘|わす}れていました。
examples.romaji: raishuu no getsuyoubi ga shukujitsu da to iu koto o wasurete imashita.
examples.en: I had forgotten that next Monday is a holiday.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんが{病気|びょうき}だ**ということ**を{聞|き}いて、びっくりしました。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san ga byouki da to iu koto o kiite, bikkuri shimashita.
examples.en: I was surprised to hear that Tanaka-san is ill.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{試合|しあい}が{中止|ちゅうし}だ**ということ**をメールで{知|し}りました。
examples.romaji: ashita no shiai ga chuushi da to iu koto o meeru de shirimashita.
examples.en: I found out by email that tomorrow's game is canceled.

title: Say that someone can do something
goal: You'll be able to change verbs into the potential form to talk about abilities and possibilities.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Say what someone can do
text: The potential form expresses ability or a possibility allowed by the situation. 乗れます says Mei is able to ride; it does not simply say that she rides regularly.
The same form can describe circumstances: a person may be able to attend because they have time. It does not automatically give permission; for permission, use the N5 pattern ～てもいいですか.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 1: change the last u-row kana to the e-row
text: For godan (Group 1) verbs, change the last kana from the u-row to the corresponding e-row, then add る: う→える, く→ける, ぐ→げる, す→せる, つ→てる, ぬ→ねる, ぶ→べる, む→める, る→れる.
For example, 乗る → 乗れる and 読む → 読める. Learn the verb group with the verb: a verb ending in る is not necessarily Group 2.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 2: replace る with られる
text: For ichidan (Group 2) verbs, remove the final る and add られる: 食べる → 食べられる; 見る → 見られる. Use the full られる form in these lessons. Shorter forms such as 食べれる occur in casual speech.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Remember する and 来る
text: する becomes できる. A する compound follows the same pattern: 勉強する → 勉強できる.
来る becomes 来られる. Notice the reading こ in 来られます.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Make potential forms polite, negative, or past
text: After forming the potential, conjugate it like a Group 2 verb: 読める → 読めます / 読めない / 読めた / 読めなかった. The polite negative and past are 読めません and 読めました.

が commonly marks the thing someone can read, eat, or do. を is also possible with many potential verbs, so it is not automatically an error. Other particles keep their roles: the に in 自転車に乗れます still belongs to 乗る.

formation: Group 1 verb with final kana changed to e-row + る
Group 2 verb without final る + られる
Potential form without final る + ます / ません / ました / ませんでした

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}はこの{漢字|かんじ}が{読|よ}**めます**。

examples.en: Ren can read this kanji.

examples.ja: カードで{払|はら}**えます**。

examples.ja: このパンは{食|た}**べられます**。

examples.ja: ここで{映画|えいが}が{見|み}**られます**。
examples.romaji: koko de eiga ga miraremasu.

examples.ja: ここでテニスが**できます**。

title: Say that an action is possible
goal: You'll be able to use ことができる to say that someone is able to do something or that an action is possible.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: State that an action is possible
text: ～ことができる states an ability or an available possibility. It is useful in explanations of facilities and activities, and is a more explicit alternative to a potential verb.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ことができる
text: Leave the main verb in dictionary form and change できる for tense or negation. Use 読むことができる, not the redundant 読めることができる. Permission is more directly expressed with ～てもいい.

formation: Verb dictionary form + ことができる

examples.ja: ここでキャンプをする**ことができます**。
examples.romaji: koko de kyanpu o suru koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: You can camp here.

examples.ja: {祖母|そぼ}は{九十歳|きゅうじゅっさい}ですが、まだ{一人|ひとり}で{歩|ある}く**ことができます**。
examples.romaji: sobo wa kyuujussai desu ga, mada hitori de aruku koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: My grandmother is ninety, but she can still walk on her own.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{漢字|かんじ}を{読|よ}む**ことができます**。
examples.romaji: ren wa kanji o yomu koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: Ren can read kanji.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{予約|よやく}する**ことができませんでした**。
examples.romaji: kinou wa yoyaku suru koto ga dekimasen deshita.
examples.en: I could not make a reservation yesterday.

examples.ja: この{駅|えき}では{新幹線|しんかんせん}の{切符|きっぷ}を{買|か}う**ことができます**。
examples.romaji: kono eki de wa shinkansen no kippu o kau koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: You can buy shinkansen tickets at this station.

examples.ja: このホテルでは、{朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}は{六時|ろくじ}から{食|た}べる**ことができます**。
examples.romaji: kono hoteru de wa, asagohan wa rokuji kara taberu koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: At this hotel, you can have breakfast from six in the morning.

examples.ja: この{図書館|としょかん}では、{本|ほん}は{一度|いちど}に{五冊|ごさつ}まで{借|か}りる**ことができます**。
examples.romaji: kono toshokan de wa, hon wa ichido ni gosatsu made kariru koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: At this library, you can borrow up to five books at a time.

title: Something can be seen or heard naturally
goal: You'll be able to describe sights and sounds that reach you without any deliberate effort.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe what reaches your senses
text: 見える describes something within sight; 聞こえる describes a sound that reaches your ears. English often uses “can see” or “can hear,” but Japanese focuses on natural perception rather than intentional ability.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use 見える・聞こえる
text: Both verbs conjugate like Group 2 verbs: 見えます, 見えない, 聞こえました. が commonly marks what is perceived. 見られる and 聞ける express the possibility of deliberately watching, listening, or asking.

formation: Visible thing + が見える / Sound + が聞こえる

examples.ja: {窓|まど}から{山|やま}が**{見|み}えます**。
examples.romaji: mado kara yama ga miemasu.
examples.en: I can see mountains from the window.

examples.ja: {隣|となり}の{部屋|へや}からテレビの{音|おと}が**{聞|き}こえます**。
examples.romaji: tonari no heya kara terebi no oto ga kikoemasu.
examples.en: I can hear the TV from the next room.

examples.ja: {鳥|とり}の{声|こえ}が**{聞|き}こえます**。
examples.romaji: tori no koe ga kikoemasu.
examples.en: I can hear birds singing.

examples.ja: {暗|くら}くて{何|なに}も**{見|み}えません**。
examples.romaji: kurakute nanimo miemasen.
examples.en: It is dark, so I cannot see anything.

examples.ja: ホテルの{部屋|へや}から{海|うみ}が**{見|み}えます**。
examples.romaji: hoteru no heya kara umi ga miemasu.
examples.en: You can see the sea from the hotel room.

examples.ja: {後|うし}ろの{席|せき}からは{先生|せんせい}の{声|こえ}がよく**{聞|き}こえません**。
examples.romaji: ushiro no seki kara wa sensei no koe ga yoku kikoemasen.
examples.en: From the back seats, you can't hear the teacher's voice well.

examples.ja: {眼鏡|めがね}をかけていないので、{黒板|こくばん}の{字|じ}がよく**{見|み}えません**。
examples.romaji: megane o kakete inai node, kokuban no ji ga yoku miemasen.
examples.en: I'm not wearing my glasses, so I can't see the letters on the blackboard well.
