title: Notice a sound, smell, taste, or feeling
goal: You'll be able to describe sensory impressions that reach you naturally.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Notice a sensory impression
text: A sensory noun followed by がする describes an impression that reaches you. Common nouns include 音, におい, and 味 for sounds, smells, and tastes. する does not mean intentionally doing something here.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～がする
text: Use が, not を. Conjugate する: がします, がした, がしません. A phrase before the sensory noun describes the impression, as in 甘い味.

formation: Sensory noun + がする

examples.ja: {台所|だいどころ}からいいにおい**がします**。
examples.romaji: daidokoro kara ii nioi ga shimasu.
examples.en: A nice smell is coming from the kitchen.

examples.ja: だれかがドアをたたく{音|おと}**がしました**。
examples.romaji: dareka ga doa o tataku oto ga shimashita.
examples.en: There was the sound of someone knocking on the door.

examples.ja: {外|そと}で{大|おお}きい{音|おと}**がしました**。
examples.romaji: soto de ookii oto ga shimashita.
examples.en: There was a loud sound outside.

examples.ja: この{お茶|おちゃ}は{甘|あま}い{味|あじ}**がします**。
examples.romaji: kono ocha wa amai aji ga shimasu.
examples.en: This tea has a sweet taste.

examples.ja: {玄関|げんかん}のほうで{変|へん}な{音|おと}**がします**。
examples.romaji: genkan no hou de hen na oto ga shimasu.
examples.en: There's a strange noise coming from the entrance.

examples.ja: この{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}、{変|へん}なにおい**がする**よ。{飲|の}まないほうがいい。
examples.romaji: kono gyuunyuu, hen na nioi ga suru yo. nomanai hou ga ii.
examples.en: This milk smells strange. You'd better not drink it.

examples.ja: このスープは{少|すこ}ししょうゆの{味|あじ}**がします**。
examples.romaji: kono suupu wa sukoshi shouyu no aji ga shimasu.
examples.en: This soup tastes a little of soy sauce.

examples.ja: ～がする
examples.romaji: Notice a sound, smell, taste, or feeling
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Something looks a certain way
goal: You'll be able to describe how a person or thing appears to your eyes, even if reality may differ.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Say how something looks
text: ～に見える and ～く見える describe the appearance of a person or thing. Use に after a noun or な-adjective stem, and く after an い-adjective stem. The impression may differ from reality.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～に見える・～く見える
text: Use 学生に見える for looking like a student and 若く見える for looking young. Do not attach に to an unchanged い-adjective. This judges appearance rather than simply saying an object is visible.

formation: Noun or な-adjective stem + に見える / い-adjective without い + く見える

examples.ja: この{写真|しゃしん}の{父|ちち}は{若|わか}**く{見|み}えます**。
examples.romaji: kono shashin no chichi wa wakaku miemasu.
examples.en: My father looks young in this photograph.

examples.ja: {祖父|そふ}は{前|まえ}より{元気|げんき}**に{見|み}えます**。
examples.romaji: sofu wa mae yori genki ni miemasu.
examples.en: My grandfather looks healthier than before.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{大学生|だいがくせい}**に{見|み}えます**。
examples.romaji: ren wa daigakusei ni miemasu.
examples.en: Ren looks like a university student.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{広|ひろ}**く{見|み}えます**。
examples.romaji: kono heya wa hiroku miemasu.
examples.en: This room looks spacious.

examples.ja: あの{人|ひと}は{先生|せんせい}**に{見|み}えます**が、{学生|がくせい}です。
examples.romaji: ano hito wa sensei ni miemasu ga, gakusei desu.
examples.en: That person looks like a teacher, but is actually a student.

examples.ja: このかばんは{高|たか}**く{見|み}えます**が、{三千円|さんぜんえん}でした。
examples.romaji: kono kaban wa takaku miemasu ga, sanzen'en deshita.
examples.en: This bag looks expensive, but it was 3,000 yen.

examples.ja: この{服|ふく}を{着|き}た{妹|いもうと}は、{大人|おとな}**に{見|み}えます**。
examples.romaji: kono fuku o kita imouto wa, otona ni miemasu.
examples.en: My younger sister looks like an adult in these clothes.

examples.ja: ～に見える・～く見える
examples.romaji: Something looks a certain way
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Describe a change or someone causing it
goal: You'll be able to distinguish verbs for events that happen from verbs for actions done to something.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Choose an event or an action on something
text: An intransitive verb describes what happens to a thing. A transitive verb describes someone acting on an object. These are different verbs, not one predictable conjugation.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use 自動詞・他動詞
text: Learn pairs together: 開く/開ける, 閉まる/閉める, つく/つける, 消える/消す. The changing thing often takes が; an object someone acts on takes を. An intransitive description need not mean nobody caused the event.

formation: Thing + が + Intransitive verb / Person は + object + を + Transitive verb

examples.ja: {父|ちち}はドアを**{開|あ}けます**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa doa o akemasu.
examples.en: My father opens the door.

examples.romaji: event → action on an object
examples.en: open

examples.romaji: event → action on an object
examples.en: close

examples.romaji: event → action on an object
examples.en: come on / turn on

examples.romaji: event → action on an object
examples.en: go out / turn off

examples.romaji: aku / akeru
shimaru / shimeru
tsuku / tsukeru
kieru / kesu

examples.ja: ドアが**{開|あ}きました**。
examples.romaji: doa ga akimashita.
examples.en: The door opened.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{電気|でんき}を**つけました**。
examples.romaji: mei wa denki o tsukemashita.
examples.en: Mei turned on the light.

examples.ja: {電気|でんき}が**つきました**。
examples.romaji: denki ga tsukimashita.
examples.en: The light came on.

examples.ja: ドアが**{閉|し}まりました**。
examples.romaji: 閉まる
examples.en: Reports the door's change without naming who closed it.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}がドアを**{閉|し}めました**。
examples.romaji: 閉める
examples.en: Identifies the person who closed the door.

examples.ja: {風|かぜ}でドアが{急|きゅう}に**{閉|し}まりました**。
examples.romaji: kaze de doa ga kyuu ni shimarimashita.
examples.en: The door suddenly shut because of the wind.

examples.ja: {寝|ね}る{前|まえ}に、{部屋|へや}の{電気|でんき}を**{消|け}しました**。
examples.romaji: neru mae ni, heya no denki o keshimashita.
examples.en: I turned off the light in my room before going to bed.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}は{九時|くじ}に**{始|はじ}まります**。
examples.romaji: kaigi wa kuji ni hajimarimasu.
examples.en: The meeting starts at nine.

examples.ja: 自動詞・他動詞
examples.romaji: Describe a change or someone causing it
examples.en: 7 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Something was done and remains that way
goal: You'll be able to describe a present state that someone intentionally created for a purpose.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Notice a prepared state
text: ～てある describes a state left by someone's intentional action. The person may be unmentioned; the useful result is what matters now.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てある
text: The prepared thing commonly takes が or は: 窓が開けてある. Use a transitive verb for the action someone performed. ～ている can describe a state without implying deliberate preparation.

formation: Transitive verb て-form + ある

examples.ja: テーブルに{お皿|おさら}が{並|なら}べ**てあります**。
examples.romaji: teeburu ni osara ga narabete arimasu.
examples.en: Plates have been laid out on the table.

examples.ja: {店|みせ}の{前|まえ}に{自転車|じてんしゃ}が{止|と}め**てあります**。
examples.romaji: mise no mae ni jitensha ga tomete arimasu.
examples.en: A bicycle has been parked in front of the shop.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}け**てあります**。
examples.romaji: mado ga akete arimasu.
examples.en: The window has been left open.

examples.ja: {地図|ちず}に{道|みち}が{書|か}い**てあります**。
examples.romaji: chizu ni michi ga kaite arimasu.
examples.en: The route has been marked on the map.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}いています。
examples.romaji: 開いている
examples.en: Reports an open state.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}け**てあります**。
examples.romaji: 開けてある
examples.en: Someone deliberately created the state.

examples.ja: {会議室|かいぎしつ}のドアに「{使用中|しようちゅう}」と{書|か}い**てあります**。
examples.romaji: kaigishitsu no doa ni "shiyouchuu" to kaite arimasu.
examples.en: "In use" is written on the meeting room door.

examples.ja: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}にビールが{冷|ひ}やし**てあります**よ。
examples.romaji: reizouko ni biiru ga hiyashite arimasu yo.
examples.en: There's beer chilling in the fridge.

examples.ja: ホテルの{部屋|へや}には、もうタオルが{置|お}い**てありました**。
examples.romaji: hoteru no heya ni wa, mou taoru ga oite arimashita.
examples.en: Towels had already been put out in the hotel room.

examples.ja: ～てある
examples.romaji: Something was done and remains that way
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Prepare ahead or leave something in a useful state
goal: You'll be able to talk about preparing in advance or leaving something in a useful state.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Prepare for later
text: ～ておく means doing something in advance for a later situation. It can also mean deliberately leaving a condition unchanged for now.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ておく
text: Conjugate おく: おきます, おいた. Casual ておく becomes とく and でおく becomes どく. Use ～ておく to prepare in advance or leave something in a useful state. ～てある describes the state left by an earlier action.

formation: Verb て-form + おく

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{旅行|りょこう}の{前|まえ}に{車|くるま}を{調|しら}べ**ておきます**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa ryokou no mae ni kuruma o shirabete okimasu.
examples.en: My father checks the car in advance of the trip.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{朝|あさ}{早|はや}いので、{今夜|こんや}{荷物|にもつ}を{準備|じゅんび}し**ておきます**。
examples.romaji: ashita wa asa hayai node, kon'ya nimotsu o junbi shite okimasu.
examples.en: I have to be up early tomorrow, so I'll get my bags ready tonight.

examples.ja: {切符|きっぷ}を{買|か}**っておきます**。
examples.romaji: kippu o katte okimasu.
examples.en: I will buy the tickets in advance.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}は{開|あ}け**ておいてください**。
examples.romaji: mado wa akete oite kudasai.
examples.en: Please leave the window open.

examples.ja: {人気|にんき}の{店|みせ}なので、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}{前|まえ}に{席|せき}を{予約|よやく}し**ておきました**。
examples.romaji: ninki no mise na node, isshuukan mae ni seki o yoyaku shite okimashita.
examples.en: It's a popular restaurant, so I booked a table a week in advance.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}の{前|まえ}に、このメールを{読|よ}**んでおいて**ください。
examples.romaji: kaigi no mae ni, kono meeru o yonde oite kudasai.
examples.en: Please read this email before the meeting.

examples.ja: お{客|きゃく}さんが{来|く}るので、ビールを{冷|ひ}やし**ておきましょう**。
examples.romaji: okyakusan ga kuru node, biiru o hiyashite okimashou.
examples.en: Guests are coming, so let's chill some beer beforehand.

examples.ja: ～ておく
examples.romaji: Prepare ahead or leave something in a useful state
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Leave or keep something unchanged
goal: You'll be able to say that a state continues while another action happens or nothing is changed.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Leave a condition unchanged
text: ～まま says that a condition continues unchanged while something else happens. An expected change may not have occurred.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～まま
text: Use た-form for an established state and ない-form for something left undone. Nouns take の, な-adjectives take な, and い-adjectives attach directly. This describes an unchanged state while another action occurs.

formation: Verb た-form / ない-form + まま / Noun + のまま

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{電気|でんき}をつけた**まま**{寝|ね}ました。
examples.romaji: ren wa denki o tsuketa mama nemashita.
examples.en: Ren slept with the light left on.

examples.ja: ドアが{開|あ}いた**まま**ですよ。
examples.romaji: doa ga aita mama desu yo.
examples.en: The door has been left open.

examples.ja: {靴|くつ}を{履|は}いた**まま**{入|はい}らないでください。
examples.romaji: kutsu o haita mama hairanaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please do not enter with your shoes on.

examples.ja: {朝ご飯|あさごはん}を{食|た}べない**まま**{出|で}かけました。
examples.romaji: asagohan o tabenai mama dekakemashita.
examples.en: I went out without eating breakfast.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{昔|むかし}の**まま**です。
examples.romaji: kono heya wa mukashi no mama desu.
examples.en: This room is just as it was long ago.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}はとても{疲|つか}れていたので、{服|ふく}を{着|き}た**まま**{寝|ね}ました。
examples.romaji: kinou wa totemo tsukarete ita node, fuku o kita mama nemashita.
examples.en: I was very tired yesterday, so I slept with my clothes on.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}を{開|あ}けた**まま**{出|で}かけないでください。
examples.romaji: mado o aketa mama dekakenaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please don't go out with the window open.

examples.ja: この{野菜|やさい}は{生|なま}の**まま**{食|た}べられます。
examples.romaji: kono yasai wa nama no mama taberaremasu.
examples.en: You can eat this vegetable raw.

examples.ja: ～まま
examples.romaji: Leave or keep something unchanged
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Try doing something to see what happens
goal: You'll be able to suggest or describe trying an action when the result is not yet known.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Try an action to find out
text: ～てみる means doing something experimentally to discover the experience or result. It is a trial rather than an unsuccessful attempt to start.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てみる
text: Conjugate みる: みます, みました, みたいです. This auxiliary is normally written in kana and does not literally mean looking.

formation: Verb て-form + みる

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{納豆|なっとう}を{食|た}べ**てみます**。
examples.romaji: mei wa nattou o tabete mimasu.
examples.en: Mei tries eating natto.

examples.ja: {駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しいラーメン{屋|や}ができたので、{行|い}**ってみました**。
examples.romaji: ekimae ni atarashii raamen'ya ga dekita node, itte mimashita.
examples.en: A new ramen shop opened near the station, so I went to check it out.

examples.ja: この{靴|くつ}を{履|は}い**てみてもいいですか**。
examples.romaji: kono kutsu o haite mite mo ii desu ka.
examples.en: May I try on these shoes?

examples.ja: {別|べつ}の{道|みち}を{歩|ある}い**てみました**。
examples.romaji: betsu no michi o aruite mimashita.
examples.en: I tried walking a different route.

examples.ja: {分|わ}からない{言葉|ことば}は、{辞書|じしょ}で{調|しら}べ**てみて**ください。
examples.romaji: wakaranai kotoba wa, jisho de shirabete mite kudasai.
examples.en: Try looking up words you don't know in the dictionary.

examples.ja: {一度|いちど}、{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}**ってみたい**です。
examples.romaji: ichido, fujisan ni nobotte mitai desu.
examples.en: I'd like to try climbing Mount Fuji once.

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めてお{好|この}み{焼|や}きを{作|つく}**ってみました**。
examples.romaji: hajimete okonomiyaki o tsukutte mimashita.
examples.en: I tried making okonomiyaki for the first time.

examples.ja: ～てみる
examples.romaji: Try doing something to see what happens
examples.en: Want extra conjugation drills for Te-form (て形) across Group 1 (Godan), Group 2 (Ichidan), and Irregular verbs? Use our Interactive Verb Conjugation Practice Tool or review the 13-Form Japanese Verb Conjugation Chart.

pattern: ～てしまう・～ちゃう・～じゃう
title: Finish completely or do something regrettable
goal: You'll be able to say an action was completed fully or happened with an unwanted result, including common casual forms.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Finish completely or react to an outcome
text: ～てしまう can emphasize complete finishing or express regret, surprise, or an unintended result. Context determines whether the outcome is unfortunate.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てしまう・～ちゃう・～じゃう
text: Casual てしまう becomes ちゃう and でしまう becomes じゃう. Past forms are ちゃった and じゃった. Finishing homework can be positive; the pattern does not always mean regret.

formation: Verb て/で-form + しまう / ～ちゃう / ～じゃう

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}はジュースをこぼし**てしまいました**。
examples.romaji: mei wa juusu o koboshite shimaimashita.
examples.en: Mei accidentally spilled her juice.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}、もう{全部|ぜんぶ}{読|よ}**んでしまいました**。
examples.romaji: kono hon, mou zenbu yonde shimaimashita.
examples.en: I've already read this whole book.

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}を{全部|ぜんぶ}や**ってしまいました**。
examples.romaji: shukudai o zenbu yatte shimaimashita.
examples.en: I finished all my homework.

examples.ja: {切符|きっぷ}をなくし**ちゃった**。
examples.romaji: kippu o nakushichatta.
examples.en: I lost my ticket.

examples.ja: {水|みず}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{飲|の}**んじゃった**。
examples.romaji: mizu o zenbu nonjatta.
examples.en: I drank all the water.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}で{寝|ね}**てしまって**、{降|お}りる{駅|えき}で{降|お}りられませんでした。
examples.romaji: densha de nete shimatte, oriru eki de oriraremasen deshita.
examples.en: I fell asleep on the train and couldn't get off at my stop.

examples.ja: {今朝|けさ}{寝坊|ねぼう}をしたので、{会議|かいぎ}に{遅|おく}れ**てしまいました**。
examples.romaji: kesa nebou o shita node, kaigi ni okurete shimaimashita.
examples.en: I overslept this morning, so I was late for the meeting.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しいスマホを{落|お}とし**てしまいました**。
examples.romaji: atarashii sumaho o otoshite shimaimashita.
examples.en: I dropped my new smartphone.

examples.ja: ～てしまう・～ちゃう・～じゃう
examples.romaji: Finish completely or do something regrettable
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Move toward here or develop up to now
goal: You'll be able to describe an action coming toward you or a change that has developed up to the present.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Move toward here or develop up to now
text: ～てくる describes movement toward the speaker, or change developing toward the present. It can also mean going to do something and then returning.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てくる
text: Use きます and きました for polite forms. Spatial movement is toward the viewpoint; a time-based development reaches now. ～ていく instead points away or onward.

formation: Verb て-form + くる

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}がこちらに{走|はし}**ってきます**。
examples.romaji: ren ga kochira ni hashitte kimasu.
examples.en: Ren comes running toward us.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}、{朝|あさ}が{寒|さむ}くなっ**てきました**。
examples.romaji: saikin, asa ga samuku natte kimashita.
examples.en: The mornings have been getting colder lately.

examples.ja: {少|すこ}し{暖|あたた}かくな**ってきました**。
examples.romaji: sukoshi atatakaku natte kimashita.
examples.en: It has gotten a little warmer.

examples.ja: パンを{買|か}**ってきます**。
examples.romaji: pan o katte kimasu.
examples.en: I will go buy bread and come back.

examples.ja: ちょっと{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}に{行|い}**ってきます**。
examples.romaji: chotto yuubinkyoku ni itte kimasu.
examples.en: I'm just going to the post office. I'll be back.

examples.ja: {向|む}こうから{大|おお}きい{犬|いぬ}が{走|はし}**ってきました**。
examples.romaji: mukou kara ookii inu ga hashitte kimashita.
examples.en: A big dog came running toward us from over there.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{母|はは}が{作|つく}ったお{弁当|べんとう}を{持|も}**ってきました**。
examples.romaji: kyou wa haha ga tsukutta obentou o motte kimashita.
examples.en: Today I brought a lunch my mother made.

examples.ja: ～てくる
examples.romaji: Move toward here or develop up to now
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: A change continues from now onward
goal: You'll be able to describe an action moving away or a change that develops into the future.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Move away or continue from now on
text: ～ていく describes movement away from the viewpoint, or a process continuing into the future. The directional idea applies to both space and time.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ていく
text: Use いきます for politeness. In movement examples identify where the speaker is; for continued change, the viewpoint is now and the process extends onward.

formation: Verb て-form + いく

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{学校|がっこう}へ{歩|ある}い**ていきます**。
examples.romaji: ren wa gakkou e aruite ikimasu.
examples.en: Ren walks away toward school.

examples.ja: これからもこの{町|まち}で{働|はたら}い**ていきたい**です。
examples.romaji: korekara mo kono machi de hataraite ikitai desu.
examples.en: I want to keep working in this town from now on.

examples.ja: これからもっと{寒|さむ}くな**っていきます**。
examples.romaji: kore kara motto samuku natte ikimasu.
examples.en: It will get colder from now on.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}の{勉強|べんきょう}を{続|つづ}け**ていきます**。
examples.romaji: nihongo no benkyou o tsuzukete ikimasu.
examples.en: I will keep studying Japanese from now on.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}、{日|ひ}が{長|なが}くなっ**てきました**。
examples.romaji: ～てくる
examples.en: The change has developed up to now.

examples.ja: これから、{日|ひ}が{長|なが}くなっ**ていきます**。
examples.romaji: ～ていく
examples.en: The change continues from now into the future.

examples.ja: これから、{日本|にほん}に{住|す}む{外国人|がいこくじん}は{増|ふ}え**ていく**でしょう。
examples.romaji: korekara, nihon ni sumu gaikokujin wa fuete iku deshou.
examples.en: From now on, the number of foreigners living in Japan will probably keep increasing.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}の{予報|よほう}ですから、かさを{持|も}**っていった**ほうがいいですよ。
examples.romaji: ame no yohou desu kara, kasa o motte itta hou ga ii desu yo.
examples.en: Rain is forecast, so you'd better take an umbrella with you.

examples.ja: {友|とも}だちの{家|いえ}にケーキを{買|か}**っていきます**。
examples.romaji: tomodachi no ie ni keeki o katte ikimasu.
examples.en: I'll buy a cake and take it to my friend's house.

examples.ja: ～ていく
examples.romaji: A change continues from now onward
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Start doing something
goal: You'll be able to combine a verb with 始める to show when an action begins.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Mark the start of an action
text: ～始める says an action or event starts. It focuses on the beginning, whether planned or simply observed.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～始める
text: Remove ます before adding 始める. Conjugate 始める for tense: 始めました. This pattern marks the beginning without necessarily suggesting a sudden onset.

formation: Verb ます-stem + 始める

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{絵|え}を{描|か}き**{始|はじ}めました**。
examples.romaji: mei wa e o kakihajimemashita.
examples.en: Mei started drawing a picture.

examples.ja: {公園|こうえん}の{桜|さくら}が{咲|さ}き**{始|はじ}めました**。
examples.romaji: kouen no sakura ga sakihajimemashita.
examples.en: The cherry blossoms in the park have started to bloom.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り**{始|はじ}めました**。
examples.romaji: ame ga furihajimemashita.
examples.en: It started raining.

examples.ja: {九時|くじ}に{勉強|べんきょう}し**{始|はじ}めます**。
examples.romaji: kuji ni benkyou shihajimemasu.
examples.en: I start studying at nine.

examples.ja: {去年|きょねん}から{日本語|にほんご}を{習|なら}い**{始|はじ}めました**。
examples.romaji: kyonen kara nihongo o naraihajimemashita.
examples.en: I started learning Japanese last year.

examples.ja: {来月|らいげつ}から{新|あたら}しい{会社|かいしゃ}で{働|はたら}き**{始|はじ}めます**。
examples.romaji: raigetsu kara atarashii kaisha de hatarakihajimemasu.
examples.en: I'll start working at a new company next month.

examples.ja: {先週|せんしゅう}から、{毎朝|まいあさ}{公園|こうえん}を{走|はし}り**{始|はじ}めました**。
examples.romaji: senshuu kara, maiasa kouen o hashirihajimemashita.
examples.en: Since last week, I've started running in the park every morning.

examples.ja: ～始める
examples.romaji: Start doing something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Suddenly begin doing something
goal: You'll be able to show that an action starts suddenly, often in a noticeable or unexpected way.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Notice a sudden beginning
text: ～出す often presents an action as suddenly breaking out. It is natural for rain, laughter, or crying that starts unexpectedly.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～出す
text: Remove ます and add 出す, which conjugates as a Group 1 verb: 出します, 出した. For a neutral planned start, 始める is usually more suitable.

formation: Verb ます-stem + 出す

examples.ja: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{急|きゅう}に{泣|な}き**{出|だ}しました**。
examples.romaji: akachan ga kyuu ni nakidashimashita.
examples.en: The baby suddenly started crying.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}を{出|で}たとき、{急|きゅう}に{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}り**{出|だ}しました**。
examples.romaji: eki o deta toki, kyuu ni yuki ga furidashimashita.
examples.en: When I left the station, it suddenly started to snow.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}が{笑|わら}い**{出|だ}しました**。
examples.romaji: mei ga waraidashimashita.
examples.en: Mei burst out laughing.

examples.ja: {犬|いぬ}が{走|はし}り**{出|だ}しました**。
examples.romaji: inu ga hashiridashimashita.
examples.en: The dog suddenly started running.

examples.ja: {静|しず}かだった{犬|いぬ}が、{急|きゅう}に{鳴|な}き**{出|だ}しました**。
examples.romaji: shizuka datta inu ga, kyuu ni nakidashimashita.
examples.en: The dog had been quiet, but it suddenly started barking.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いて、{学生|がくせい}たちはみんな{笑|わら}い**{出|だ}しました**。
examples.romaji: sensei no hanashi o kiite, gakuseitachi wa minna waraidashimashita.
examples.en: When they heard what the teacher said, all the students burst out laughing.

examples.ja: バスが{急|きゅう}に{動|うご}き**{出|だ}しました**。
examples.romaji: basu ga kyuu ni ugokidashimashita.
examples.en: The bus suddenly started moving.

examples.ja: ～出す
examples.romaji: Suddenly begin doing something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Keep doing something
goal: You'll be able to say that an action continues without stopping or carries on over time.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Keep an action going
text: ～続ける says an action continues rather than stopping. It highlights duration or persistence, not merely repeating an action on separate occasions.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～続ける
text: Remove ます and add 続ける. Use 続けています for an ongoing continuation and 続けました for a past stretch of activity.

formation: Verb ます-stem + 続ける

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}み**{続|つづ}けています**。
examples.romaji: ren wa hon o yomitsuzukete imasu.
examples.en: Ren keeps reading his book.

examples.ja: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{朝|あさ}まで{泣|な}き**{続|つづ}けました**。
examples.romaji: akachan ga asa made nakitsuzukemashita.
examples.en: The baby kept crying until morning.

examples.ja: {一時間|いちじかん}{歩|ある}き**{続|つづ}けました**。
examples.romaji: ichijikan arukitsuzukemashita.
examples.en: I kept walking for an hour.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り**{続|つづ}けています**。
examples.romaji: ame ga furitsuzukete imasu.
examples.en: The rain keeps falling.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{三十年|さんじゅうねん}{同|おな}じ{会社|かいしゃ}で{働|はたら}き**{続|つづ}けています**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa sanjuunen onaji kaisha de hatarakitsuzukete imasu.
examples.en: My father has kept working at the same company for thirty years.

examples.ja: {一日中|いちにちじゅう}パソコンを{使|つか}い**{続|つづ}けた**ので、{目|め}が{痛|いた}いです。
examples.romaji: ichinichijuu pasokon o tsukaitsuzuketa node, me ga itai desu.
examples.en: I kept using my computer all day, so my eyes hurt.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{五十年|ごじゅうねん}、{同|おな}じ{味|あじ}のラーメンを{作|つく}り**{続|つづ}けています**。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa gojuunen, onaji aji no raamen o tsukuritsuzukete imasu.
examples.en: This shop has kept making ramen with the same taste for fifty years.

examples.ja: ～続ける
examples.romaji: Keep doing something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Finish doing something
goal: You'll be able to combine a verb with 終わる to say an action has been brought to an end.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Reach the end of an action
text: ～終わる marks finishing an action with an endpoint, such as reading a book or eating a meal. The emphasis is reaching completion.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～終わる
text: Remove ます and add 終わる. Use 終わりました for completed actions. Choose activities that naturally have a finish; the construction is not a general replacement for stopping any state.

formation: Verb ます-stem + 終わる

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{ご飯|ごはん}を{食|た}べ**{終|お}わりました**。
examples.romaji: mei wa gohan o tabeowarimashita.
examples.en: Mei finished eating her meal.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}の{夜|よる}、ドラマを{最後|さいご}まで{見|み}**{終|お}わりました**。
examples.romaji: kinou no yoru, dorama o saigo made miowarimashita.
examples.en: Last night I finished watching the drama to the end.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}を{読|よ}み**{終|お}わりました**。
examples.romaji: kono hon o yomiowarimashita.
examples.en: I finished reading this book.

examples.ja: {手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}き**{終|お}わってから**{寝|ね}ます。
examples.romaji: tegami o kakiowatte kara nemasu.
examples.en: I will go to bed after finishing the letter.

examples.ja: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{荷物|にもつ}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{片付|かたづ}け**{終|お}わりました**。
examples.romaji: hikkoshi no nimotsu o zenbu katazukeowarimashita.
examples.en: I've finished putting away everything from the move.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}を{読|よ}み**{終|お}わった**ので、{図書館|としょかん}に{返|かえ}します。
examples.romaji: kono hon o yomiowatta node, toshokan ni kaeshimasu.
examples.en: I've finished reading this book, so I'll return it to the library.

examples.ja: {晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べ**{終|お}わって**から、お{皿|さら}を{洗|あら}います。
examples.romaji: bangohan o tabeowatte kara, osara o araimasu.
examples.en: I wash the dishes after I finish eating dinner.

examples.ja: ～終わる
examples.romaji: Finish doing something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Do something again to correct it
goal: You'll be able to say that an action is repeated because the first attempt needs correcting.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Do something again to improve it
text: ～直す means doing an action again to correct, revise, or improve it. It adds a reason for repetition that a plain “again” does not necessarily express.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～直す
text: Remove ます and add 直す. This works naturally with revisable actions such as writing, reading again to check, or making something again; it is not a mechanical suffix for every verb.

formation: Verb ます-stem + 直す

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}き**{直|なお}します**。
examples.romaji: mei wa namae o kakinaoshimasu.
examples.en: Mei rewrites her name.

examples.ja: {写真|しゃしん}が{暗|くら}かったので、{撮|と}り**{直|なお}しました**。
examples.romaji: shashin ga kurakatta node, torinaoshimashita.
examples.en: The photo was dark, so I took it again.

examples.ja: {間違|まちが}えた{文|ぶん}を{読|よ}み**{直|なお}しました**。
examples.romaji: machigaeta bun o yominaoshimashita.
examples.en: I reread the sentence I got wrong.

examples.ja: この{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}り**{直|なお}します**。
examples.romaji: kono ryouri o tsukurinaoshimasu.
examples.en: I will remake this dish.

examples.ja: {間違|まちが}いが{多|おお}かったので、レポートを{書|か}き**{直|なお}しました**。
examples.romaji: machigai ga ookatta node, repooto o kakinaoshimashita.
examples.en: There were a lot of mistakes, so I rewrote my report.

examples.ja: {電話番号|でんわばんごう}が{違|ちが}いました。もう{一度|いちど}かけ**{直|なお}します**。
examples.romaji: denwa bangou ga chigaimashita. mou ichido kakenaoshimasu.
examples.en: I had the wrong number. I'll call again.

examples.ja: すみません、よく{分|わ}かりません。もう{少|すこ}し{簡単|かんたん}に{言|い}い**{直|なお}して**ください。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, yoku wakarimasen. mou sukoshi kantan ni iinaoshite kudasai.
examples.en: Sorry, I don't quite understand. Could you say it again more simply?

examples.ja: ～直す
examples.romaji: Do something again to correct it
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Easy or likely to do
goal: You'll be able to describe actions that are easy to perform or things that tend to happen readily.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe an easy action
text: ～やすい describes something as easy to do, often because of its design or condition. It can also describe a tendency for an event to happen.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～やすい
text: The result is an い-adjective: やすいです, やすかったです, やすくないです. It describes ease, not whether someone has the ability at all.

formation: Verb ます-stem + やすい

examples.ja: この{靴|くつ}は{軽|かる}くて、{歩|ある}き**やすい**です。
examples.romaji: kono kutsu wa karukute, arukiyasui desu.
examples.en: These shoes are light and easy to walk in.

examples.ja: この{駅|えき}の{地図|ちず}は{大|おお}きくて{分|わ}かり**やすい**です。
examples.romaji: kono eki no chizu wa ookikute wakariyasui desu.
examples.en: This station map is big and easy to understand.

examples.ja: このペンは{書|か}き**やすい**です。
examples.romaji: kono pen wa kakiyasui desu.
examples.en: This pen is easy to write with.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{滑|すべ}り**やすい**です。
examples.romaji: ame no hi wa suberiyasui desu.
examples.en: It is easy to slip on rainy days.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}{先生|せんせい}は{声|こえ}が{大|おお}きいので、{授業|じゅぎょう}が{聞|き}き**やすい**です。
examples.romaji: tanaka sensei wa koe ga ookii node, jugyou ga kikiyasui desu.
examples.en: Mr. Tanaka has a loud voice, so his classes are easy to hear.

examples.ja: {冬|ふゆ}は{空気|くうき}が{乾|かわ}いているので、{風邪|かぜ}をひき**やすい**です。
examples.romaji: fuyu wa kuuki ga kawaite iru node, kaze o hikiyasui desu.
examples.en: The air is dry in winter, so it's easy to catch a cold.

examples.ja: このかばんは{軽|かる}くて、{旅行|りょこう}に{持|も}っていき**やすい**です。
examples.romaji: kono kaban wa karukute, ryokou ni motte ikiyasui desu.
examples.en: This bag is light and easy to take on trips.

examples.ja: ～やすい
examples.romaji: Easy or likely to do
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Difficult to do
goal: You'll be able to describe an action that is difficult because of the situation or the thing involved.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe a difficult action
text: ～にくい describes an action as difficult because of the thing or conditions involved. It can also describe something as resistant to a change.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～にくい
text: The result conjugates as an い-adjective. Difficulty is not impossibility: 読みにくい says reading takes effort, while 読めない says it cannot be read in that situation.

formation: Verb ます-stem + にくい

examples.ja: この{肉|にく}は{硬|かた}くて、{切|き}り**にくい**です。
examples.romaji: kono niku wa katakute, kirinikui desu.
examples.en: This meat is tough and hard to cut.

examples.ja: この{説明書|せつめいしょ}は{字|じ}が{小|ちい}さくて{読|よ}み**にくい**です。
examples.romaji: kono setsumeisho wa ji ga chiisakute yominikui desu.
examples.en: The letters in this manual are small, so it's hard to read.

examples.ja: この{靴|くつ}は{歩|ある}き**にくい**です。
examples.romaji: kono kutsu wa arukinikui desu.
examples.en: These shoes are difficult to walk in.

examples.ja: このコップは{割|わ}れ**にくい**です。
examples.romaji: kono koppu wa warenikui desu.
examples.en: This cup is hard to break.

examples.ja: このパンは{硬|かた}くて、{小|ちい}さい{子|こ}どもには{食|た}べ**にくい**です。
examples.romaji: kono pan wa katakute, chiisai kodomo ni wa tabenikui desu.
examples.en: This bread is hard, so it's difficult for small children to eat.

examples.ja: このコートは{汚|よご}れ**にくい**ので、{子|こ}どもにいいです。
examples.romaji: kono kooto wa yogorenikui node, kodomo ni ii desu.
examples.en: This coat doesn't get dirty easily, so it's good for children.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}のアナウンスは{声|こえ}が{小|ちい}さくて、{聞|き}き**にくい**です。
examples.romaji: eki no anaunsu wa koe ga chiisakute, kikinikui desu.
examples.en: The station announcements are quiet and hard to hear.

examples.ja: ～にくい
examples.romaji: Difficult to do
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Hard to do because it feels uncomfortable
goal: You'll be able to describe actions that feel emotionally, socially, or physically difficult to carry out.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Express personally felt difficulty
text: ～づらい often emphasizes difficulty felt by the person acting: discomfort, emotional reluctance, or practical strain. ～にくい is a broader description of difficulty, and the two can overlap.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～づらい
text: Write づらい, not ずらい. It conjugates as an い-adjective. It fits actions such as speaking about something awkward or walking with painful shoes, rather than a neutral material property like being hard to break.

formation: Verb ます-stem + づらい

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}には{言|い}い**づらい**です。
examples.romaji: sensei ni wa iizurai desu.
examples.en: It is hard to tell the teacher about it.

examples.ja: {部長|ぶちょう}はいつも{忙|いそが}しいので、{質問|しつもん}し**づらい**です。
examples.romaji: buchou wa itsumo isogashii node, shitsumon shizurai desu.
examples.en: My manager is always busy, so I feel awkward asking questions.

examples.ja: この{靴|くつ}では{歩|ある}き**づらい**です。
examples.romaji: kono kutsu dewa arukizurai desu.
examples.en: It is uncomfortable to walk in these shoes.

examples.ja: {人|ひと}が{多|おお}くて{話|はな}し**づらい**です。
examples.romaji: hito ga ookute hanashizurai desu.
examples.en: There are many people, so it is hard to talk.

examples.ja: {友|とも}だちに「お{金|かね}を{貸|か}して」とは{言|い}い**づらい**です。
examples.romaji: tomodachi ni "okane o kashite" to wa iizurai desu.
examples.en: It's awkward to ask a friend to lend me money.

examples.ja: {歯|は}が{痛|いた}くて、{食|た}べ**づらい**です。
examples.romaji: ha ga itakute, tabezurai desu.
examples.en: My tooth hurts, so it's hard for me to eat.

examples.ja: {眼鏡|めがね}を{忘|わす}れたので、{黒板|こくばん}の{字|じ}が{見|み}**づらい**です。
examples.romaji: megane o wasureta node, kokuban no ji ga mizurai desu.
examples.en: I forgot my glasses, so the writing on the blackboard is hard for me to see.

examples.ja: ～づらい
examples.romaji: Hard to do because it feels uncomfortable
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Something was happening in the past
goal: You'll be able to describe an action or continuing state that was in progress at an earlier time.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Look back at an ongoing action or state
text: ～ていた is the past of ～ている. It describes what was happening, a state that existed, or a repeated habit at a past time. The verb and context determine the interpretation.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ていた
text: With an action such as reading, it can mean “was reading.” With a change verb such as 開く, it describes the resulting state: 開いていた means “was open,” not continuously opening.

formation: Verb て-form + いた / いました

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{部屋|へや}でギターの{練習|れんしゅう}をし**ていました**。
examples.romaji: ren wa heya de gitaa no renshuu o shite imashita.
examples.en: Ren was practicing guitar in his room.

examples.ja: {家|いえ}に{帰|かえ}ったとき、{部屋|へや}の{電気|でんき}がつい**ていました**。
examples.romaji: ie ni kaetta toki, heya no denki ga tsuite imashita.
examples.en: When I got home, the light in my room was on.

examples.ja: {窓|まど}が{開|あ}い**ていました**。
examples.romaji: mado ga aite imashita.
examples.en: The window was open.

examples.ja: {去年|きょねん}は{毎日|まいにち}{走|はし}**っていました**。
examples.romaji: kyonen wa mainichi hashitte imashita.
examples.en: Last year I used to run every day.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}{電話|でんわ}をもらったとき、お{風呂|ふろ}に{入|はい}**っていました**。
examples.romaji: kinou denwa o moratta toki, ofuro ni haitte imashita.
examples.en: When I got a phone call yesterday, I was in the bath.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}{起|お}きたとき、{外|そと}は{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}**っていました**。
examples.romaji: asa okita toki, soto wa yuki ga futte imashita.
examples.en: When I got up in the morning, it was snowing outside.

examples.ja: {子|こ}どものころ、{夏|なつ}は{毎日|まいにち}{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}い**でいました**。
examples.romaji: kodomo no koro, natsu wa mainichi kawa de oyoide imashita.
examples.en: As a child, I used to swim in the river every day in summer.

examples.ja: ～ていた
examples.romaji: Something was happening in the past
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Just about to, in the middle of, or just finished
goal: You'll be able to pinpoint the exact stage of an action by attaching ところです to dictionary, ている, and た verb forms.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Locate an action just before, during, or just after
text: ところ identifies the exact stage of an action. The verb form before it distinguishes being about to start, being in the middle, and having just finished.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ところです
text: 食べるところ is just before eating; 食べているところ is during it; 食べたところ is immediately afterward. Here ところ means a stage, not a physical place.

formation: Verb dictionary / ている / た form + ところです

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{ご飯|ごはん}を{食|た}べる**ところです**。
examples.romaji: mei wa gohan o taberu tokoro desu.
examples.en: Mei is about to eat her meal.

examples.ja: すみません、{今|いま}{電話|でんわ}をしている**ところ**なので、{少|すこ}し{待|ま}ってください。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, ima denwa o shite iru tokoro na node, sukoshi matte kudasai.
examples.en: Sorry, I'm in the middle of a phone call, so please wait a moment.

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{ご飯|ごはん}を{食|た}べている**ところです**。
examples.romaji: ima, gohan o tabete iru tokoro desu.
examples.en: I am right in the middle of eating.

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{ご飯|ごはん}を{食|た}べた**ところです**。
examples.romaji: ima, gohan o tabeta tokoro desu.
examples.en: I have just finished eating.

examples.ja: ちょうど{今|いま}から{出|で}かける**ところです**。
examples.romaji: choudo ima kara dekakeru tokoro desu.
examples.en: I'm just about to go out.

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{駅|えき}に{向|む}かっている**ところです**。
examples.romaji: ima, eki ni mukatte iru tokoro desu.
examples.en: I'm on my way to the station right now.

examples.ja: ちょうど{今|いま}、{家|いえ}に{着|つ}いた**ところです**。
examples.romaji: choudo ima, ie ni tsuita tokoro desu.
examples.en: I've just this moment arrived home.

examples.ja: ～ところです
examples.romaji: Just about to, in the middle of, or just finished
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Something happened only recently
goal: You'll be able to present an event as recent from the speaker's point of view.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Present an event as recent
text: ～たばかりです says an action happened only recently from the speaker's perspective. “Recent” can cover more than a few seconds if that is short in the relevant context.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～たばかりです
text: Use a plain past verb even though です describes the present assessment. Before a noun use ばかりの. Unlike たところ, this is subjective recency rather than the exact immediate aftermath.

formation: Verb た-form + ばかりです

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{帰|かえ}ってきた**ばかりです**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa kaette kita bakari desu.
examples.en: My father has only just come home.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}に{来|き}た**ばかり**なので、まだ{日本語|にほんご}がよく{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: nihon ni kita bakari na node, mada nihongo ga yoku wakarimasen.
examples.en: I've only just come to Japan, so I don't understand Japanese well yet.

examples.ja: この{靴|くつ}は{買|か}った**ばかりです**。
examples.romaji: kono kutsu wa katta bakari desu.
examples.en: I have only just bought these shoes.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}を{習|なら}い{始|はじ}めた**ばかりです**。
examples.romaji: nihongo o naraihajimeta bakari desu.
examples.en: I have only recently started learning Japanese.

examples.ja: このスマホは{先週|せんしゅう}{買|か}った**ばかりです**。
examples.romaji: kono sumaho wa senshuu katta bakari desu.
examples.en: I only bought this smartphone last week.

examples.ja: さっき{食|た}べた**ばかり**なので、おなかがいっぱいです。
examples.romaji: sakki tabeta bakari na node, onaka ga ippai desu.
examples.en: I just ate a little while ago, so I'm full.

examples.ja: この{会社|かいしゃ}に{入|はい}った**ばかりです**。よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.romaji: kono kaisha ni haitta bakari desu. yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
examples.en: I've only just joined this company. It's nice to meet you.

examples.ja: ～たばかりです
examples.romaji: Something happened only recently
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: There are times when something happens
goal: You'll be able to say that an action or situation occurs sometimes, rather than all the time.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Say something happens sometimes
text: Dictionary-form verb + ことがある describes an occasional event or habit. It differs from the N5 past-form pattern meaning experience at least once.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ことがある (occasional action)
text: Use 遅れることがある for sometimes being late and 食べないことがある for sometimes not eating. A preceding た-form normally changes this to an experience statement.

formation: Verb dictionary form or ない-form + ことがある / ことがあります

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{日曜日|にちようび}に{料理|りょうり}する**ことがあります**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa nichiyoubi ni ryouri suru koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: My father sometimes cooks on Sundays.

examples.ja: {週末|しゅうまつ}は、{図書館|としょかん}で{勉強|べんきょう}する**ことがあります**。
examples.romaji: shuumatsu wa, toshokan de benkyou suru koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: On weekends, I sometimes study at the library.

examples.ja: {朝ご飯|あさごはん}を{食|た}べない**ことがあります**。
examples.romaji: asagohan o tabenai koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: I sometimes skip breakfast.

examples.ja: このバスは{遅|おく}れる**ことがあります**。
examples.romaji: kono basu wa okureru koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: This bus is sometimes late.

examples.ja: この{電車|でんしゃ}は{雪|ゆき}の{日|ひ}に{止|と}まる**ことがあります**。
examples.romaji: kono densha wa yuki no hi ni tomaru koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: This train sometimes stops running on snowy days.

examples.ja: {忙|いそが}しいときは、{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}を{食|た}べない**ことがあります**。
examples.romaji: isogashii toki wa, hirugohan o tabenai koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: When I'm busy, I sometimes skip lunch.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{仕事|しごと}で{夜|よる}{遅|おそ}く{帰|かえ}る**ことがあります**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa shigoto de yoru osoku kaeru koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: My father sometimes comes home late at night because of work.

examples.ja: ～ことがある (occasional action)
examples.romaji: There are times when something happens
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: In the middle of an activity or period
goal: You'll be able to say that an activity is underway or that something falls within a stated period.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Mark an activity in progress
text: ～中 says an activity is currently underway. It is common in short status descriptions such as studying, eating, or being in a meeting.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～中
text: In 勉強中 and 食事中, 中 is read ちゅう. Do not attach it directly to a verb dictionary form. Other compounds, such as 一日中 meaning “all day,” may use じゅう; learn the reading with the expression.

formation: Activity noun + 中

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{勉強|べんきょう}**{中|ちゅう}**です。
examples.romaji: ren wa benkyouchuu desu.
examples.en: Ren is studying.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}は{今|いま}{電話|でんわ}**{中|ちゅう}**です。
examples.romaji: tanaka wa ima denwachuu desu.
examples.en: Tanaka is on the phone right now.

examples.ja: {今|いま}は{食事|しょくじ}**{中|ちゅう}**です。
examples.romaji: ima wa shokujichuu desu.
examples.en: I am eating at the moment.

examples.ja: {母|はは}は{会議|かいぎ}**{中|ちゅう}**です。
examples.romaji: haha wa kaigichuu desu.
examples.en: My mother is in a meeting.

examples.ja: {工事|こうじ}**{中|ちゅう}**なので、この{道|みち}は{通|とお}れません。
examples.romaji: koujichuu na node, kono michi wa tooremasen.
examples.en: Construction is going on, so you can't go through on this road.

examples.ja: {授業|じゅぎょう}**{中|ちゅう}**は、スマホを{使|つか}わないでください。
examples.romaji: jugyouchuu wa, sumaho o tsukawanaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please don't use your phone during class.

examples.ja: このトイレは{今|いま}{掃除|そうじ}**{中|ちゅう}**です。
examples.romaji: kono toire wa ima soujichuu desu.
examples.en: This restroom is being cleaned right now.

examples.ja: ～中
examples.romaji: In the middle of an activity or period
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Throughout the time something continues
goal: You'll be able to say that one situation lasts for the entire duration of another.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Continue throughout a period
text: ～間 describes an action or state that lasts through another period. Both situations are understood as overlapping in duration.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～間
text: The main action usually continues over the interval. Different people may perform the two actions.

formation: Verb ている / い-adjective + 間 / Noun の / な-adjective な + 間

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}が{寝|ね}ている**{間|あいだ}**、{母|はは}はお{弁当|べんとう}を{作|つく}っていました。
examples.romaji: mei ga nete iru aida, haha wa obentou o tsukutte imashita.
examples.en: While Mei was sleeping, mother was making bento lunches.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}っている**{間|あいだ}**、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいました。
examples.romaji: densha ni notte iru aida, hon o yonde imashita.
examples.en: I was reading a book the whole time I was on the train.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みの**{間|あいだ}**、{祖父|そふ}の{家|いえ}にいました。
examples.romaji: natsuyasumi no aida, sofu no ie ni imashita.
examples.en: I stayed at my grandfather's house during the summer vacation.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}が{運転|うんてん}している**{間|あいだ}**、{静|しず}かにしていました。
examples.romaji: chichi ga unten shite iru aida, shizuka ni shite imashita.
examples.en: I stayed quiet while my father was driving.

examples.ja: {冬休|ふゆやす}みの**{間|あいだ}**、スキー{場|じょう}でアルバイトをしていました。
examples.romaji: fuyuyasumi no aida, sukiijou de arubaito o shite imashita.
examples.en: During the winter vacation, I was working part-time at a ski resort.

examples.ja: {母|はは}が{買|か}い{物|もの}をしている**{間|あいだ}**、{私|わたし}と{弟|おとうと}は{車|くるま}の{中|なか}で{待|ま}っていました。
examples.romaji: haha ga kaimono o shite iru aida, watashi to otouto wa kuruma no naka de matte imashita.
examples.en: While my mother was shopping, my younger brother and I waited in the car.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}の**{間|あいだ}**は、{静|しず}かにしていてください。
examples.romaji: kaigi no aida wa, shizuka ni shite ite kudasai.
examples.en: Please stay quiet for the whole meeting.

examples.ja: ～間
examples.romaji: Throughout the time something continues
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Something happens within a period of time
goal: You'll be able to place an event at some point while another situation is continuing.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Fit an event inside a period
text: ～間に locates an event or completed action somewhere within a time window. It need not occupy the whole period.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～間に
text: に turns the interval into a window for an occurrence. Compare 寝ている間、読んでいた with 寝ている間に、帰ってきた: reading continues, while returning happens at a point.

formation: Verb ている / い-adjective + 間に / Noun の / な-adjective な + 間に

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}が{寝|ね}ている**{間|あいだ}に**、{父|ちち}が{帰|かえ}ってきました。
examples.romaji: mei ga nete iru aida ni, chichi ga kaette kimashita.
examples.en: My father came home while Mei was sleeping.

examples.ja: {留守|るす}の**{間|あいだ}に**、{荷物|にもつ}が{届|とど}きました。
examples.romaji: rusu no aida ni, nimotsu ga todokimashita.
examples.en: A package arrived while I was out.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの**{間|あいだ}に**、この{本|ほん}を{読|よ}み{終|お}わります。
examples.romaji: yasumi no aida ni, kono hon o yomiowarimasu.
examples.en: I will finish this book during the break.

examples.ja: {母|はは}が{買|か}い{物|もの}している**{間|あいだ}に**、{掃除|そうじ}をしました。
examples.romaji: haha ga kaimono shite iru aida ni, souji o shimashita.
examples.en: I did the cleaning while my mother was shopping.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}が{寝|ね}ている**{間|あいだ}**、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいました。
examples.romaji: 間
examples.en: Reading is presented as ongoing while Mei sleeps.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}が{寝|ね}ている**{間|あいだ}に**、{本|ほん}を{読|よ}み{終|お}わりました。
examples.romaji: 間に
examples.en: Finishing the book occurs within the time Mei is asleep.

examples.ja: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{寝|ね}ている**{間|あいだ}に**、{洗濯|せんたく}をしました。
examples.romaji: akachan ga nete iru aida ni, sentaku o shimashita.
examples.en: I did the laundry while the baby was asleep.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}にいる**{間|あいだ}に**、{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}りたいです。
examples.romaji: nihon ni iru aida ni, fujisan ni noboritai desu.
examples.en: I want to climb Mount Fuji while I'm in Japan.

examples.ja: {学生|がくせい}の**{間|あいだ}に**、いろいろな{国|くに}へ{行|い}ってみたいです。
examples.romaji: gakusei no aida ni, iroiro na kuni e itte mitai desu.
examples.en: I want to travel to lots of countries while I'm a student.

examples.ja: ～間に
examples.romaji: Something happens within a period of time
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Do two actions at the same time
goal: You'll be able to describe one person carrying out two actions simultaneously.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Do two actions at the same time
text: ～ながら links two actions performed by the same person simultaneously. The final action is usually the main one, and the ながら action is accompanying it.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ながら
text: Remove ます rather than using the て-form. Both actions normally share their subject. If different people are involved, use an appropriate time clause such as 間.

formation: Verb ます-stem + ながら + Main action

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}き**ながら**{勉強|べんきょう}します。
examples.romaji: ren wa ongaku o kikinagara benkyou shimasu.
examples.en: Ren studies while listening to music.

examples.ja: {地図|ちず}を{見|み}**ながら**、ホテルを{探|さが}しました。
examples.romaji: chizu o minagara, hoteru o sagashimashita.
examples.en: I looked for the hotel while checking the map.

examples.ja: {お茶|おちゃ}を{飲|の}み**ながら**{話|はな}しましょう。
examples.romaji: ocha o nominagara hanashimashou.
examples.en: Let's talk while drinking tea.

examples.ja: {母|はは}は{歌|うた}い**ながら**{料理|りょうり}します。
examples.romaji: haha wa utainagara ryouri shimasu.
examples.en: My mother cooks while singing.

examples.ja: スマホを{見|み}**ながら**{歩|ある}くのは{危|あぶ}ないです。
examples.romaji: sumaho o minagara aruku no wa abunai desu.
examples.en: It's dangerous to walk while looking at your phone.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はいつもラジオを{聞|き}き**ながら**{運転|うんてん}します。
examples.romaji: watashi wa itsumo rajio o kikinagara unten shimasu.
examples.en: I always listen to the radio while I drive.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}、コーヒーを{飲|の}み**ながら**{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}みます。
examples.romaji: maiasa, koohii o nominagara shinbun o yomimasu.
examples.en: Every morning, I read the newspaper while drinking coffee.

examples.ja: ～ながら
examples.romaji: Do two actions at the same time
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Do something after another event
goal: You'll be able to place an action after another action, event, or point in time.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Put one action after another
text: ～後で says an action happens after another action or event. It establishes sequence without necessarily saying the second action happens immediately.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～後で
text: Use the た-form before 後で even for a future sequence: 食べた後で出かけます. The final predicate carries the sentence's tense.

formation: Verb た-form + 後で / Noun + の後で

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{ご飯|ごはん}を{食|た}べた**{後|あと}で**{歯|は}を{磨|みが}きます。
examples.romaji: mei wa gohan o tabeta ato de ha o migakimasu.
examples.en: Mei brushes her teeth after eating.

examples.ja: {食事|しょくじ}の**{後|あと}で**、この{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んでください。
examples.romaji: shokuji no ato de, kono kusuri o nonde kudasai.
examples.en: Please take this medicine after meals.

examples.ja: {授業|じゅぎょう}の**{後|あと}で**{図書館|としょかん}に{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: jugyou no ato de toshokan ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I go to the library after class.

examples.ja: {手|て}を{洗|あら}った**{後|あと}で**{料理|りょうり}します。
examples.romaji: te o aratta ato de ryouri shimasu.
examples.en: I cook after washing my hands.

examples.ja: {仕事|しごと}が{終|お}わった**{後|あと}で**、ジムに{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: shigoto ga owatta ato de, jimu ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I go to the gym after work finishes.

examples.ja: シャワーを{浴|あ}びた**{後|あと}で**、ビールを{飲|の}みました。
examples.romaji: shawaa o abita ato de, biiru o nomimashita.
examples.en: After taking a shower, I drank a beer.

examples.ja: {映画|えいが}を{見|み}た**{後|あと}で**、レストランで{食事|しょくじ}をしました。
examples.romaji: eiga o mita ato de, resutoran de shokuji o shimashita.
examples.en: After seeing the movie, we had a meal at a restaurant.

examples.ja: ～後で
examples.romaji: Do something after another event
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Complete something by a deadline
goal: You'll be able to state the latest time by which an action must be completed.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Set a deadline
text: ～までに gives the latest time by which an action must happen or be completed. It does not mean the action continues until that time.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～までに
text: Choose a completion or occurrence such as returning, submitting, or finishing. Plain まで describes continuation up to an endpoint; adding に changes the time relationship.

formation: Time or event boundary + までに + Bounded action

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{五時|ごじ}**までに**{宿題|しゅくだい}を{終|お}わらせます。
examples.romaji: ren wa goji made ni shukudai o owarasemasu.
examples.en: Ren will finish his homework by five.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}**までに**{返事|へんじ}をください。
examples.romaji: ashita no asa made ni henji o kudasai.
examples.en: Please give me your answer by tomorrow morning.

examples.ja: {金曜日|きんようび}**までに**{返|かえ}してください。
examples.romaji: kin'youbi made ni kaeshite kudasai.
examples.en: Please return it by Friday.

examples.ja: バスが{来|く}る**までに**{切符|きっぷ}を{買|か}います。
examples.romaji: basu ga kuru made ni kippu o kaimasu.
examples.en: I will buy a ticket before the bus arrives.

examples.ja: {五時|ごじ}まで{勉強|べんきょう}します。
examples.romaji: まで
examples.en: Studying continues up to five.

examples.ja: {五時|ごじ}**までに**{勉強|べんきょう}を{終|お}えます。
examples.romaji: までに
examples.en: Finishing happens no later than five.

examples.ja: レポートは{金曜日|きんようび}**までに**{出|だ}してください。
examples.romaji: repooto wa kin'youbi made ni dashite kudasai.
examples.en: Please hand in your report by Friday.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}の{本|ほん}は{来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}**までに**{返|かえ}します。
examples.romaji: toshokan no hon wa raishuu no getsuyoubi made ni kaeshimasu.
examples.en: I'll return the library books by next Monday.

examples.ja: {夜|よる}{十時|じゅうじ}**までに**{帰|かえ}ってきてね。
examples.romaji: yoru juuji made ni kaette kite ne.
examples.en: Be home by ten tonight, okay?

examples.ja: ～までに
examples.romaji: Complete something by a deadline
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Say how often something happens
goal: You'll be able to state how many times an action occurs within a given period.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: State how often something happens
text: A time span followed by に establishes the period within which a frequency is counted. It answers how often, rather than the clock time of one event.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Time span + に + frequency
text: Use 一週間に三回 for three times a week and 一日に二回 for twice a day. Keep the period and the count distinct; 回 counts occasions, while 時間 measures duration.

formation: Time span + に + Frequency + Verb

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{一週間|いっしゅうかん}**に**{三回|さんかい}{走|はし}ります。
examples.romaji: chichi wa isshuukan ni sankai hashirimasu.
examples.en: My father runs three times a week.

examples.ja: このバスは{一時間|いちじかん}**に**{二本|にほん}{来|き}ます。
examples.romaji: kono basu wa ichijikan ni nihon kimasu.
examples.en: This bus comes twice an hour.

examples.ja: {一日|いちにち}**に**{二回|にかい}{歯|は}を{磨|みが}きます。
examples.romaji: ichinichi ni nikai ha o migakimasu.
examples.en: I brush my teeth twice a day.

examples.ja: {一年|いちねん}**に**{一回|いっかい}{京都|きょうと}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: ichinen ni ikkai kyouto e ikimasu.
examples.en: I go to Kyoto once a year.

examples.ja: この{薬|くすり}は{一日|いちにち}**に**{三回|さんかい}、{食事|しょくじ}の{後|あと}で{飲|の}んでください。
examples.romaji: kono kusuri wa ichinichi ni sankai, shokuji no ato de nonde kudasai.
examples.en: Please take this medicine three times a day, after meals.

examples.ja: {一|いっ}か{月|げつ}**に**{一回|いっかい}、{髪|かみ}を{切|き}りに{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: ikkagetsu ni ikkai, kami o kiri ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I go to get my hair cut once a month.

examples.ja: {週|しゅう}**に**{二回|にかい}、ジムに{通|かよ}っています。
examples.romaji: shuu ni nikai, jimu ni kayotte imasu.
examples.en: I go to the gym twice a week.

title: Each time or every unit
goal: You'll be able to say that something happens with every item, occasion, or fixed unit.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Repeat at each unit or occasion
text: ～ごとに means every stated interval, item, or occurrence. Each unit triggers the action or distribution.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ごとに
text: Use 一時間ごとに for every hour and 会うごとに for every time you meet. おきに emphasizes a gap; with days and counted items the two can yield different schedules.

formation: Noun, quantity, or dictionary-form verb + ごとに

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{一時間|いちじかん}**ごとに**{休憩|きゅうけい}します。
examples.romaji: chichi wa ichijikan goto ni kyuukei shimasu.
examples.en: My father takes a break every hour.

examples.ja: {季節|きせつ}**ごとに**、{店|みせ}のメニューが{変|か}わります。
examples.romaji: kisetsu goto ni, mise no menyuu ga kawarimasu.
examples.en: The restaurant's menu changes with each season.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}**ごとに**{紙|かみ}を{配|くば}ります。
examples.romaji: hitori goto ni kami o kubarimasu.
examples.en: I distribute paper to each person.

examples.ja: {会|あ}う**ごとに**{芽衣|めい}は{背|せ}が{高|たか}くなっています。
examples.romaji: au goto ni mei wa se ga takaku natte imasu.
examples.en: Mei is taller every time we meet.

examples.ja: このビルは{階|かい}**ごとに**トイレがあります。
examples.romaji: kono biru wa kai goto ni toire ga arimasu.
examples.en: There's a restroom on every floor of this building.

examples.ja: ゴミは{種類|しゅるい}**ごとに**{分|わ}けて{出|だ}してください。
examples.romaji: gomi wa shurui goto ni wakete dashite kudasai.
examples.en: Please sort your trash by type before putting it out.

examples.ja: このホテルは{部屋|へや}**ごとに**エアコンがついています。
examples.romaji: kono hoteru wa heya goto ni eakon ga tsuite imasu.
examples.en: Every room in this hotel has an air conditioner.

examples.ja: ～ごとに

title: At regular intervals
goal: You'll be able to describe actions or spacing that repeat after a fixed interval.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Leave a regular gap
text: ～おきに describes repeated events separated by a gap. With 一日おきに, one whole day is skipped, giving an every-other-day pattern.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～おきに
text: For hours and minutes, 一時間おきに normally means every hour. For days or counted objects, pay attention to the skipped unit: 一日おきに is every other day. Confirm the actual schedule instead of translating every phrase mechanically.

formation: Time span or quantity + おきに

examples.ja: {母|はは}は{一日|いちにち}**おきに**{花|はな}に{水|みず}をやります。
examples.romaji: haha wa ichinichi oki ni hana ni mizu o yarimasu.
examples.en: My mother waters the flowers every other day.

examples.ja: {一週間|いっしゅうかん}**おきに**、{祖母|そぼ}の{家|いえ}に{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: isshuukan oki ni, sobo no ie ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I go to my grandmother's house every other week.

examples.ja: {三十分|さんじゅっぷん}**おきに**バスが{来|き}ます。
examples.romaji: sanjuppun oki ni basu ga kimasu.
examples.en: A bus comes every thirty minutes.

examples.ja: {椅子|いす}を{一|ひと}つ**おきに**{使|つか}います。
examples.romaji: isu o hitotsu oki ni tsukaimasu.
examples.en: We use every other chair.

examples.ja: {一日|いちにち}**ごとに**{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ります。
examples.romaji: 一日ごとに
examples.en: A photo is taken on each day; no day is skipped.

examples.ja: {一日|いちにち}**おきに**{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ります。
examples.romaji: 一日おきに
examples.en: One full day is left between photo days.

examples.ja: この{薬|くすり}は{一日|いちにち}**おきに**{飲|の}んでください。
examples.romaji: kono kusuri wa ichinichi oki ni nonde kudasai.
examples.en: Please take this medicine every other day.

examples.ja: コンサートの{席|せき}は、{一|ひと}つ**おきに**{座|すわ}ってください。
examples.romaji: konsaato no seki wa, hitotsu oki ni suwatte kudasai.
examples.en: Please sit in every other seat at the concert.

examples.ja: ノートには{一行|いちぎょう}**おきに**{書|か}いてください。
examples.romaji: nooto ni wa ichigyou oki ni kaite kudasai.
examples.en: Please write on every other line in your notebook.

title: The same amount at a time
goal: You'll be able to divide or distribute people, things, or actions into equal amounts.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Distribute equally or progress little by little
text: ～ずつ divides an amount equally among recipients or repeats an action in small units. It can mean each, at a time, or little by little.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ずつ
text: Place ずつ after the amount being distributed. Context identifies the recipients. 少しずつ describes gradual progress; 一人ずつ describes one person at a time.

formation: Quantity + ずつ

examples.ja: {母|はは}は{子供|こども}にりんごを{一|ひと}つ**ずつ**あげます。
examples.romaji: haha wa kodomo ni ringo o hitotsu zutsu agemasu.
examples.en: My mother gives each child one apple.

examples.ja: {祖母|そぼ}は{階段|かいだん}を{一段|いちだん}**ずつ**ゆっくり{上|のぼ}ります。
examples.romaji: sobo wa kaidan o ichidan zutsu yukkuri noborimasu.
examples.en: My grandmother goes up the stairs slowly, one step at a time.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}**ずつ**{入|はい}ってください。
examples.romaji: hitori zutsu haitte kudasai.
examples.en: Please enter one person at a time.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}し**ずつ**{勉強|べんきょう}します。
examples.romaji: mainichi sukoshi zutsu benkyou shimasu.
examples.en: I study a little each day.

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}**ずつ**{名前|なまえ}を{呼|よ}びます。
examples.romaji: hitori zutsu namae o yobimasu.
examples.en: I'll call your names one at a time.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{少|すこ}し**ずつ**{漢字|かんじ}を{覚|おぼ}えています。
examples.romaji: mainichi sukoshi zutsu kanji o oboete imasu.
examples.en: I'm learning kanji a little at a time every day.

examples.ja: みんなにお{菓子|かし}を{二|ふた}つ**ずつ**{配|くば}りました。
examples.romaji: minna ni okashi o futatsu zutsu kubarimashita.
examples.en: I handed out two sweets to each person.

examples.ja: ～ずつ
examples.romaji: The same amount at a time

title: Say how much time or money something takes
goal: You'll be able to state the cost or duration an action requires, and ask about it.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Say how much time or money is needed
text: かかる describes the time or cost required for an action. English often uses “take” for time and “cost” for money.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～かかる
text: A bare amount can precede かかる: 三十分かかる. Use 時間がかかる or お金がかかる when naming the resource rather than an exact amount. The actor does not take that resource as an を object.

formation: Exact amount + かかる / Time or money noun + がかかる

examples.ja: {駅|えき}まで{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}**かかります**。
examples.romaji: eki made sanjuppun kakarimasu.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes to reach the station.

examples.ja: {家|いえ}から{会社|かいしゃ}まで{電車|でんしゃ}で{一時間|いちじかん}**かかります**。
examples.romaji: ie kara kaisha made densha de ichijikan kakarimasu.
examples.en: It takes an hour by train from my home to the office.

examples.ja: {空港|くうこう}までタクシーで{五千円|ごせんえん}**かかりました**。
examples.romaji: kuukou made takushii de gosen'en kakarimashita.
examples.en: It cost 5,000 yen to get to the airport by taxi.

examples.ja: この{仕事|しごと}は{時間|じかん}**がかかります**。
examples.romaji: kono shigoto wa jikan ga kakarimasu.
examples.en: This job takes time.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}には{お金|おかね}**がかかります**。
examples.romaji: ryokou ni wa okane ga kakarimasu.
examples.en: Travel costs money.

examples.ja: パソコンが{直|なお}るまで、{一週間|いっしゅうかん}ぐらい**かかります**。
examples.romaji: pasokon ga naoru made, isshuukan gurai kakarimasu.
examples.en: It will take about a week for the computer to be fixed.

examples.ja: {東京|とうきょう}から{大阪|おおさか}まで{新幹線|しんかんせん}でどのぐらい**かかります**か。
examples.romaji: toukyou kara oosaka made shinkansen de dono gurai kakarimasu ka.
examples.en: How long does it take from Tokyo to Osaka by shinkansen?

examples.ja: {東京|とうきょう}は{生活|せいかつ}にお{金|かね}**がかかります**。
examples.romaji: toukyou wa seikatsu ni okane ga kakarimasu.
examples.en: Living in Tokyo costs a lot of money.

examples.ja: ～かかる (time and cost)
examples.romaji: Say how much time or money something takes

title: Emphasize that an amount is surprisingly large
goal: You'll be able to show surprise that a number or amount is as large as it is.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: React to a surprisingly large amount
text: A quantity followed by も presents the amount as larger than expected. It expresses the speaker's evaluation, not an objective definition of “a lot.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Quantity + も
text: Place も after the full amount and counter. This differs from additive も meaning “also.” The same number can sound large or small depending on the situation.

formation: Quantity + も

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}で{写真|しゃしん}を{百枚|ひゃくまい}**も**{撮|と}りました。
examples.romaji: ryokou de shashin o hyakumai mo torimashita.
examples.en: We took as many as a hundred photos during the trip.

examples.ja: {人気|にんき}のラーメン{屋|や}の{前|まえ}に、{五十人|ごじゅうにん}**も**{並|なら}んでいました。
examples.romaji: ninki no raamen'ya no mae ni, gojuunin mo narande imashita.
examples.en: As many as fifty people were lined up outside the popular ramen shop.

examples.ja: {二時間|にじかん}**も**{待|ま}ちました。
examples.romaji: nijikan mo machimashita.
examples.en: I waited for a whole two hours.

examples.ja: このかばんは{一万円|いちまんえん}**も**します。
examples.romaji: kono kaban wa ichiman'en mo shimasu.
examples.en: This bag costs as much as ten thousand yen.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}で{電車|でんしゃ}を{一時間|いちじかん}**も**{待|ま}ちました。
examples.romaji: eki de densha o ichijikan mo machimashita.
examples.en: I waited a whole hour for the train at the station.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}はコーヒーを{五杯|ごはい}**も**{飲|の}んでしまいました。
examples.romaji: kinou wa koohii o gohai mo nonde shimaimashita.
examples.en: I drank as many as five cups of coffee yesterday.

examples.ja: このホテルは{一泊|いっぱく}{五万円|ごまんえん}**も**します。
examples.romaji: kono hoteru wa ippaku goman'en mo shimasu.
examples.en: This hotel costs a whopping 50,000 yen a night.

examples.ja: Quantity + も
examples.romaji: Emphasize that an amount is surprisingly large

title: No more than this one limited choice
goal: You'll be able to emphasize that nothing beyond a small amount or limited option is available.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Limit the available amount
text: ～しか～ない means only or nothing except. It often emphasizes that the amount or choice is limited. Although the Japanese predicate is negative, the English translation often is not.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～しか～ない
text: Use しか with a negative ending: 一つしかない. It replaces が or を, while particles such as に may remain before it. だけ can use an affirmative predicate and is more neutral.

formation: Noun or quantity + しか + Negative predicate

examples.ja: りんごは{一|ひと}つ**しか**あり**ません**。
examples.romaji: ringo wa hitotsu shika arimasen.
examples.en: There is only one apple.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}では{現金|げんきん}**しか**{使|つか}え**ません**。
examples.romaji: kono mise de wa genkin shika tsukaemasen.
examples.en: You can only use cash at this shop.

examples.ja: {百円|ひゃくえん}**しか**{持|も}ってい**ません**。
examples.romaji: hyakuen shika motte imasen.
examples.en: I have only one hundred yen.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{水|みず}**しか**{飲|の}み**ません**。
examples.romaji: ren wa mizu shika nomimasen.
examples.en: Ren drinks only water.

examples.ja: {財布|さいふ}に{千円|せんえん}**しか**ありません。
examples.romaji: saifu ni sen'en shika arimasen.
examples.en: I only have 1,000 yen in my wallet.

examples.ja: この{村|むら}にはバスが{一日|いちにち}に{二本|にほん}**しか**{来|き}ません。
examples.romaji: kono mura ni wa basu ga ichinichi ni nihon shika kimasen.
examples.en: Only two buses a day come to this village.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{忙|いそが}しくて、{三時間|さんじかん}**しか**{寝|ね}られませんでした。
examples.romaji: kinou wa isogashikute, sanjikan shika neraremasen deshita.
examples.en: I was busy yesterday and only got three hours of sleep.

examples.ja: ～しか～ない
examples.romaji: No more than this one limited choice
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Nothing but the same kind of thing
goal: You'll be able to say that something is overwhelmingly limited to one kind, often more than expected or wanted.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe an unbalanced concentration
text: ～ばかり says someone does or chooses almost nothing but one thing. It often suggests the concentration is excessive, although criticism depends on context.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ばかり
text: Noun + ばかり can be followed by particles. てばかりいる describes repeated or continual focus on an action. Do not confuse this with たばかり, which means recently did.

formation: Noun + ばかり / Verb て-form + ばかりいる

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{お菓子|おかし}**ばかり**{食|た}べています。
examples.romaji: mei wa okashi bakari tabete imasu.
examples.en: Mei is eating almost nothing but sweets.

examples.ja: {弟|おとうと}は{毎日|まいにち}ゲーム**ばかり**しています。
examples.romaji: otouto wa mainichi geemu bakari shite imasu.
examples.en: My younger brother does nothing but play games every day.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{寝|ね}て**ばかりいます**。
examples.romaji: yasumi no hi wa nete bakari imasu.
examples.en: On days off I do almost nothing but sleep.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{高|たか}い{物|もの}**ばかり**です。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa takai mono bakari desu.
examples.en: This shop has almost nothing but expensive things.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}、{父|ちち}はゴルフ**ばかり**しています。
examples.romaji: yasumi no hi, chichi wa gorufu bakari shite imasu.
examples.en: On his days off, my father plays nothing but golf.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{家|いえ}ではテレビを{見|み}て**ばかり**います。
examples.romaji: chichi wa ie de wa terebi o mite bakari imasu.
examples.en: At home, my father does nothing but watch TV.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}、{雨|あめ}**ばかり**{降|ふ}っています。
examples.romaji: saikin, ame bakari futte imasu.
examples.en: Lately, it's done nothing but rain.

examples.ja: ～ばかり
examples.romaji: Nothing but the same kind of thing
