title: A result comes from just one thing
goal: You'll be able to say that a single action or condition is enough to produce a result.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: A small condition is enough
text: ～だけで says that one limited action, condition, or means is sufficient for a result. It often highlights how little is needed.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～だけで
text: Use 押すだけで for “just by pressing” and 一人だけで for “with only one person.” Do not interpret で here only as a location marker.

formation: Plain verb or Noun + だけで + Result

examples.ja: このボタンを{押|お}す**だけで**ドアが{開|あ}きます。
examples.romaji: kono botan o osu dake de doa ga akimasu.
examples.en: The door opens just by pressing this button.

examples.ja: カードをタッチする**だけで**、{電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}れます。
examples.romaji: kaado o tatchi suru dake de, densha ni noremasu.
examples.en: You can get on the train just by touching your card.

examples.ja: {見|み}る**だけで**{分|わ}かります。
examples.romaji: miru dake de wakarimasu.
examples.en: I can understand just by looking.

examples.ja: {千円|せんえん}**だけで**{買|か}えます。
examples.romaji: sen'en dake de kaemasu.
examples.en: You can buy it for only one thousand yen.

examples.ja: このアプリは{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}る**だけで**、{言葉|ことば}の{意味|いみ}が{分|わ}かります。
examples.romaji: kono apuri wa shashin o toru dake de, kotoba no imi ga wakarimasu.
examples.en: With this app, you can find out what a word means just by taking a photo.

examples.ja: この{紙|かみ}に{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}く**だけで**、{図書館|としょかん}のカードが{作|つく}れます。
examples.romaji: kono kami ni namae o kaku dake de, toshokan no kaado ga tsukuremasu.
examples.en: You can get a library card just by writing your name on this sheet.

examples.ja: {彼女|かのじょ}の{顔|かお}を{見|み}る**だけで**、{元気|げんき}になります。
examples.romaji: kanojo no kao o miru dake de, genki ni narimasu.
examples.en: Just seeing her face cheers me up.

examples.ja: ～だけで
examples.romaji: A result comes from just one thing
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Anyone, anything, anywhere, or anytime
goal: You'll be able to remove limits from question words to mean any person, thing, place, or time.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Allow any choice
text: Question word + でも means any member of the relevant set: anyone, anything, anywhere, or anytime. It removes a restriction rather than asking a question.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Question word + でも
text: 誰でも means anyone, while 誰か means someone. Let the surrounding predicate define the allowed choices. Do not confuse でも with the negative pairing 誰も…ない.

formation: 誰 / 何 / どこ / いつ + でも

examples.ja: このゲームは{誰|だれ}**でも**{楽|たの}しめます。
examples.romaji: kono geemu wa dare demo tanoshimemasu.
examples.en: Anyone can enjoy this game.

examples.ja: このカードは{日本|にほん}のどこ**でも**{使|つか}えます。
examples.romaji: kono kaado wa nihon no doko demo tsukaemasu.
examples.en: You can use this card anywhere in Japan.

examples.ja: いつ**でも**{来|き}てください。
examples.romaji: itsu demo kite kudasai.
examples.en: Please come anytime.

examples.ja: {何|なん}**でも**{食|た}べます。
examples.romaji: nan demo tabemasu.
examples.en: I eat anything.

examples.ja: {分|わ}からないことは、{何|なん}**でも**{聞|き}いてください。
examples.romaji: wakaranai koto wa, nan demo kiite kudasai.
examples.en: Ask me anything you don't understand.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{二十四時間|にじゅうよじかん}{開|あ}いているので、いつ**でも**{買|か}い{物|もの}ができます。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa nijuuyojikan aite iru node, itsu demo kaimono ga dekimasu.
examples.en: This shop is open 24 hours, so you can shop there anytime.

examples.ja: この{公園|こうえん}はだれ**でも**{無料|むりょう}で{入|はい}れます。
examples.romaji: kono kouen wa dare demo muryou de hairemasu.
examples.en: Anyone can enter this park for free.

examples.ja: Question word + でも
examples.romaji: Anyone, anything, anywhere, or anytime
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Include something surprising or unexpected
goal: You'll be able to use まで to emphasize that even an unexpected person, thing, place, or extent is included.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Include an unexpected extreme
text: まで can mean even when it adds a surprising person or thing to what is already true. The surprise comes from including something beyond the expected range.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～まで (even)
text: This is not the endpoint meaning “until” or “as far as.” も can simply add another item; まで emphasizes that even this unexpected case is included.

formation: Unexpected person or thing + まで

examples.ja: {祖父|そふ}**まで**ゲームに{参加|さんか}しました。
examples.romaji: sofu made geemu ni sanka shimashita.
examples.en: Even my grandfather joined the game.

examples.ja: このアニメは{大人|おとな}**まで**{見|み}ています。
examples.romaji: kono anime wa otona made mite imasu.
examples.en: Even adults watch this anime.

examples.ja: {靴|くつ}の{中|なか}**まで**ぬれました。
examples.romaji: kutsu no naka made nuremashita.
examples.en: Even the inside of my shoes got wet.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}**まで**{笑|わら}いました。
examples.romaji: sensei made waraimashita.
examples.en: Even the teacher laughed.

examples.ja: {近所|きんじょ}の{子|こ}ども**まで**その{歌|うた}を{歌|うた}っています。
examples.romaji: kinjo no kodomo made sono uta o utatte imasu.
examples.en: Even the children in my neighborhood are singing that song.

examples.ja: {大雨|おおあめ}で、かばんの{中|なか}の{本|ほん}**まで**ぬれてしまいました。
examples.romaji: ooame de, kaban no naka no hon made nurete shimaimashita.
examples.en: In the heavy rain, even the books inside my bag got wet.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{暑|あつ}いので、いつも{元気|げんき}な{犬|いぬ}**まで**{寝|ね}ています。
examples.romaji: kyou wa atsui node, itsumo genki na inu made nete imasu.
examples.en: It's so hot today that even our usually lively dog is sleeping.

examples.ja: ～まで (even)
examples.romaji: Include something surprising or unexpected
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: At least this amount or more
goal: You'll be able to set a lower boundary that is included in a number or range.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Include a lower boundary
text: ～以上 means at least the stated number: the boundary itself is included. It is useful for minimum ages, amounts, or group sizes.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～以上
text: 十人以上 includes exactly ten and any higher number. It does not mean strictly more than ten. Keep the counter with its number.

formation: Number and counter + 以上

examples.ja: このゲームは{三人|さんにん}**{以上|いじょう}**で{遊|あそ}べます。
examples.romaji: kono geemu wa sannin ijou de asobemasu.
examples.en: This game can be played by three or more people.

examples.ja: {六十五歳|ろくじゅうごさい}**{以上|いじょう}**の{方|かた}は、バスの{料金|りょうきん}が{安|やす}くなります。
examples.romaji: rokujuugosai ijou no kata wa, basu no ryoukin ga yasuku narimasu.
examples.en: The bus fare is cheaper for people aged sixty-five and over.

examples.ja: {千円|せんえん}**{以上|いじょう}**{買|か}うと、{送料無料|そうりょうむりょう}です。
examples.romaji: sen'en ijou kau to, souryou muryou desu.
examples.en: Shipping is free when you spend at least one thousand yen.

examples.ja: {一時間|いちじかん}**{以上|いじょう}**{待|ま}ちました。
examples.romaji: ichijikan ijou machimashita.
examples.en: I waited for at least an hour.

examples.ja: この{映画|えいが}は{十八歳|じゅうはっさい}**{以上|いじょう}**の{人|ひと}しか{見|み}られません。
examples.romaji: kono eiga wa juuhassai ijou no hito shika miraremasen.
examples.en: Only people aged eighteen and over can see this movie.

examples.ja: {三千円|さんぜんえん}**{以上|いじょう}**{買|か}い{物|もの}をした{人|ひと}は、{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}が{無料|むりょう}です。
examples.romaji: sanzen'en ijou kaimono o shita hito wa, chuushajou ga muryou desu.
examples.en: Parking is free for people who spend 3,000 yen or more.

examples.ja: {病院|びょういん}で{二時間|にじかん}**{以上|いじょう}**{待|ま}ちました。
examples.romaji: byouin de nijikan ijou machimashita.
examples.en: I waited at the hospital for more than two hours.

examples.ja: ～以上
examples.romaji: At least this amount or more
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: This amount or less
goal: You'll be able to set an upper boundary that is included in a number or range.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Include an upper boundary
text: ～以下 means no more than the stated amount. The upper boundary itself is included. It is common for limits and eligibility conditions.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～以下
text: 十歳以下 includes someone exactly ten years old. 未満 means strictly below the boundary, which is a different limit.

formation: Number and counter + 以下

examples.ja: {荷物|にもつ}は{五|ご}キロ**{以下|いか}**にしてください。
examples.romaji: nimotsu wa gokiro ika ni shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please keep the luggage to five kilograms or less.

examples.ja: {六歳|ろくさい}**{以下|いか}**の{子|こ}どもは{無料|むりょう}です。
examples.romaji: rokusai ika no kodomo wa muryou desu.
examples.en: Children aged six and under are free.

examples.ja: {千円|せんえん}**{以下|いか}**の{本|ほん}を{探|さが}しています。
examples.romaji: sen'en ika no hon o sagashite imasu.
examples.en: I am looking for a book costing no more than one thousand yen.

examples.ja: {十人|じゅうにん}**{以下|いか}**で{入|はい}ってください。
examples.romaji: juunin ika de haitte kudasai.
examples.en: Please enter in groups of no more than ten.

examples.ja: {荷物|にもつ}を{七|なな}キロ**{以下|いか}**に{減|へ}らしてください。
examples.romaji: nimotsu o nana kiro ika ni herashite kudasai.
examples.en: Please reduce your luggage to seven kilograms or less.

examples.ja: {今朝|けさ}は{気温|きおん}がゼロ{度|ど}**{以下|いか}**になりました。
examples.romaji: kesa wa kion ga zero do ika ni narimashita.
examples.en: This morning the temperature fell to zero degrees or below.

examples.ja: {作文|さくぶん}は{八百字|はっぴゃくじ}**{以下|いか}**で{書|か}いてください。
examples.romaji: sakubun wa happyakuji ika de kaite kudasai.
examples.en: Please write your essay in 800 characters or fewer.

examples.ja: ～以下
examples.romaji: This amount or less
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Everything except this
goal: You'll be able to exclude one person, thing, place, or category from a statement.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Exclude one thing from a set
text: ～以外 means other than or except. It identifies what is excluded; the predicate tells you what is true of the remaining possibilities.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～以外
text: Use 以外は to discuss the remaining set, 以外に for another option, and 以外の before a noun. It does not automatically mean every other item exists or participates.

formation: Noun + 以外 + Particle or の + noun

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}**{以外|いがい}**はみんな{起|お}きています。
examples.romaji: mei igai wa minna okite imasu.
examples.en: Everyone except Mei is awake.

examples.ja: スタッフ**{以外|いがい}**は、この{部屋|へや}に{入|はい}ってはいけません。
examples.romaji: sutaffu igai wa, kono heya ni haitte wa ikemasen.
examples.en: No one except staff may enter this room.

examples.ja: {水|みず}**{以外|いがい}**に{何|なに}がありますか。
examples.romaji: mizu igai ni nani ga arimasu ka.
examples.en: What is there besides water?

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}**{以外|いがい}**は{働|はたら}いています。
examples.romaji: nichiyoubi igai wa hataraite imasu.
examples.en: I work every day except Sunday.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{水曜日|すいようび}**{以外|いがい}**、{毎日|まいにち}{開|あ}いています。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa suiyoubi igai, mainichi aite imasu.
examples.en: This shop is open every day except Wednesday.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}**{以外|いがい}**の{家族|かぞく}は、みんな{犬|いぬ}が{好|す}きです。
examples.romaji: watashi igai no kazoku wa, minna inu ga suki desu.
examples.en: Everyone in my family except me likes dogs.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}**{以外|いがい}**に、{何|なに}か{外国語|がいこくご}ができますか。
examples.romaji: nihongo igai ni, nanika gaikokugo ga dekimasu ka.
examples.en: Can you speak any other foreign languages besides Japanese?

examples.ja: ～以外
examples.romaji: Everything except this
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Ask which of two choices
goal: You'll be able to ask which of two specific options someone prefers or which has a property.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Ask a comparison between two choices
text: AとBとどちら asks which of two choices has a property or is preferred. Put と after each option before どちら.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use AとBとどちら
text: Use どちら for two alternatives. With three or more items, a question with どれ and 一番 is often more suitable. Conversational どっち is less formal.

formation: A + と + B + とどちらが + Predicate

examples.ja: りんご**と**みかん**とどちらが**{好|す}きですか。
examples.romaji: ringo to mikan to dochira ga suki desu ka.
examples.en: Which do you prefer, apples or mandarins?

examples.ja: {東京|とうきょう}**と**{大阪|おおさか}**とどちらが**{人|ひと}が{多|おお}いですか。
examples.romaji: toukyou to oosaka to dochira ga hito ga ooi desu ka.
examples.en: Which has more people, Tokyo or Osaka?

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}**と**バス**とどちらが**{速|はや}いですか。
examples.romaji: densha to basu to dochira ga hayai desu ka.
examples.en: Which is faster, the train or the bus?

examples.ja: {お茶|おちゃ}**と**コーヒー**とどちらが**{好|す}きですか。
examples.romaji: ocha to koohii to dochira ga suki desu ka.
examples.en: Which do you prefer, tea or coffee?

examples.ja: {新幹線|しんかんせん}と{飛行機|ひこうき}**とどちらが**{便利|べんり}ですか。
examples.romaji: shinkansen to hikouki to dochira ga benri desu ka.
examples.en: Which is more convenient, the shinkansen or a plane?

examples.ja: {夏|なつ}と{冬|ふゆ}**とどちらが**{好|す}きですか。
examples.romaji: natsu to fuyu to dochira ga suki desu ka.
examples.en: Which do you like better, summer or winter?

examples.ja: この{赤|あか}いシャツと{青|あお}いシャツ**とどちらが**{似合|にあ}いますか。
examples.romaji: kono akai shatsu to aoi shatsu to dochira ga niaimasu ka.
examples.en: Which suits me better, this red shirt or the blue one?

examples.ja: AとBとどちら
examples.romaji: Ask which of two choices
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Not as much as something else
goal: You'll be able to compare two things and say that one does not reach the other's degree.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Say one thing is not as much as another
text: AはBほど～ない says A does not reach B's degree of the quality. The item before ほど is the higher comparison standard.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ほど～ない
text: Use a negative ending such as 高くない or 上手ではない. Reversing A and B reverses the comparison. It need not say A has none of the quality.

formation: A は B + ほど + Negative predicate

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{蓮|れん}**ほど**{背|せ}が{高|たか}く**ありません**。
examples.romaji: mei wa ren hodo se ga takaku arimasen.
examples.en: Mei is not as tall as Ren.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{姉|あね}**ほど**{日本語|にほんご}が{上手|じょうず}**ではありません**。
examples.romaji: watashi wa ane hodo nihongo ga jouzu de wa arimasen.
examples.en: My Japanese isn't as good as my older sister's.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{昨日|きのう}**ほど**{寒|さむ}く**ない**です。
examples.romaji: kyou wa kinou hodo samukunai desu.
examples.en: Today is not as cold as yesterday.

examples.ja: バスは{電車|でんしゃ}**ほど**{速|はや}く**ありません**。
examples.romaji: basu wa densha hodo hayaku arimasen.
examples.en: The bus is not as fast as the train.

examples.ja: {今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}は{去年|きょねん}**ほど**{暑|あつ}くないです。
examples.romaji: kotoshi no natsu wa kyonen hodo atsuku nai desu.
examples.en: This summer isn't as hot as last year.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}のラーメンは、{駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}**ほど**おいしくありません。
examples.romaji: kono mise no raamen wa, ekimae no mise hodo oishiku arimasen.
examples.en: The ramen at this shop isn't as good as at the shop by the station.

examples.ja: {大阪|おおさか}は{東京|とうきょう}**ほど**{大|おお}きくないです。
examples.romaji: oosaka wa toukyou hodo ookiku nai desu.
examples.en: Osaka isn't as big as Tokyo.

examples.ja: ～ほど～ない
examples.romaji: Not as much as something else
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Not very or not much
goal: You'll be able to soften a negative statement by saying something is not true to a great degree.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Express a low degree or frequency
text: あまり with a negative predicate means not very much or not often. It leaves room for a small amount, unlike a complete denial.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use あまり～ない
text: Use あまり食べない for not eating much and あまり高くない for not very expensive. This lesson uses the negative pattern, not other affirmative uses of あまり.

formation: あまり + Negative verb or adjective

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{野菜|やさい}を**あまり**{食|た}べ**ません**。
examples.romaji: mei wa yasai o amari tabemasen.
examples.en: Mei does not eat many vegetables.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}はお{酒|さけ}を**あまり**{飲|の}み**ません**。
examples.romaji: watashi wa osake o amari nomimasen.
examples.en: I don't drink much alcohol.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}は**あまり**{高|たか}く**ない**です。
examples.romaji: kono hon wa amari takakunai desu.
examples.en: This book is not very expensive.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}は**あまり**テレビを{見|み}**ません**。
examples.romaji: saikin wa amari terebi o mimasen.
examples.en: I do not watch television much these days.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}は{忙|いそが}しくて、**あまり**{寝|ね}ていません。
examples.romaji: saikin wa isogashikute, amari nete imasen.
examples.en: I've been busy lately and haven't been sleeping much.

examples.ja: この{映画|えいが}は**あまり**おもしろくなかったです。
examples.romaji: kono eiga wa amari omoshiroku nakatta desu.
examples.en: This movie wasn't very interesting.

examples.ja: この{辺|へん}は{夜|よる}、**あまり**{人|ひと}がいません。
examples.romaji: kono hen wa yoru, amari hito ga imasen.
examples.en: There aren't many people around here at night.

examples.ja: あまり～ない
examples.romaji: Not very or not much
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Something does not happen easily
goal: You'll be able to express that an expected or desired result is taking longer or proving harder than hoped.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Wait longer than expected for a result
text: なかなか～ない says an expected result does not happen easily or soon. It often conveys difficulty, delay, or frustration despite effort or waiting.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use なかなか～ない
text: Use 来ない for a delayed arrival and 覚えられない for difficulty memorizing. Affirmative なかなか can mean “quite,” which is a separate use.

formation: なかなか + Negative predicate

examples.ja: バスが**なかなか**{来|き}**ません**。
examples.romaji: basu ga nakanaka kimasen.
examples.en: The bus is taking a long time to come.

examples.ja: {風邪|かぜ}が**なかなか**{治|なお}り**ません**。
examples.romaji: kaze ga nakanaka naorimasen.
examples.en: My cold just won't go away.

examples.ja: この{漢字|かんじ}が**なかなか**{覚|おぼ}えられ**ません**。
examples.romaji: kono kanji ga nakanaka oboeraremasen.
examples.en: I cannot seem to memorize this kanji.

examples.ja: {夜|よる}、**なかなか**{眠|ねむ}れ**ません**。
examples.romaji: yoru, nakanaka nemuremasen.
examples.en: At night I have trouble getting to sleep.

examples.ja: タクシーが**なかなか**{来|こ}ないので、{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}きました。
examples.romaji: takushii ga nakanaka konai node, eki made arukimashita.
examples.en: The taxi just wasn't coming, so I walked to the station.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{生活|せいかつ}に**なかなか**{慣|な}れません。
examples.romaji: nihon no seikatsu ni nakanaka naremasen.
examples.en: I just can't get used to life in Japan.

examples.ja: {仕事|しごと}が{多|おお}くて、**なかなか**{帰|かえ}れません。
examples.romaji: shigoto ga ookute, nakanaka kaeremasen.
examples.en: I have so much work that I just can't get away and go home.

examples.ja: なかなか～ない
examples.romaji: Something does not happen easily
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Not at all
goal: You'll be able to make a strong negative statement that leaves no degree or amount.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Deny something completely
text: 全然～ない means not at all. It emphasizes a complete lack of an action, understanding, or quality.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use 全然～ない
text: Use negative verbs, adjectives, or copular forms. Colloquial affirmative expressions such as 全然大丈夫 exist, but this lesson practices the negative construction.

formation: 全然 + Negative predicate

examples.ja: この{問題|もんだい}は**{全然|ぜんぜん}**{分|わ}かり**ません**。
examples.romaji: kono mondai wa zenzen wakarimasen.
examples.en: I do not understand this question at all.

examples.ja: すみません、その{人|ひと}の{名前|なまえ}は**{全然|ぜんぜん}**{知|し}り**ません**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, sono hito no namae wa zenzen shirimasen.
examples.en: Sorry, I don't know that person's name at all.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は**{全然|ぜんぜん}**{寒|さむ}く**ない**です。
examples.romaji: kyou wa zenzen samukunai desu.
examples.en: It is not cold at all today.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は**{全然|ぜんぜん}**{勉強|べんきょう}し**ませんでした**。
examples.romaji: kinou wa zenzen benkyou shimasen deshita.
examples.en: I did not study at all yesterday.

examples.ja: {卒業|そつぎょう}してから、{高校|こうこう}の{友|とも}だちには**{全然|ぜんぜん}**{会|あ}っていません。
examples.romaji: sotsugyou shite kara, koukou no tomodachi ni wa zenzen atte imasen.
examples.en: Since graduating, I haven't seen my high school friends at all.

examples.ja: {先月|せんげつ}から、{兄|あに}から**{全然|ぜんぜん}**{連絡|れんらく}がありません。
examples.romaji: sengetsu kara, ani kara zenzen renraku ga arimasen.
examples.en: I haven't heard from my older brother at all since last month.

examples.ja: {去年|きょねん}{買|か}った{自転車|じてんしゃ}は、**{全然|ぜんぜん}**{使|つか}っていません。
examples.romaji: kyonen katta jitensha wa, zenzen tsukatte imasen.
examples.en: I haven't used the bicycle I bought last year at all.

examples.ja: 全然～ない
examples.romaji: Not at all
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Not even a little
goal: You'll be able to stress that there is not the slightest amount of something.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Emphasize not even a little
text: 少しも～ない means not the slightest amount or not at all. 少し sets a tiny amount that the negative predicate denies.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use 少しも～ない
text: Use a negative form even though 少し alone means a little. This can sound emphatic. 少しだけ instead allows a small positive amount.

formation: 少しも + Negative predicate

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は**{少|すこ}しも**{怖|こわ}く**ありません**。
examples.romaji: mei wa sukoshi mo kowaku arimasen.
examples.en: Mei is not scared at all.

examples.ja: この{薬|くすり}は**{少|すこ}しも**{苦|にが}く**ない**ですよ。
examples.romaji: kono kusuri wa sukoshi mo nigaku nai desu yo.
examples.en: This medicine isn't the least bit bitter.

examples.ja: この{荷物|にもつ}は**{少|すこ}しも**{重|おも}く**ない**です。
examples.romaji: kono nimotsu wa sukoshi mo omokunai desu.
examples.en: This luggage is not heavy at all.

examples.ja: **{少|すこ}しも**{疲|つか}れてい**ません**。
examples.romaji: sukoshi mo tsukarete imasen.
examples.en: I am not tired in the slightest.

examples.ja: {心配|しんぱい}していた{試験|しけん}は、**{少|すこ}しも**{難|むずか}しくなかったです。
examples.romaji: shinpai shite ita shiken wa, sukoshi mo muzukashiku nakatta desu.
examples.en: The exam I'd been worried about wasn't the least bit difficult.

examples.ja: {長|なが}い{旅行|りょこう}でしたが、{祖母|そぼ}は**{少|すこ}しも**{疲|つか}れた{顔|かお}をしませんでした。
examples.romaji: nagai ryokou deshita ga, sobo wa sukoshi mo tsukareta kao o shimasen deshita.
examples.en: It was a long trip, but my grandmother didn't look the least bit tired.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}はエアコンが{壊|こわ}れているので、**{少|すこ}しも**{涼|すず}しくないです。
examples.romaji: kono heya wa eakon ga kowarete iru node, sukoshi mo suzushiku nai desu.
examples.en: The air conditioner in this room is broken, so it isn't the least bit cool.

examples.ja: 少しも～ない
examples.romaji: Not even a little
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Not as much as you might think
goal: You'll be able to correct an assumption by saying something is not true to the degree the listener suggested.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Reject an assumed degree
text: そんなに～ない means not that much or not as much as suggested. It responds to a degree raised by the listener or situation.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use そんなに～ない
text: This differs from a neutral あまり～ない because it points back to an assumed degree. そんなに can also occur affirmatively; the negative use here denies that level.

formation: そんなに + Negative predicate

examples.ja: この{荷物|にもつ}は**そんなに**{重|おも}く**ない**です。
examples.romaji: kono nimotsu wa sonna ni omokunai desu.
examples.en: This luggage is not that heavy.

examples.ja: この{映画|えいが}はみんな{怖|こわ}いと{言|い}っていますが、**そんなに**{怖|こわ}く**なかった**です。
examples.romaji: kono eiga wa minna kowai to itte imasu ga, sonna ni kowaku nakatta desu.
examples.en: Everyone says this movie is scary, but it wasn't that scary.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}は**そんなに**{遠|とお}く**ありません**。
examples.romaji: eki wa sonna ni tooku arimasen.
examples.en: The station is not that far away.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は**そんなに**{忙|いそが}しく**ない**です。
examples.romaji: kyou wa sonna ni isogashikunai desu.
examples.en: I am not that busy today.

examples.ja: この{仕事|しごと}は**そんなに**{難|むずか}しくないですから、{心配|しんぱい}しないでください。
examples.romaji: kono shigoto wa sonna ni muzukashiku nai desu kara, shinpai shinaide kudasai.
examples.en: This job isn't as hard as you think, so please don't worry.

examples.ja: え、このかばん、**そんなに**{高|たか}くなかったよ。{三千円|さんぜんえん}だった。
examples.romaji: e, kono kaban, sonna ni takaku nakatta yo. sanzen'en datta.
examples.en: What? This bag wasn't that expensive. It was 3,000 yen.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}はまだ**そんなに**{上手|じょうず}じゃありません。
examples.romaji: nihongo wa mada sonna ni jouzu ja arimasen.
examples.en: My Japanese isn't that good yet.

examples.ja: そんなに～ない
examples.romaji: Not as much as you might think
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Almost all, or hardly anything
goal: You'll be able to describe amounts that are nearly complete, and use negative verbs to say something hardly ever happens.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe almost all or almost none
text: ほとんど with an affirmative predicate means almost all or nearly complete. With a negative predicate, it means hardly any or almost never. The polarity changes the overall meaning.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ほとんど
text: ほとんど終わった leaves only a little unfinished. ほとんど食べない allows very little eating. It is not identical to 全部 or 全然, which can express complete totals or denial.

formation: ほとんど + Predicate / ほとんどの + Noun

examples.ja: {宿題|しゅくだい}は**ほとんど**{終|お}わりました。
examples.romaji: shukudai wa hotondo owarimashita.
examples.en: My homework is almost finished.

examples.ja: {財布|さいふ}にお{金|かね}が**ほとんど**ありません。
examples.romaji: saifu ni okane ga hotondo arimasen.
examples.en: There's hardly any money in my wallet.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}は**ほとんど**{外食|がいしょく}しません。
examples.romaji: saikin wa hotondo gaishoku shimasen.
examples.en: I hardly ever eat out these days.

examples.ja: **ほとんどの**{人|ひと}が{帰|かえ}りました。
examples.romaji: hotondo no hito ga kaerimashita.
examples.en: Almost everyone has gone home.

examples.ja: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{準備|じゅんび}は**ほとんど**{終|お}わりました。
examples.romaji: hikkoshi no junbi wa hotondo owarimashita.
examples.en: I've almost finished getting ready for the move.

examples.ja: {週末|しゅうまつ}は**ほとんど**{家|いえ}にいます。
examples.romaji: shuumatsu wa hotondo ie ni imasu.
examples.en: On weekends, I'm at home almost all the time.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}は**ほとんど**テレビを{見|み}ません。
examples.romaji: saikin wa hotondo terebi o mimasen.
examples.en: I hardly watch TV these days.

examples.ja: ほとんど
examples.romaji: Almost all, or hardly anything
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Roughly, approximately, or the general gist
goal: You'll be able to give rough estimates for numbers and time, or state that you grasp the main outline of something.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Give an approximate amount or general picture
text: だいたい means approximately or in broad outline. It is useful when an exact number or every detail is unnecessary.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use だいたい
text: Use it before a number for an estimate, or with 分かる for general understanding. It does not promise exactness and is not the same as “all without exception.”

formation: だいたい + Quantity or predicate

examples.ja: {駅|えき}まで**だいたい**{二十分|にじゅっぷん}です。
examples.romaji: eki made daitai nijuppun desu.
examples.en: It is about twenty minutes to the station.

examples.ja: {道|みち}は**だいたい**{分|わ}かりますから、{地図|ちず}はいりません。
examples.romaji: michi wa daitai wakarimasu kara, chizu wa irimasen.
examples.en: I roughly know the way, so I don't need a map.

examples.ja: {話|はなし}は**だいたい**{分|わ}かりました。
examples.romaji: hanashi wa daitai wakarimashita.
examples.en: I understood the general idea of the story.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}**だいたい**{七時|しちじ}に{起|お}きます。
examples.romaji: maiasa daitai shichiji ni okimasu.
examples.en: I get up at around seven every morning.

examples.ja: {家|いえ}から{会社|かいしゃ}まで、**だいたい**{四十分|よんじゅっぷん}かかります。
examples.romaji: ie kara kaisha made, daitai yonjuppun kakarimasu.
examples.en: It takes roughly forty minutes to get from my home to the office.

examples.ja: この{仕事|しごと}は**だいたい**{三時間|さんじかん}で{終|お}わります。
examples.romaji: kono shigoto wa daitai sanjikan de owarimasu.
examples.en: This job takes about three hours to finish.

examples.ja: {毎晩|まいばん}**だいたい**{十一時|じゅういちじ}に{寝|ね}ます。
examples.romaji: maiban daitai juuichiji ni nemasu.
examples.en: I usually go to bed around eleven every night.

examples.ja: だいたい
examples.romaji: Roughly, approximately, or the general gist
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: The whole time, or by far
goal: You'll be able to stress that something continues unbroken, or that it beats an alternative by a wide margin.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Extend through time or strengthen a comparison
text: ずっと can mean continuously or all along. In a comparison it means much or far more. The surrounding words tell you which use applies.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ずっと
text: With a time period, it extends the state through that period. With より, it strengthens the difference. Do not translate every occurrence as “always.”

formation: ずっと + Continuing predicate / Comparison + ずっと + adjective

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は**ずっと**{窓|まど}の{外|そと}を{見|み}ていました。
examples.romaji: mei wa zutto mado no soto o mite imashita.
examples.en: Mei was looking out of the window the whole time.

examples.ja: {新幹線|しんかんせん}はバスより**ずっと**{速|はや}いです。
examples.romaji: shinkansen wa basu yori zutto hayai desu.
examples.en: The shinkansen is much faster than the bus.

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}はあの{部屋|へや}より**ずっと**{広|ひろ}いです。
examples.romaji: kono heya wa ano heya yori zutto hiroi desu.
examples.en: This room is much larger than that room.

examples.ja: これからも**ずっと**{友達|ともだち}です。
examples.romaji: kore kara mo zutto tomodachi desu.
examples.en: We will remain friends from now on.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{一日中|いちにちじゅう}、**ずっと**{家|いえ}で{寝|ね}ていました。
examples.romaji: kinou wa ichinichijuu, zutto ie de nete imashita.
examples.en: Yesterday I stayed home in bed the whole day.

examples.ja: {子|こ}どものときから、**ずっと**この{町|まち}に{住|す}んでいます。
examples.romaji: kodomo no toki kara, zutto kono machi ni sunde imasu.
examples.en: I've lived in this town ever since I was a child.

examples.ja: {朝|あさ}から**ずっと**{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っています。
examples.romaji: asa kara zutto ame ga futte imasu.
examples.en: It's been raining nonstop since the morning.

examples.ja: ずっと
examples.romaji: The whole time, or by far
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Set one topic against another
goal: You'll be able to use は contrastively to highlight a difference between people, things, situations, or parts of a sentence.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Set one alternative against another
text: Contrastive は singles out one item against another stated or implied possibility. It may suggest “as for this one, however” rather than simply introducing a topic.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Contrastive は
text: は replaces が or を in many contrastive phrases, but follows particles such as に and で: には, では. A second contrast need not be spoken if the context supplies it.

formation: Contrasted item + は + Predicate

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}はコーヒー**は**{飲|の}みますが、{紅茶|こうちゃ}**は**{飲|の}みません。
examples.romaji: ren wa koohii wa nomimasu ga, koucha wa nomimasen.
examples.en: Ren drinks coffee, but he does not drink black tea.

examples.ja: ひらがな**は**{読|よ}めますが、{漢字|かんじ}**は**まだ{読|よ}めません。
examples.romaji: hiragana wa yomemasu ga, kanji wa mada yomemasen.
examples.en: I can read hiragana, but I can't read kanji yet.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}**は**{行|い}けませんが、{明日|あした}**は**{行|い}けます。
examples.romaji: kyou wa ikemasen ga, ashita wa ikemasu.
examples.en: I cannot go today, but I can go tomorrow.

examples.ja: {魚|さかな}**は**{好|す}きですが、{肉|にく}**は**あまり{好|す}きではありません。
examples.romaji: sakana wa suki desu ga, niku wa amari suki dewa arimasen.
examples.en: I like fish, but I do not like meat very much.

examples.ja: {肉|にく}は{食|た}べますが、{魚|さかな}**は**{食|た}べません。
examples.romaji: niku wa tabemasu ga, sakana wa tabemasen.
examples.en: I eat meat, but I don't eat fish.

examples.ja: {平日|へいじつ}は{忙|いそが}しいですが、{週末|しゅうまつ}**は**{時間|じかん}があります。
examples.romaji: heijitsu wa isogashii desu ga, shuumatsu wa jikan ga arimasu.
examples.en: I'm busy on weekdays, but I have time on weekends.

examples.ja: {東京|とうきょう}には{行|い}ったことがありますが、{大阪|おおさか}に**は**{行|い}ったことがありません。
examples.romaji: toukyou ni wa itta koto ga arimasu ga, oosaka ni wa itta koto ga arimasen.
examples.en: I've been to Tokyo, but I've never been to Osaka.

examples.ja: Contrastive は
examples.romaji: Set one topic against another
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: If or when this happens, then...
goal: You'll be able to describe a result that depends on a condition or follows after it is completed.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Respond when a condition is met
text: ～たら is a flexible way to say if or when. The result follows the condition being met, and can be a plan, request, or suggestion. It can also describe discovering something after an action.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～たら
text: Use 行ったら, 安かったら, 静かだったら, and 雨だったら. Negative verbs use なかったら. The past-shaped form does not make a future condition past.

formation: Plain past form + ら

examples.ja: キャンプ{場|じょう}に{着|つ}い**たら**、テントを{立|た}てましょう。
examples.romaji: kyanpujou ni tsuitara, tento o tatemashou.
examples.en: When we arrive at the campsite, let's pitch the tent.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}に{行|い}っ**たら**、{富士山|ふじさん}に{登|のぼ}りたいです。
examples.romaji: nihon ni ittara, fujisan ni noboritai desu.
examples.en: When I go to Japan, I want to climb Mount Fuji.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}に{着|つ}い**たら**、{電話|でんわ}してください。
examples.romaji: eki ni tsuitara, denwa shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please call when you reach the station.

examples.ja: {安|やす}かっ**たら**、{買|か}います。
examples.romaji: yasukattara, kaimasu.
examples.en: If it is inexpensive, I will buy it.

examples.ja: {店|みせ}に{行|い}っ**たら**、{休|やす}みでした。
examples.romaji: mise ni ittara, yasumi deshita.
examples.en: When I went to the shop, I found it was closed.

examples.ja: {仕事|しごと}が{早|はや}く{終|お}わっ**たら**、{飲|の}みに{行|い}きませんか。
examples.romaji: shigoto ga hayaku owattara, nomi ni ikimasen ka.
examples.en: If work finishes early, would you like to go for a drink?

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っ**たら**、{試合|しあい}は{中止|ちゅうし}です。
examples.romaji: ame ga futtara, shiai wa chuushi desu.
examples.en: If it rains, the match will be canceled.

examples.ja: もし{時間|じかん}があっ**たら**、{手伝|てつだ}ってください。
examples.romaji: moshi jikan ga attara, tetsudatte kudasai.
examples.en: If you have time, please give me a hand.

examples.ja: ～たら
examples.romaji: If or when this happens, then...
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Whenever this happens, that result follows
goal: You'll be able to describe automatic results, repeated consequences, instructions, and natural rules.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe a reliable result
text: Conditional と links a condition to a regular, automatic, or predictable result. It is common for mechanisms, natural changes, habits, and directions.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～と (condition)
text: Do not use this basic conditional for a freely chosen future request or invitation. Use たら for “if it rains, let's…” instead. Nouns and な-adjectives use だと.

formation: Plain nonpast affirmative or negative clause + と + Result

examples.ja: このボタンを{押|お}す**と**、{電気|でんき}がつきます。
examples.romaji: kono botan o osu to, denki ga tsukimasu.
examples.en: When you press this button, the light comes on.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{夜|よる}コーヒーを{飲|の}む**と**、{眠|ねむ}れなくなります。
examples.romaji: watashi wa yoru koohii o nomu to, nemurenaku narimasu.
examples.en: If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep.

examples.ja: {春|はる}になる**と**、{花|はな}が{咲|さ}きます。
examples.romaji: haru ni naru to, hana ga sakimasu.
examples.en: When spring comes, flowers bloom.

examples.ja: {右|みぎ}に{曲|ま}がる**と**、{駅|えき}があります。
examples.romaji: migi ni magaru to, eki ga arimasu.
examples.en: When you turn right, you will find the station.

examples.ja: この{道|みち}をまっすぐ{行|い}く**と**、{左|ひだり}に{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}があります。
examples.romaji: kono michi o massugu iku to, hidari ni yuubinkyoku ga arimasu.
examples.en: If you go straight along this road, you'll find the post office on your left.

examples.ja: {冬|ふゆ}になる**と**、この{山|やま}は{雪|ゆき}で{白|しろ}くなります。
examples.romaji: fuyu ni naru to, kono yama wa yuki de shiroku narimasu.
examples.en: When winter comes, this mountain turns white with snow.

examples.ja: このカードをタッチする**と**、ドアが{開|あ}きます。
examples.romaji: kono kaado o tatchi suru to, doa ga akimasu.
examples.en: When you touch this card, the door opens.

examples.ja: ～と (condition)
examples.romaji: Whenever this happens, that result follows
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: If that is the situation
goal: You'll be able to respond to known information by giving advice, a judgment, or a result for that case.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Give advice based on a premise
text: ～なら takes a proposed or known situation as the basis for a response. It often means “if that is the case” or “if you are talking about that.” The advice can concern something done before the proposed event.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～なら
text: Nouns and な-adjectives normally omit だ before なら. Unlike たら, なら does not require the main action to wait until the premise has happened.

formation: Plain clause / Noun / な-adjective stem + なら

examples.ja: {京都|きょうと}に{行|い}く**なら**、この{お寺|おてら}がおすすめです。
examples.romaji: kyouto ni iku nara, kono otera ga osusume desu.
examples.en: If you are going to Kyoto, I recommend this temple.

examples.ja: パソコンを{買|か}う**なら**、{駅前|えきまえ}の{店|みせ}が{安|やす}いですよ。
examples.romaji: pasokon o kau nara, ekimae no mise ga yasui desu yo.
examples.en: If you're buying a computer, the shop by the station is cheap.

examples.ja: {車|くるま}で{行|い}く**なら**、{早|はや}く{出|で}ましょう。
examples.romaji: kuruma de iku nara, hayaku demashou.
examples.en: If we are going by car, let's leave early.

examples.ja: {静|しず}か**なら**、ここで{勉強|べんきょう}します。
examples.romaji: shizuka nara, koko de benkyou shimasu.
examples.en: If it is quiet, I will study here.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}で{桜|さくら}を{見|み}る**なら**、{四月|しがつ}がいいですよ。
examples.romaji: nihon de sakura o miru nara, shigatsu ga ii desu yo.
examples.en: If you want to see cherry blossoms in Japan, April is a good time.

examples.ja: {寒|さむ}い**なら**、{窓|まど}を{閉|し}めましょうか。
examples.romaji: samui nara, mado o shimemashou ka.
examples.en: If you're cold, shall I close the window?

examples.ja: お{寿司|すし}を{食|た}べる**なら**、あの{店|みせ}がおいしいですよ。
examples.romaji: osushi o taberu nara, ano mise ga oishii desu yo.
examples.en: If you're going to have sushi, that restaurant is good.

examples.ja: ～なら
examples.romaji: If that is the situation
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: If this condition is met
goal: You'll be able to build the ば conditional and connect a condition to its expected result.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Set a condition for a result
text: ～ば highlights a condition under which a result is possible or expected. It is useful for explaining what is needed, as in having enough time or a low enough price.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 1 · Godan
text: For Group 1 verbs, change the final u-row kana to the e-row and add ば.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 2 · Ichidan
text: Remove final る and add れば. The result expresses a condition, not ability.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 3 · Irregular
text: する becomes すれば. 来る becomes 来れば, with the reading くれば.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Adjectives and negative conditions
text: For い-adjectives, replace final い with ければ. The negative ending ない follows the same rule: なければ. Nouns and な-adjectives usually use なら; であれば is a more formal alternative.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ば
text: する becomes すれば and 来る becomes 来れば (くれば). い-adjectives use ければ; negatives use なければ. Nouns and な-adjectives commonly use なら or であれば. With a controllable action by the same subject, requests and intentions in the result may call for たら instead.

formation: Group 2 without final る + れば
い-adjective without い + ければ / Negative without final い + ければ
Group 1 e-row stem + ば / Group 2 without る + れば

examples.ja: {時間|じかん}があれ**ば**、{公園|こうえん}に{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: jikan ga areba, kouen ni ikimasu.
examples.en: If I have time, I will go to the park.

examples.ja: {安|やす}けれ**ば**、{買|か}います。

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}すれ**ば**、{上手|じょうず}になります。
examples.romaji: mainichi renshuu sureba, jouzu ni narimasu.
examples.en: If you practice every day, you will improve.

examples.ja: {分|わ}からなけれ**ば**、{聞|き}いてください。
examples.romaji: wakaranakereba, kiite kudasai.
examples.en: If you do not understand, please ask.

examples.ja: お{金|かね}があれ**ば**、{新|あたら}しいパソコンを{買|か}いたいです。
examples.romaji: okane ga areba, atarashii pasokon o kaitai desu.
examples.en: If I had the money, I'd like to buy a new computer.

examples.ja: このボタンを{押|お}せ**ば**、{駅員|えきいん}さんと{話|はな}せます。
examples.romaji: kono botan o oseba, ekiinsan to hanasemasu.
examples.en: If you press this button, you can talk to a station attendant.

examples.ja: {急|いそ}げ**ば**、{九時|くじ}の{電車|でんしゃ}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}います。
examples.romaji: isogeba, kuji no densha ni maniaimasu.
examples.en: If we hurry, we'll make the nine o'clock train.

examples.ja: ～ば
examples.romaji: If this condition is met
examples.en: Want extra conjugation drills for Conditional -ba Form (ば形) across Group 1 (Godan), Group 2 (Ichidan), and Irregular verbs? Use our Interactive Verb Conjugation Practice Tool or review the 13-Form Japanese Verb Conjugation Chart.

title: In the event that something happens
goal: You'll be able to state what applies in a particular case, especially in rules and formal guidance.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe what to do in a case
text: ～場合は means in the case that a situation occurs. It is common in instructions, procedures, and contingency plans, and sounds more formal than an everyday たら.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～場合(は)
text: Use 雨の場合 and 静かな場合. Keep the situation before 場合 and the applicable response afterward. は may be omitted.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + 場合は / Noun の / な-adjective な + 場合は

examples.ja: {地震|じしん}の**{場合|ばあい}は**、{机|つくえ}の{下|した}に{入|はい}ってください。
examples.romaji: jishin no baai wa, tsukue no shita ni haitte kudasai.
examples.en: In case of an earthquake, please get under the desk.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まった**{場合|ばあい}は**、バスを{使|つか}ってください。
examples.romaji: densha ga tomatta baai wa, basu o tsukatte kudasai.
examples.en: In the event that the trains stop, please use the bus.

examples.ja: {遅|おく}れる**{場合|ばあい}は**、{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.romaji: okureru baai wa, renraku shite kudasai.
examples.en: If you are going to be late, please contact us.

examples.ja: {危険|きけん}な**{場合|ばあい}は**、{入|はい}らないでください。
examples.romaji: kiken na baai wa, hairanaide kudasai.
examples.en: If it is dangerous, please do not enter.

examples.ja: {火事|かじ}の**{場合|ばあい}は**、エレベーターを{使|つか}わないでください。
examples.romaji: kaji no baai wa, erebeetaa o tsukawanaide kudasai.
examples.en: In case of fire, do not use the elevator.

examples.ja: {予約|よやく}をキャンセルする**{場合|ばあい}は**、{前|まえ}の{日|ひ}までに{電話|でんわ}してください。
examples.romaji: yoyaku o kyanseru suru baai wa, mae no hi made ni denwa shite kudasai.
examples.en: In the event that you cancel your reservation, please call by the day before.

examples.ja: {気分|きぶん}が{悪|わる}くなった**{場合|ばあい}は**、すぐ{係|かかり}の{人|ひと}に{言|い}ってください。
examples.romaji: kibun ga waruku natta baai wa, sugu kakari no hito ni itte kudasai.
examples.en: In case you feel unwell, please tell a staff member right away.

examples.ja: ～場合(は)
examples.romaji: In the event that something happens

title: Even if something happens
goal: You'll be able to say that a result stays the same despite a condition that might normally change it.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Keep the result despite a condition
text: ～ても says the result holds even if or even though a condition is true. The condition might normally lead to a different outcome.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ても
text: Negatives use なくても. The condition may be hypothetical or actual. Unlike a simple if-clause, it says the obstacle does not change the result.

formation: Verb て-form + も / い-adjective ～くて + も / Noun or な-adjective + でも

examples.ja: {寒|さむ}く**ても**、{芽衣|めい}は{外|そと}で{元気|げんき}に{遊|あそ}びます。
examples.romaji: samukutemo, mei wa soto de genki ni asobimasu.
examples.en: Even if it is cold, Mei plays energetically outside.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っ**ても**、{試合|しあい}はあります。
examples.romaji: ame ga futte mo, shiai wa arimasu.
examples.en: The match will go ahead even if it rains.

examples.ja: {高|たか}**くても**、この{本|ほん}が{欲|ほ}しいです。
examples.romaji: takakute mo, kono hon ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: Even if it is expensive, I want this book.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}**でも**、{働|はたら}きます。
examples.romaji: nichiyoubi demo, hatarakimasu.
examples.en: I work even on Sundays.

examples.ja: {予約|よやく}し**なくても**、{入|はい}れます。
examples.romaji: yoyaku shinakute mo, hairemasu.
examples.en: You can enter even without a reservation.

examples.ja: {少|すこ}し{高|たか}く**ても**、{駅|えき}に{近|ちか}い{部屋|へや}がいいです。
examples.romaji: sukoshi takakute mo, eki ni chikai heya ga ii desu.
examples.en: Even if it's a little expensive, I'd like an apartment near the station.

examples.ja: {何度|なんど}{聞|き}い**ても**、{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: nando kiite mo, wakarimasen.
examples.en: No matter how many times I ask, I don't understand.

examples.ja: {雪|ゆき}の{日|ひ}**でも**、{父|ちち}は{車|くるま}で{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: yuki no hi demo, chichi wa kuruma de kaisha ni ikimasu.
examples.en: Even on snowy days, my father drives to work.

examples.ja: ～ても
examples.romaji: Even if something happens
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

pattern: ～たらいい・～たらどうですか
title: Ask for or suggest a course of action
goal: You'll be able to ask for guidance with ～たらいい and offer advice or suggestions using ～たらいい and ～たらどうですか.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Offer advice or ask what to do
text: ～たらいい suggests a good course of action. ～たらどうですか offers a suggestion as “how about…?” Questions such as どうしたらいいですか ask for advice.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～たらいい・～たらどうですか
text: The form is conditional, not a report of a past action. ～たらどうですか may sound pointed when repeated or said sharply, so match your tone to the relationship.

formation: Verb た-form + らいい / らどうですか

examples.ja: {少|すこ}し{休|やす}ん**だらどうですか**。
examples.romaji: sukoshi yasundara dou desu ka.
examples.en: How about resting for a while?

examples.ja: {一人|ひとり}で{決|き}めないで、{先生|せんせい}に{相談|そうだん}し**たらどうですか**。
examples.romaji: hitori de kimenaide, sensei ni soudan shitara dou desu ka.
examples.en: Instead of deciding on your own, why not talk it over with your teacher?

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}に{聞|き}い**たらいい**ですよ。
examples.romaji: sensei ni kiitara ii desu yo.
examples.en: You could ask the teacher.

examples.ja: {寒|さむ}いなら、もう{一枚|いちまい}{着|き}**たらどうですか**。
examples.romaji: samui nara, mou ichimai kitara dou desu ka.
examples.en: If you're cold, why don't you put on another layer?

examples.ja: どこで{切符|きっぷ}を{買|か}っ**たらいいですか**。
examples.romaji: doko de kippu o kattara ii desu ka.
examples.en: Where should I buy a ticket?

examples.ja: そんなに{心配|しんぱい}なら、{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}っ**たらどうですか**。
examples.romaji: sonna ni shinpai nara, byouin ni ittara dou desu ka.
examples.en: If you're that worried, why don't you go to the hospital?

examples.ja: {駅|えき}までどうやって{行|い}っ**たらいいですか**。
examples.romaji: eki made dou yatte ittara ii desu ka.
examples.en: How should I get to the station?

examples.ja: {母|はは}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}のプレゼントは、{何|なに}を{買|か}っ**たらいいですか**。
examples.romaji: haha no tanjoubi no purezento wa, nani o kattara ii desu ka.
examples.en: What should I buy my mother for her birthday?

examples.ja: ～たらいい・～たらどうですか
examples.romaji: Ask for or suggest a course of action
examples.en: 5 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Hope that something turns out well
goal: You'll be able to express a hope for yourself or someone else and offer gentle advice.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Express a hope
text: ～といい expresses a wished-for outcome: it would be good if something happened. ね can share a hope with someone, while な can make it feel like a personal wish.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～といい
text: Use a hoped-for state or outcome, often a potential form for personal success. Context may also make といい into advice; here focus on hopes rather than automatic results.

formation: Plain nonpast clause + といい

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}のチームが{試合|しあい}に{勝|か}てる**といい**ですね。
examples.romaji: ren no chiimu ga shiai ni kateru to ii desu ne.
examples.en: I hope Ren's team wins the game.

examples.ja: {早|はや}く{元気|げんき}になる**といい**ですね。
examples.romaji: hayaku genki ni naru to ii desu ne.
examples.en: I hope you get well soon.

examples.ja: {試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}できる**といい**ですね。
examples.romaji: shiken ni goukaku dekiru to ii desu ne.
examples.en: I hope you can pass the exam.

examples.ja: また{会|あ}える**といい**ですね。
examples.romaji: mata aeru to ii desu ne.
examples.en: I hope we can meet again.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}の{日|ひ}、{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}らない**といい**ですね。
examples.romaji: ryokou no hi, ame ga furanai to ii desu ne.
examples.en: I hope it doesn't rain on the day of our trip.

examples.ja: テストでいい{点|てん}が{取|と}れる**といい**ですね。
examples.romaji: tesuto de ii ten ga toreru to ii desu ne.
examples.en: I hope you get a good score on the test.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}は{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れない**といい**な。
examples.romaji: ashita no asa wa densha ga okurenai to ii na.
examples.en: I hope the train isn't late tomorrow morning.

examples.ja: ～といい
examples.romaji: Hope that something turns out well
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Regret that you did not make a better choice
goal: You'll be able to look back and say that a different action would have been better.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Regret a choice in the past
text: ～ばよかった says a different past choice would have been better. A positive form regrets not doing something; a negative form regrets having done it.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ばよかった
text: 持ってくればよかった means “I should have brought it.” 行かなければよかった means “I wish I had not gone.” This is counterfactual regret, not relief about the actual outcome.

formation: Verb ば-form + よかった

examples.ja: もっと{厚|あつ}い{上着|うわぎ}を{着|き}て**くればよかった**です。
examples.romaji: motto atsui uwagi o kite kureba yokatta desu.
examples.en: I should have worn a thicker jacket.

examples.ja: もっと{早|はや}く{家|いえ}を{出|で}れ**ばよかった**。{電車|でんしゃ}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}いませんでした。
examples.romaji: motto hayaku ie o dereba yokatta. densha ni maniaimasen deshita.
examples.en: I should have left home earlier. I missed the train.

examples.ja: もっと{勉強|べんきょう}すれ**ばよかった**です。
examples.romaji: motto benkyou sureba yokatta desu.
examples.en: I should have studied more.

examples.ja: あの{店|みせ}に{行|い}かなけれ**ばよかった**です。
examples.romaji: ano mise ni ikanakereba yokatta desu.
examples.en: I wish I had not gone to that shop.

examples.ja: あの{店|みせ}で{買|か}え**ばよかった**です。ここは{高|たか}いですね。
examples.romaji: ano mise de kaeba yokatta desu. koko wa takai desu ne.
examples.en: I should have bought it at that other shop. It's expensive here, isn't it?

examples.ja: こんなに{混|こ}むなら、{予約|よやく}すれ**ばよかった**。
examples.romaji: konna ni komu nara, yoyaku sureba yokatta.
examples.en: If it was going to be this crowded, I should have made a reservation.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}、あんなに{食|た}べなけれ**ばよかった**。おなかが{痛|いた}いです。
examples.romaji: kinou, anna ni tabenakereba yokatta. onaka ga itai desu.
examples.en: I wish I hadn't eaten so much yesterday. My stomach hurts.

examples.ja: ～ばよかった
examples.romaji: Regret that you did not make a better choice
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Feel glad that something happened
goal: You'll be able to express relief or happiness about an action, decision, or result.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Feel glad about what happened
text: ～てよかった expresses relief or satisfaction about an actual outcome. It means being glad something happened or glad something did not happen.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てよかった
text: Use 行ってよかった for being glad you went. Use 忘れなくてよかった for being glad you did not forget. Unlike ～ばよかった, it approves the real outcome rather than wishing for a different one.

formation: Verb て-form / negative ～なくて + よかった

examples.ja: {温|あたた}かい{上着|うわぎ}を{持|も}って**きてよかった**です。
examples.romaji: atatakai uwagi o mottekite yokatta desu.
examples.en: I'm glad I brought a warm jacket.

examples.ja: {財布|さいふ}が{見|み}つかっ**てよかった**ですね。
examples.romaji: saifu ga mitsukatte yokatta desu ne.
examples.en: I'm glad your wallet turned up.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}に{来|き}**てよかった**です。
examples.romaji: kono machi ni kite yokatta desu.
examples.en: I am glad I came to this town.

examples.ja: {遅|おく}れ**なくてよかった**です。
examples.romaji: okurenakute yokatta desu.
examples.en: I am glad I was not late.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}を{持|も}ってき**てよかった**です。
examples.romaji: てよかった
examples.en: The umbrella was brought, and that was good.

examples.ja: {傘|かさ}を{持|も}ってくれ**ばよかった**です。
examples.romaji: ばよかった
examples.en: It was not brought, and the speaker regrets that.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し**てよかった**です。
examples.romaji: kono machi ni hikkoshite yokatta desu.
examples.en: I'm glad I moved to this town.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る{前|まえ}に{家|いえ}に{着|つ}い**てよかった**。
examples.romaji: ame ga furu mae ni ie ni tsuite yokatta.
examples.en: I'm glad I got home before it rained.

examples.ja: {大|おお}きなけがじゃなく**てよかった**ですね。
examples.romaji: ookina kega ja nakute yokatta desu ne.
examples.en: I'm glad it wasn't a serious injury.

examples.ja: ～てよかった
examples.romaji: Feel glad that something happened
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Offer one example without ruling out others
goal: You'll be able to propose an option lightly, leaving the listener free to choose something else.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Offer one possible option
text: Noun + でも can offer an example without insisting on that exact choice. It often sounds like “tea or something” in a relaxed invitation.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～でも (suggestion)
text: Use it with an invitation or proposal. The named item is a representative option; this differs from conditional でも meaning “even if” and question-word でも meaning “any.” でも replaces を or が, but other particles stay in place: a destination keeps に, as in 公園にでも行きましょう。

formation: Noun (+ particle) + でも + Suggestion

examples.ja: {お茶|おちゃ}**でも**{飲|の}みませんか。
examples.romaji: ocha demo nomimasen ka.
examples.en: Would you like some tea or something?

examples.ja: {今度|こんど}、{一緒|いっしょ}に{食事|しょくじ}**でも**しませんか。
examples.romaji: kondo, issho ni shokuji demo shimasen ka.
examples.en: Would you like to have a meal or something together sometime?

examples.ja: {公園|こうえん}に**でも**{行|い}きましょう。
examples.romaji: kouen ni demo ikimashou.
examples.en: Let's go to the park or somewhere.

examples.ja: {映画|えいが}**でも**{見|み}ませんか。
examples.romaji: eiga demo mimasen ka.
examples.en: Would you like to watch a movie or something?

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れましたね。コーヒー**でも**{飲|の}みませんか。
examples.romaji: tsukaremashita ne. koohii demo nomimasen ka.
examples.en: That was tiring, wasn't it? How about a coffee or something?

examples.ja: {週末|しゅうまつ}、{買|か}い{物|もの}に**でも**{行|い}きませんか。
examples.romaji: shuumatsu, kaimono ni demo ikimasen ka.
examples.en: How about going shopping or something this weekend?

examples.ja: {暇|ひま}なら、{本|ほん}**でも**{読|よ}んだらどうですか。
examples.romaji: hima nara, hon demo yondara dou desu ka.
examples.en: If you're bored, why not read a book or something?

examples.ja: ～でも (suggestion)
examples.romaji: Offer one example without ruling out others
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

pattern: ～必要があります・～が必要です
title: State plainly what is required
goal: You'll be able to say that an action or item is necessary in a neutral tone, without the pressure of must-forms.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: State what is necessary
text: Verb dictionary form + 必要があります says an action is needed. Noun + が必要です identifies a required thing. The pattern describes necessity rather than merely a personal wish.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Express necessary actions with ～必要があります
text: Place the verb in its dictionary form directly before 必要があります—do not add の. Even in polite speech, the verb before 必要 stays in plain form.
To say an action is not necessary, change the end to 必要はありません. This means “there is no need to do it,” not that the action is forbidden.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Express required items with ～が必要です
text: To state that a thing or person is required, mark the noun with が before 必要です. To state the purpose or occasion the item is needed for, mark it with には (such as 旅行には).
When something is not needed, mark the noun with は and say 必要ありません or 必要ではありません. You can also use 必要はありません for emphasis.

formation: Verb dictionary form + 必要があります
Noun + が必要です

examples.ja: {早|はや}く{出|で}る**{必要|ひつよう}があります**。
examples.romaji: hayaku deru hitsuyou ga arimasu.
examples.en: We need to leave early.

examples.ja: この{病院|びょういん}は{予約|よやく}**が{必要|ひつよう}**です。
examples.romaji: kono byouin wa yoyaku ga hitsuyou desu.
examples.en: This hospital requires an appointment.

examples.ja: {予約|よやく}する**{必要|ひつよう}があります**。
examples.romaji: yoyaku suru hitsuyou ga arimasu.
examples.en: You need to make a reservation.

examples.ja: {急|いそ}ぐ**{必要|ひつよう}はありません**。
examples.romaji: isogu hitsuyou wa arimasen.
examples.en: There is no need to hurry.

examples.ja: {靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ**{必要|ひつよう}があります**。
examples.romaji: kutsu o nugu hitsuyou ga arimasu.
examples.en: You need to take off your shoes.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}までに{書類|しょるい}を{出|だ}す**{必要|ひつよう}があります**。
examples.romaji: ashita made ni shorui o dasu hitsuyou ga arimasu.
examples.en: You need to submit the documents by tomorrow.

examples.ja: {全部|ぜんぶ}{覚|おぼ}える**{必要|ひつよう}はありません**。
examples.romaji: zenbu oboeru hitsuyou wa arimasen.
examples.en: You don't need to memorize everything.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}には{お金|おかね}**が{必要|ひつよう}です**。
examples.romaji: ryokou ni wa okane ga hitsuyou desu.
examples.en: Money is needed for the trip.

examples.ja: パスポートは**{必要|ひつよう}ありません**。
examples.romaji: pasupooto wa hitsuyou arimasen.
examples.en: A passport is not needed.

examples.ja: ここでは{車|くるま}**が{必要|ひつよう}です**。
examples.romaji: koko de wa kuruma ga hitsuyou desu.
examples.en: A car is needed here.

examples.ja: ビザ**が{必要|ひつよう}です**。
examples.romaji: biza ga hitsuyou desu.
examples.en: A visa is required.

examples.ja: {予約|よやく}は**{必要|ひつよう}ありません**。
examples.romaji: yoyaku wa hitsuyou arimasen.
examples.en: A reservation is not needed.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}で{働|はたら}く{場合|ばあい}は、ビザを{取|と}る**{必要|ひつよう}があります**。
examples.romaji: nihon de hataraku baai wa, biza o toru hitsuyou ga arimasu.
examples.en: If you're going to work in Japan, you need to get a visa.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{五時|ごじ}に{起|お}きる**{必要|ひつよう}があります**。
examples.romaji: ashita wa goji ni okiru hitsuyou ga arimasu.
examples.en: I need to get up at five tomorrow.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}には{出|で}る**{必要|ひつよう}はありません**。メールで{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
examples.romaji: kaigi ni wa deru hitsuyou wa arimasen. meeru de daijoubu desu.
examples.en: You don't need to attend the meeting. Email is fine.

examples.ja: ～必要があります・～が必要です
examples.romaji: State plainly what is required
