title: Connect a situation directly to its cause
goal: You'll be able to explain simple causes involving verbs, adjectives, nouns, and negative forms.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Connect a cause with a natural result
text: The て connective can give a reason for a feeling, difficulty, or other natural result. The cause is integrated into the sentence rather than presented as a strong argument.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～て・～くて・～で・～なくて (reason)
text: Use the connective appropriate to the word class. A main-clause command, request, or deliberate proposal usually needs から or ので instead of this causal て.

formation: Cause clause + て / くて / で / なくて + Result

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{疲|つか}れ**て**、{歩|ある}けません。
examples.romaji: mei wa tsukarete, arukemasen.
examples.en: Mei is tired and cannot walk.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}の{階段|かいだん}が{多|おお}**くて**、{疲|つか}れました。
examples.romaji: eki no kaidan ga ookute, tsukaremashita.
examples.en: There were so many stairs at the station that I got tired.

examples.ja: {事故|じこ}があっ**て**、{遅|おく}れました。
examples.romaji: jiko ga atte, okuremashita.
examples.en: There was an accident, so I was late.

examples.ja: {暑|あつ}**くて**、{眠|ねむ}れません。
examples.romaji: atsukute, nemuremasen.
examples.en: It is hot, so I cannot sleep.

examples.ja: {道|みち}が{複雑|ふくざつ}**で**、{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: michi ga fukuzatsu de, wakarimasen.
examples.en: The route is complicated, so I do not understand it.

examples.ja: バスが{来|こ}**なくて**、{困|こま}っています。
examples.romaji: basu ga konakute, komatte imasu.
examples.en: The bus has not come, and I am having trouble.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{熱|ねつ}があっ**て**、{何|なに}も{食|た}べられませんでした。
examples.romaji: kinou wa netsu ga atte, nani mo taberaremasen deshita.
examples.en: I had a fever yesterday and couldn't eat anything.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{寒|さむ}**くて**、{外|そと}に{出|で}たくありません。
examples.romaji: kyou wa samukute, soto ni detaku arimasen.
examples.en: It's so cold today that I don't want to go outside.

examples.ja: {電話|でんわ}がつながら**なくて**、{困|こま}りました。
examples.romaji: denwa ga tsunagaranakute, komarimashita.
examples.en: I couldn't get through on the phone, and I didn't know what to do.

examples.ja: ～て・～くて・～で・～なくて (reason)
examples.romaji: Connect a situation directly to its cause
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Give several supporting reasons or qualities
goal: You'll be able to list reasons or features while suggesting that more could be added.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Offer reasons without claiming a complete list
text: ～し lists reasons or qualities supporting a judgment. Even a single し may imply there are other reasons as well.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～し
text: Nouns and な-adjectives retain だ: 便利だし. Polite ですし and ますし are also possible. It is useful for accumulating support rather than naming one exclusive cause.

formation: Plain predicate + し

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}い**し**、おいしいです。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa yasui shi, oishii desu.
examples.en: This shop is inexpensive, and the food is delicious too.

examples.ja: {時間|じかん}もない**し**、タクシーで{行|い}きましょう。
examples.romaji: jikan mo nai shi, takushii de ikimashou.
examples.en: We don't have much time either, so let's take a taxi.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}に{近|ちか}い**し**、{便利|べんり}です。
examples.romaji: eki ni chikai shi, benri desu.
examples.en: It is near the station, and it is convenient.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}だ**し**、{家|いえ}にいましょう。
examples.romaji: ame da shi, ie ni imashou.
examples.en: It is raining, among other things, so let's stay home.

examples.ja: このアパートは{駅|えき}に{近|ちか}い**し**、{家賃|やちん}も{安|やす}いです。
examples.romaji: kono apaato wa eki ni chikai shi, yachin mo yasui desu.
examples.en: This apartment is close to the station, and the rent is cheap too.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{料理|りょうり}もおいしい**し**、{店員|てんいん}さんも{親切|しんせつ}です。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa ryouri mo oishii shi, ten'insan mo shinsetsu desu.
examples.en: The food at this restaurant is good, and the staff are kind too.

examples.ja: {彼|かれ}は{頭|あたま}もいい**し**、スポーツも{上手|じょうず}です。
examples.romaji: kare wa atama mo ii shi, supootsu mo jouzu desu.
examples.en: He's smart, and he's good at sports too.

examples.ja: ～し
examples.romaji: Give several supporting reasons or qualities
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Add another supporting point
goal: You'll be able to connect sentences by adding a related reason, fact, or advantage.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Add another supporting point
text: それに introduces an additional related fact. It often adds another reason for the same conclusion, like “besides” or “on top of that.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use それに
text: Use it between complete statements. B adds information; it is not necessarily caused by A. For a consequence, use それで.

formation: Statement A + それに + Additional statement B

examples.ja: この{部屋|へや}は{広|ひろ}いです。**それに**、{明|あか}るいです。
examples.romaji: kono heya wa hiroi desu. sore ni, akarui desu.
examples.en: This room is spacious. Besides, it is bright.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{雨|あめ}です。**それに**、{風|かぜ}も{強|つよ}いです。
examples.romaji: kyou wa ame desu. soreni, kaze mo tsuyoi desu.
examples.en: It's raining today. Besides that, the wind is strong too.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}は{面白|おもしろ}いです。**それに**、{安|やす}いです。
examples.romaji: kono hon wa omoshiroi desu. sore ni, yasui desu.
examples.en: This book is interesting. It is inexpensive too.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}は{近|ちか}いです。**それに**、バス{停|てい}もあります。
examples.romaji: eki wa chikai desu. sore ni, basutei mo arimasu.
examples.en: The station is nearby. There is also a bus stop.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}いです。**それに**、{店員|てんいん}さんも{親切|しんせつ}です。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa yasui desu. soreni, ten'insan mo shinsetsu desu.
examples.en: This shop is cheap. On top of that, the staff are kind.

examples.ja: このスマホは{軽|かる}いです。**それに**、{写真|しゃしん}もきれいに{撮|と}れます。
examples.romaji: kono sumaho wa karui desu. soreni, shashin mo kirei ni toremasu.
examples.en: This smartphone is light. On top of that, it takes nice photos.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんは{英語|えいご}が{話|はな}せます。**それに**、{中国語|ちゅうごくご}もできます。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san wa eigo ga hanasemasu. soreni, chuugokugo mo dekimasu.
examples.en: Tanaka-san can speak English. On top of that, she can speak Chinese too.

examples.ja: それに
examples.romaji: Add another supporting point
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Show the result of what was just said
goal: You'll be able to connect a cause or background situation to the result that followed.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Explain the resulting situation
text: それで connects a cause or background fact to its consequence. It can mean “so” or “that is why.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use それで
text: Use it to explain what resulted, not merely the next event in time. A new invitation or command based on a reason often uses だから instead.

formation: Cause + それで + Result

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まりました。**それで**、{遅|おく}れました。
examples.romaji: densha ga tomarimashita. sore de, okuremashita.
examples.en: The train stopped. That is why I was late.

examples.ja: {財布|さいふ}を{忘|わす}れました。**それで**、{昼|ひる}ご{飯|はん}が{買|か}えませんでした。
examples.romaji: saifu o wasuremashita. sorede, hirugohan ga kaemasen deshita.
examples.en: I forgot my wallet. That's why I couldn't buy lunch.

examples.ja: {道|みち}が{混|こ}んでいました。**それで**、バスが{遅|おく}れました。
examples.romaji: michi ga konde imashita. sore de, basu ga okuremashita.
examples.en: The road was congested. As a result, the bus was late.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{眠|ねむ}れませんでした。**それで**、{今日|きょう}は{眠|ねむ}いです。
examples.romaji: kinou wa nemuremasen deshita. sore de, kyou wa nemui desu.
examples.en: I could not sleep yesterday. That is why I am sleepy today.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}は{雪|ゆき}がたくさん{降|ふ}りました。**それで**、{学校|がっこう}が{休|やす}みになりました。
examples.romaji: kinou wa yuki ga takusan furimashita. sorede, gakkou ga yasumi ni narimashita.
examples.en: It snowed a lot yesterday. That's why school was canceled.

examples.ja: {今朝|けさ}{寝坊|ねぼう}をしました。**それで**、{会議|かいぎ}に{遅|おく}れました。
examples.romaji: kesa nebou o shimashita. sorede, kaigi ni okuremashita.
examples.en: I overslept this morning. That's why I was late for the meeting.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}のアニメが{好|す}きです。**それで**、{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}し{始|はじ}めました。
examples.romaji: nihon no anime ga suki desu. sorede, nihongo o benkyou shihajimemashita.
examples.en: I love Japanese anime. That's why I started studying Japanese.

examples.ja: それで
examples.romaji: Show the result of what was just said
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: A result happens because of a particular cause
goal: You'll be able to give a neutral or formal cause for an event or situation.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Give a formal cause
text: Causal ～ため or ～ために gives an objective-sounding reason, often in reports or notices. It frequently explains delays, cancellations, or difficulties.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ため・～ために (cause)
text: Use 雨のため and 危険なため. に is optional in many causal statements. Distinguish a cause already explaining the result from purpose ために, which names a goal.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + ため / Noun の / な-adjective な + ため

examples.ja: {大雪|おおゆき}の**ため**、{電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れています。
examples.romaji: ooyuki no tame, densha ga okurete imasu.
examples.en: The train is delayed because of heavy snow.

examples.ja: {台風|たいふう}の**ため**、{今日|きょう}は{飛行機|ひこうき}が{飛|と}びません。
examples.romaji: taifuu no tame, kyou wa hikouki ga tobimasen.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, planes aren't flying today.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}が{遅|おく}れた**ため**、{間|ま}に{合|あ}いませんでした。
examples.romaji: densha ga okureta tame, maniaimasen deshita.
examples.en: Because the train was delayed, I did not arrive in time.

examples.ja: {道|みち}が{危険|きけん}な**ため**、{通|とお}れません。
examples.romaji: michi ga kiken na tame, tooremasen.
examples.en: Because the road is dangerous, we cannot pass.

examples.ja: {工事|こうじ}の**ため**、この{道|みち}は{通|とお}れません。
examples.romaji: kouji no tame, kono michi wa tooremasen.
examples.en: This road is closed due to construction.

examples.ja: {事故|じこ}の**ため**、バスが{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}{遅|おく}れました。
examples.romaji: jiko no tame, basu ga sanjuppun okuremashita.
examples.en: The bus was thirty minutes late because of an accident.

examples.ja: {病気|びょうき}の**ため**、{田中|たなか}さんは{今日|きょう}{休|やす}みです。
examples.romaji: byouki no tame, tanaka-san wa kyou yasumi desu.
examples.en: Tanaka-san is off today due to illness.

examples.ja: ～ため・～ために (cause)
examples.romaji: A result happens because of a particular cause
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: The result goes against what you expected
goal: You'll be able to contrast a fact with a surprising, disappointing, or frustrating result.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Point out a surprising contradiction
text: ～のに connects a fact with an unexpected result. It often conveys disappointment or surprise because reality conflicts with what the first clause would suggest.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～のに (although)
text: Nouns and な-adjectives need な before のに. This use normally connects actual situations, not an imagined “even if.” Purpose のに is a separate pattern.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + のに / Noun or な-adjective + なのに

examples.ja: たくさん{練習|れんしゅう}した**のに**、{試合|しあい}に{負|ま}けてしまいました。
examples.romaji: takusan renshuu shita noni, shiai ni makete shimaimashita.
examples.en: Even though we practiced so hard, we lost the match.

examples.ja: {約束|やくそく}した**のに**、{友|とも}だちは{来|き}ませんでした。
examples.romaji: yakusoku shita noni, tomodachi wa kimasen deshita.
examples.en: We'd made a promise, and yet my friend didn't come.

examples.ja: たくさん{寝|ね}た**のに**、まだ{眠|ねむ}いです。
examples.romaji: takusan neta noni, mada nemui desu.
examples.en: Although I slept a lot, I am still sleepy.

examples.ja: {日曜日|にちようび}**なのに**、{仕事|しごと}があります。
examples.romaji: nichiyoubi na noni, shigoto ga arimasu.
examples.en: Even though it is Sunday, I have work.

examples.ja: {一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}{勉強|べんきょう}した**のに**、{試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちてしまいました。
examples.romaji: isshoukenmei benkyou shita noni, shiken ni ochite shimaimashita.
examples.en: I studied so hard, and yet I failed the exam.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}**なのに**、{朝|あさ}{六時|ろくじ}に{起|お}きてしまいました。
examples.romaji: yasumi no hi na noni, asa rokuji ni okite shimaimashita.
examples.en: Even though it was my day off, I ended up waking up at six.

examples.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだ**のに**、まだ{頭|あたま}が{痛|いた}いです。
examples.romaji: kusuri o nonda noni, mada atama ga itai desu.
examples.en: I took some medicine, and yet my head still hurts.

examples.ja: ～のに (although)
examples.romaji: The result goes against what you expected
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: The result remains true despite that
goal: You'll be able to continue with a contrasting fact that holds even after the previous information.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Continue despite the preceding fact
text: それでも means even so or nevertheless. It acknowledges an obstacle or contrary fact and then gives an outcome that still holds.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use それでも
text: Unlike それで, it does not present the second statement as the expected consequence. It can connect complete sentences and is useful for persistence or unexpected choices.

formation: Obstacle or contrary fact + それでも + Outcome

examples.ja: {外|そと}はとても{寒|さむ}いです。**それでも**、{子供|こども}たちは{公園|こうえん}へ{行|い}きます。
examples.romaji: soto wa totemo samui desu. soredemo, kodomotachi wa kouen e ikimasu.
examples.en: It is very cold outside. Even so, the children go to the park.

examples.ja: {祖父|そふ}は{足|あし}が{悪|わる}いです。**それでも**、{毎朝|まいあさ}{散歩|さんぽ}をします。
examples.romaji: sofu wa ashi ga warui desu. soredemo, maiasa sanpo o shimasu.
examples.en: My grandfather has bad legs. Even so, he goes for a walk every morning.

examples.ja: {難|むずか}しいです。**それでも**、やってみます。
examples.romaji: muzukashii desu. sore demo, yatte mimasu.
examples.en: It is difficult. Even so, I will try.

examples.ja: {遠|とお}いです。**それでも**、{行|い}きたいです。
examples.romaji: tooi desu. sore demo, ikitai desu.
examples.en: It is far away. Even so, I want to go.

examples.ja: {外|そと}は{雨|あめ}です。**それでも**、{子|こ}どもたちは{遊|あそ}びに{行|い}きました。
examples.romaji: soto wa ame desu. soredemo, kodomotachi wa asobi ni ikimashita.
examples.en: It's raining outside. Even so, the children went out to play.

examples.ja: この{仕事|しごと}は{大変|たいへん}です。**それでも**、{私|わたし}はこの{仕事|しごと}が{好|す}きです。
examples.romaji: kono shigoto wa taihen desu. soredemo, watashi wa kono shigoto ga suki desu.
examples.en: This job is hard. Even so, I like it.

examples.ja: {何度|なんど}も{失敗|しっぱい}しました。**それでも**、もう{一度|いちど}やってみます。
examples.romaji: nando mo shippai shimashita. soredemo, mou ichido yatte mimasu.
examples.en: I've failed many times. Even so, I'll try once more.

examples.ja: それでも
examples.romaji: The result remains true despite that
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Do something in order to reach a goal
goal: You'll be able to explain the intended purpose behind a deliberate action.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Act toward a deliberate goal
text: Purpose ～ために links an intentional goal to the action taken to achieve it. It answers what the action is for.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ために (purpose)
text: The goal is usually something the actor can deliberately do. For a desired ability or prevention of an unintended event, ように is often more natural. Noun + のために can also name a beneficiary.

formation: Verb dictionary form + ために / Noun + のために

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{旅行|りょこう}する**ために**{お金|おかね}を{貯|た}めています。
examples.romaji: chichi wa ryokou suru tame ni okane o tamete imasu.
examples.en: My father is saving money to travel.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しいパソコンを{買|か}う**ために**、アルバイトをしています。
examples.romaji: atarashii pasokon o kau tame ni, arubaito o shite imasu.
examples.en: I'm working part-time to buy a new computer.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}で{働|はたら}く**ために**{日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
examples.romaji: nihon de hataraku tame ni nihongo o benkyou shite imasu.
examples.en: I am studying Japanese to work in Japan.

examples.ja: {家族|かぞく}の**ために**{料理|りょうり}します。
examples.romaji: kazoku no tame ni ryouri shimasu.
examples.en: I cook for my family.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{大学|だいがく}に{入|はい}る**ために**、{毎日|まいにち}{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
examples.romaji: nihon no daigaku ni hairu tame ni, mainichi benkyou shite imasu.
examples.en: I'm studying every day so that I can get into a Japanese university.

examples.ja: {健康|けんこう}の**ために**、{毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}っています。
examples.romaji: kenkou no tame ni, maiasa hashitte imasu.
examples.en: I run every morning for my health.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}の{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}る**ために**、いいカメラを{買|か}いました。
examples.romaji: ryokou no shashin o toru tame ni, ii kamera o kaimashita.
examples.en: I bought a good camera to take photos on my trip.

examples.ja: ～ために (purpose)
examples.romaji: Do something in order to reach a goal
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Act so that a desired situation becomes possible
goal: You'll be able to express goals involving ability, change, or outcomes you cannot control directly.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Aim for a desired state
text: Goal ～ように names a state you want to achieve or an unwanted event you want to prevent. The main action is an effort to make that outcome possible.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ように (goal)
text: Potential and negative clauses are common: 読めるように, 忘れないように. The goal can have a different subject from the effort. This is not similarity ように meaning “like.”

formation: Dictionary, potential, or negative verb + ように + Purposeful action

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}に{聞|き}こえる**ように**、{蓮|れん}は{大|おお}きな{声|こえ}で{話|はな}します。
examples.romaji: mei ni kikoeru you ni, ren wa ookina koe de hanashimasu.
examples.en: Ren speaks loudly so that Mei can hear.

examples.ja: {電車|でんしゃ}に{遅|おく}れない**ように**、{少|すこ}し{早|はや}く{家|いえ}を{出|で}ます。
examples.romaji: densha ni okurenai you ni, sukoshi hayaku ie o demasu.
examples.en: I leave home a little early so that I don't miss the train.

examples.ja: {忘|わす}れない**ように**、メモをします。
examples.romaji: wasurenai you ni, memo o shimasu.
examples.en: I make a note so that I will not forget.

examples.ja: {漢字|かんじ}が{読|よ}める**ように**、{練習|れんしゅう}します。
examples.romaji: kanji ga yomeru you ni, renshuu shimasu.
examples.en: I practice so that I can read kanji.

examples.ja: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}み{忘|わす}れない**ように**、テーブルの{上|うえ}に{置|お}いておきます。
examples.romaji: kusuri o nomiwasurenai you ni, teeburu no ue ni oite okimasu.
examples.en: I keep my medicine on the table so that I don't forget to take it.

examples.ja: {後|うし}ろの{人|ひと}にも{聞|き}こえる**ように**、{大|おお}きい{声|こえ}で{話|はな}してください。
examples.romaji: ushiro no hito ni mo kikoeru you ni, ookii koe de hanashite kudasai.
examples.en: Please speak loudly so that the people at the back can hear too.

examples.ja: {風邪|かぜ}をひかない**ように**、{暖|あたた}かい{服|ふく}を{着|き}てください。
examples.romaji: kaze o hikanai you ni, atatakai fuku o kite kudasai.
examples.en: Wear warm clothes so that you don't catch a cold.

examples.ja: ～ように (goal)
examples.romaji: Act so that a desired situation becomes possible
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: For doing or useful for doing
goal: You'll be able to explain what an object is used for or what is needed to perform an action.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Evaluate something for an activity
text: This のに connects an activity to a judgment about the tool, resource, cost, or time it needs. It often translates as “for doing” rather than “although.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～のに (for doing)
text: Use it with 便利, 必要, 使う, or かかる. It is not a general replacement for every “in order to” clause. This の nominalizes the activity and に relates it to the evaluation.

formation: Verb dictionary form + のに + Usefulness, necessity, cost, or time predicate

examples.ja: このはさみは{紙|かみ}を{切|き}る**のに**{便利|べんり}です。
examples.romaji: kono hasami wa kami o kiru noni benri desu.
examples.en: These scissors are useful for cutting paper.

examples.ja: この{辞書|じしょ}は{漢字|かんじ}を{調|しら}べる**のに**{役|やく}に{立|た}ちます。
examples.romaji: kono jisho wa kanji o shiraberu noni yaku ni tachimasu.
examples.en: This dictionary is useful for looking up kanji.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}する**のに**{お金|おかね}が{必要|ひつよう}です。
examples.romaji: ryokou suru noni okane ga hitsuyou desu.
examples.en: Money is needed for traveling.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む**のに**{二時間|にじかん}かかりました。
examples.romaji: kono hon o yomu noni nijikan kakarimashita.
examples.en: It took two hours to read this book.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む**のに**{二時間|にじかん}かかりました。

examples.romaji: 読んだのに — , although

title: It looks or seems likely based on what you see
goal: You'll be able to describe an appearance or predict an event from visible signs.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Judge from signs you can observe
text: Use ～そうです when what you observe suggests a quality or a likely event. Dark clouds can prompt 雨が降りそうです even before the first drops fall.

With an adjective, you judge a quality without directly confirming it: a cake looks delicious before you taste it. With a verb, you judge that an event seems likely, often that it is about to happen. ～そうです is the polite ending.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Attach そう to an adjective stem
text: For an い-adjective, remove the final い: おいしい → おいしそう. For a な-adjective, attach そう to the stem without な or だ: 元気 → 元気そう.
This pattern expresses an impression. Do not attach it directly to a noun to say someone “looks like a student”; that requires a different pattern, such as ～のようだ.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Attach そう to a verb's ます-stem
text: Start from the polite ます form and remove ます: 降ります → 降りそう; 落ちます → 落ちそう. Use present signs to judge what is likely to happen. An event that is already happening normally needs a direct description instead.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Handle いい and negative impressions
text: いい becomes よさそう. The adjective ない becomes なさそう, including adjective negatives such as おいしくない → おいしくなさそう.
For a verb that seems unlikely to happen, use the ます-stem + そうにない. Its polite form is そうにありません. This gives 降りそうにありません, “does not look likely to rain.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Use そうな before a noun and そうに before an action
text: A phrase ending in this appearance そう behaves like a な-adjective. Use そうな to describe a noun and そうに to describe how someone acts.

formation: い-adjective without final い / な-adjective stem + そうです
Verb ます-stem + そうです
いい / adjective ending in ない → よさそう / ～なさそう ; Verb ます-stem + そうにありません
Appearance phrase ending in そう + な + Noun / に + Verb

examples.ja: {荷物|にもつ}が{棚|たな}から{落|お}ち**そうです**。

examples.ja: このケーキはおいし**そうです**。

examples.ja: おじいちゃんは{元気|げんき}**そうです**。

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り**そうです**。

examples.ja: コップが{落|お}ち**そうです**。

examples.en: This problem looks difficult, but I'll give it a try.

title: Report information you heard elsewhere
goal: You'll be able to pass on information from another person or source without claiming it as your own observation.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Pass on information from a source
text: Hearsay ～そうです reports information learned from someone or something else. It does not directly judge how something looks. A source such as a forecast may be stated with ～によると.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～そうです (hearsay)
text: Keep the full plain form: 降るそうです, おいしいそうです, 元気だそうです. Tense and negation stay inside the reported clause. Unlike appearance そう, do not remove adjective い or use a verb stem.

formation: Complete plain clause + そうです

examples.ja: ニュースによると、{山|やま}に{雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}った**そうです**。
examples.romaji: nyuusu ni yoru to, yama ni yuki ga futta sou desu.
examples.en: According to the news, snow has fallen on the mountains.

examples.ja: {天気|てんき}{予報|よほう}によると、{明日|あした}は{雪|ゆき}だ**そうです**。
examples.romaji: tenki yohou ni yoru to, ashita wa yuki da sou desu.
examples.en: According to the weather forecast, it's going to snow tomorrow.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}はおいしい**そうです**。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa oishii sou desu.
examples.en: I hear the food at this shop is delicious.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{今日|きょう}{来|こ}ない**そうです**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa kyou konai sou desu.
examples.en: I hear the teacher is not coming today.

examples.ja: ニュースによると、{来月|らいげつ}からこの{道|みち}で{工事|こうじ}がある**そうです**。
examples.romaji: nyuusu ni yoru to, raigetsu kara kono michi de kouji ga aru sou desu.
examples.en: According to the news, there will be construction on this road from next month.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんの{話|はなし}では、{来週|らいしゅう}の{会議|かいぎ}は{中止|ちゅうし}だ**そうです**。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san no hanashi de wa, raishuu no kaigi wa chuushi da sou desu.
examples.en: According to Tanaka-san, next week's meeting is canceled.

examples.en: According to the teacher, tomorrow's test will be easy.

title: It appears so from the available clues
goal: You'll be able to make a careful judgment based on what you see, hear, or know.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Infer a situation from evidence
text: ～ようです presents a judgment based on clues. The speaker reasons from what is observed, rather than simply quoting a report or directly asserting certainty.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ようです (inference)
text: Use 休みのようです and 静かなようです. Evidence may be a combination of signs, not only visual appearance. The ending marks an inference whose truth is not fully confirmed.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + ようです / Noun の / な-adjective な + ようです

examples.ja: {店|みせ}は{休|やす}みの**ようです**。
examples.romaji: mise wa yasumi no you desu.
examples.en: It seems the shop is closed today.

examples.ja: {隣|となり}の{家|いえ}は{電気|でんき}がついていません。{留守|るす}の**ようです**。
examples.romaji: tonari no ie wa denki ga tsuite imasen. rusu no you desu.
examples.en: The lights next door aren't on. It seems they're out.

examples.ja: {誰|だれ}もいない**ようです**。
examples.romaji: daremo inai you desu.
examples.en: It seems nobody is there.

examples.ja: この{問題|もんだい}は{難|むずか}しい**ようです**。
examples.romaji: kono mondai wa muzukashii you desu.

examples.en: I can hear music outside. There seems to be a festival nearby.

examples.ja: {部長|ぶちょう}の{席|せき}にだれもいません。{今日|きょう}は{出張|しゅっちょう}の**ようです**。

examples.en: There's nobody at the manager's desk. It seems the manager is away on business today.

examples.romaji: kono hako wa totemo omoi desu. nakami wa hon no you desu.

title: A casual way to say it seems or looks like
goal: You'll be able to share an informal impression, guess, or comparison in everyday conversation.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Make a conversational inference or resemblance
text: ～みたいです is a conversational way to say something seems a certain way or resembles something. It often overlaps with ようだ but sounds less formal.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～みたいです
text: Nouns and な-adjectives attach directly: 休みみたい. Use みたいな before a noun and みたいに before an action. Do not confuse this with 見たい, “want to see.”

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective / Noun / な-adjective stem + みたいです

examples.ja: あの{雲|くも}は{犬|いぬ}**みたいです**。
examples.romaji: ano kumo wa inu mitai desu.
examples.en: That cloud looks like a dog.

examples.ja: だれか{来|き}た**みたい**。{今|いま}、ドアの{音|おと}がしたよ。
examples.romaji: dareka kita mitai. ima, doa no oto ga shita yo.
examples.en: Sounds like someone's here. I just heard the door.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{休|やす}み**みたいです**。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa yasumi mitai desu.
examples.en: It looks like this shop is closed today.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{眠|ねむ}い**みたいです**。
examples.romaji: mei wa nemui mitai desu.
examples.en: Mei seems sleepy.

examples.en: This bread is as hard as a rock.

examples.en: Look, that cloud looks like soft-serve ice cream.

examples.en: That dog looks like a doll. It's so cute.

title: Apparently, according to what you heard
goal: You'll be able to report information that seems reliable while keeping some distance from the claim.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Give an indirect report or supposition
text: ～らしいです can pass on information or make a supposition from indirect evidence. It often leaves the source or certainty less explicit than a direct report with そうだ.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～らしいです (report)
text: Use 休みらしい and 来ないらしい without inserting だ. The report sense differs from noun + らしい meaning typical of that noun.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective / Noun / な-adjective stem + らしいです

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{新|あたら}しい{店|みせ}が{開|あ}く**らしいです**。
examples.romaji: ashita, atarashii mise ga aku rashii desu.
examples.en: Apparently, a new shop opens tomorrow.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{先生|せんせい}はアメリカ{人|じん}**らしいです**よ。
examples.romaji: atarashii sensei wa amerikajin rashii desu yo.
examples.en: I hear the new teacher is American.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{忙|いそが}しい**らしいです**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa isogashii rashii desu.
examples.en: Apparently, the teacher is busy.

examples.ja: この{道|みち}は{通|とお}れない**らしいです**。
examples.romaji: kono michi wa toorenai rashii desu.
examples.en: Apparently, we cannot use this road.

examples.ja: {駅前|えきまえ}のパン{屋|や}は、{来月|らいげつ}で{終|お}わり**らしいです**。
examples.romaji: ekimae no pan'ya wa, raigetsu de owari rashii desu.
examples.en: I hear the bakery by the station is closing at the end of next month.

examples.ja: あのレストランは{予約|よやく}が{必要|ひつよう}**らしいです**。
examples.romaji: ano resutoran wa yoyaku ga hitsuyou rashii desu.
examples.en: I hear you need a reservation at that restaurant.

examples.ja: {今年|ことし}の{花火|はなび}{大会|たいかい}は{中止|ちゅうし}**らしいです**。
examples.romaji: kotoshi no hanabi taikai wa chuushi rashii desu.
examples.en: I hear this year's fireworks festival has been canceled.

title: Just like a typical example of something
goal: You'll be able to say that someone or something shows the qualities normally expected of a group.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Recognize a characteristic quality
text: Noun + らしい can mean typical of or suitably characteristic of that noun. Unlike a simple resemblance, the thing is understood as showing the expected qualities of its category.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～らしい (typical)
text: This use conjugates like an い-adjective: らしくない, らしかった. 春らしい means spring-like in a characteristic way; it is not a rumor that something is spring.

formation: Noun + らしい

examples.ja: {子|こ}{供|ども}**らしい**{元気|げんき}な{笑顔|えがお}です。
examples.romaji: kodomorashii genki na egao desu.
examples.en: That is a characteristically cheerful smile, just like a child.

examples.ja: {三月|さんがつ}になって、{春|はる}**らしい**{暖|あたた}かい{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いています。

examples.ja: {父|ちち}**らしい**{考|かんが}えです。

examples.en: That is a very typical idea of my father's.

examples.romaji: sono shizuka na hanashikata wa ren rashii desu.
examples.en: That quiet way of speaking is typical of Ren.

examples.en: The speaker passes on indirect information about Ren's future.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}の{説明|せつめい}は{先生|せんせい}**らしいです**。

title: Something is commonly said or believed
goal: You'll be able to report a widely held statement without naming a particular speaker.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Present a generally repeated claim
text: ～と言われています means that something is said or generally described in a certain way. It leaves the people making the claim unspecified.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～と言われています
text: Nouns and な-adjectives normally keep だ in the quoted clause. The expression attributes a claim to others; it does not itself prove that the claim is true.

formation: Plain clause + と言われています

examples.ja: この{木|き}は{千年|せんねん}{前|まえ}からある**と{言|い}われています**。
examples.romaji: kono ki wa sennen mae kara aru to iwarete imasu.
examples.en: This tree is said to have been here for a thousand years.

examples.ja: {納豆|なっとう}は{体|からだ}にいい**と{言|い}われています**。
examples.romaji: nattou wa karada ni ii to iwarete imasu.
examples.en: Natto is said to be good for your health.

examples.ja: この{町|まち}は{静|しず}かだ**と{言|い}われています**。
examples.romaji: kono machi wa shizuka da to iwarete imasu.
examples.en: This town is said to be quiet.

examples.ja: この{山|やま}は{美|うつく}しい**と{言|い}われています**。
examples.romaji: kono yama wa utsukushii to iwarete imasu.
examples.en: This mountain is said to be beautiful.

examples.ja: このお{寺|てら}は{日本|にほん}でいちばん{古|ふる}い**と{言|い}われています**。
examples.romaji: kono otera wa nihon de ichiban furui to iwarete imasu.
examples.en: This temple is said to be the oldest in Japan.

examples.romaji: kono machi no mizu wa totemo oishii to iwarete imasu.
examples.en: The water in this town is said to be very good.

examples.romaji: mainichi aruku koto wa kenkou ni ii to iwarete imasu.
examples.en: Walking every day is said to be good for your health.

title: Something might be true
goal: You'll be able to express a real possibility when you are not certain what is true or what will happen.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Leave open a possibility
text: ～かもしれません says something may be true. It expresses possibility without committing to a strong prediction.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～かもしれません
text: Nouns and な-adjectives omit だ. Past or negative forms can precede it: 忘れたかもしれない, 来ないかもしれない. Avoid interpreting it as a fixed numerical probability.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective / Noun / な-adjective stem + かもしれません

examples.ja: {鍵|かぎ}を{車|くるま}の{中|なか}に{忘|わす}れた**かもしれません**。
examples.romaji: kagi o kuruma no naka ni wasureta kamoshiremasen.
examples.en: I might have forgotten the keys inside the car.

examples.ja: {午後|ごご}から{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}る**かもしれません**。{傘|かさ}を{持|も}っていきましょう。
examples.romaji: gogo kara ame ga furu kamoshiremasen. kasa o motte ikimashou.
examples.en: It might rain from the afternoon. Let's take umbrellas.

examples.ja: {鍵|かぎ}を{忘|わす}れた**かもしれません**。
examples.romaji: kagi o wasureta kamoshiremasen.
examples.en: I may have forgotten my key.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{行|い}けない**かもしれません**。
examples.romaji: ashita wa ikenai kamoshiremasen.
examples.en: I may not be able to go tomorrow.

examples.ja: {道|みち}が{混|こ}んでいるので、{会議|かいぎ}に{遅|おく}れる**かもしれません**。
examples.romaji: michi ga konde iru node, kaigi ni okureru kamoshiremasen.
examples.en: The roads are crowded, so I might be late for the meeting.

examples.ja: {財布|さいふ}は{電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}に{忘|わす}れた**かもしれません**。
examples.romaji: saifu wa densha no naka ni wasureta kamoshiremasen.
examples.en: I might have left my wallet on the train.

examples.ja: {今週|こんしゅう}は{仕事|しごと}が{多|おお}いので、{週末|しゅうまつ}も{働|はたら}く**かもしれません**。
examples.romaji: konshuu wa shigoto ga ooi node, shuumatsu mo hataraku kamoshiremasen.
examples.en: I have a lot of work this week, so I might work on the weekend too.

examples.ja: ～かもしれません
examples.romaji: Something might be true
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: A result is expected from what you know
goal: You'll be able to state a strong expectation based on facts, plans, or reasonable evidence.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Expect a result from a reason
text: ～はずです expresses an expectation grounded in what the speaker knows. It means something should be the case, rather than that someone has a duty to do it.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～はずです
text: Use a supporting reason such as a schedule or known fact. The expectation can turn out wrong. Obligation is expressed with other patterns, not this はず.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + はずです / Noun の / な-adjective な + はずです

examples.ja: {父|ちち}はもう{家|いえ}にいる**はずです**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa mou ie ni iru hazu desu.
examples.en: My father should be at home by now.

examples.ja: {荷物|にもつ}は{昨日|きのう}{送|おく}ったので、{明日|あした}{届|とど}く**はずです**。
examples.romaji: nimotsu wa kinou okutta node, ashita todoku hazu desu.
examples.en: I sent the package yesterday, so it should arrive tomorrow.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{今日|きょう}も{開|あ}いている**はずです**。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa kyou mo aite iru hazu desu.
examples.en: This shop should be open today too.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}は{今|いま}、{静|しず}か**なはずです**。
examples.romaji: toshokan wa ima, shizuka na hazu desu.
examples.en: The library should be quiet right now.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}はこの{道|みち}を{知|し}っている**はずです**。
examples.romaji: ren wa kono michi o shitte iru hazu desu.
examples.en: Ren should know this road.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}は{三時|さんじ}に{終|お}わる**はずです**から、その{後|あと}で{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.romaji: kaigi wa sanji ni owaru hazu desu kara, sono ato de denwa shimasu.
examples.en: The meeting should end at three, so I'll call you after that.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんは{毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}していたから、{今日|きょう}の{試合|しあい}は{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}な**はずです**。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san wa mainichi renshuu shite ita kara, kyou no shiai wa daijoubu na hazu desu.
examples.en: Tanaka-san practiced every day, so today's match should go fine.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{土曜日|どようび}だから、{銀行|ぎんこう}は{休|やす}みの**はずです**。
examples.romaji: kyou wa doyoubi da kara, ginkou wa yasumi no hazu desu.
examples.en: It's Saturday today, so the bank should be closed.

examples.ja: ～はずです
examples.romaji: A result is expected from what you know
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: There is no reasonable way this can be true
goal: You'll be able to reject a possibility confidently because it conflicts with what you know.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Reject a possibility based on reason
text: ～はずがありません strongly rejects a possibility as incompatible with what the speaker knows. It means “there is no way” or “cannot possibly,” as a judgment rather than an objective guarantee.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～はずがありません
text: Contrast this with ないはず: 来ないはず means you expect someone not to come; 来るはずがない strongly rejects their coming. The reason should support the strength of the statement.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + はずがありません / Noun の / な-adjective な + はずがありません

examples.ja: この{小|ちい}さな{箱|はこ}に{自転車|じてんしゃ}が{入|はい}る**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: kono chiisana hako ni jitensha ga hairu hazu ga arimasen.
examples.en: There is no way a bicycle will fit in this tiny box.

examples.ja: {五百円|ごひゃくえん}で{新|あたら}しいパソコンが{買|か}える**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: gohyakuen de atarashii pasokon ga kaeru hazu ga arimasen.
examples.en: There's no way you can buy a new computer for 500 yen.

examples.ja: {一分|いっぷん}で{駅|えき}に{着|つ}く**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: ippun de eki ni tsuku hazu ga arimasen.
examples.en: There is no way we can reach the station in one minute.

examples.ja: あの{店|みせ}が{安|やす}い**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: ano mise ga yasui hazu ga arimasen.
examples.en: There is no way that shop is inexpensive.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{来|こ}**ないはずです**。
examples.romaji: 来ないはず
examples.en: The speaker expects Ren not to come, but does not rule out his arrival.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{来|く}る**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: 来るはずがない
examples.en: The speaker strongly rejects Ren's arrival as incompatible with what they know.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんは{今|いま}、アメリカに{住|す}んでいます。{今日|きょう}のパーティーに{来|く}る**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san wa ima, amerika ni sunde imasu. kyou no paatii ni kuru hazu ga arimasen.
examples.en: Tanaka-san lives in America now. There's no way she's coming to today's party.

examples.ja: あんなに{練習|れんしゅう}した{彼|かれ}が{負|ま}ける**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: anna ni renshuu shita kare ga makeru hazu ga arimasen.
examples.en: There's no way he'll lose after practicing that much.

examples.ja: {鍵|かぎ}はちゃんとかけました。ドアが{開|あ}いている**はずがありません**。
examples.romaji: kagi wa chanto kakemashita. doa ga aite iru hazu ga arimasen.
examples.en: I definitely locked it. There's no way the door is open.

examples.ja: ～はずがありません
examples.romaji: There is no reasonable way this can be true
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Float a guess and invite agreement
goal: You'll be able to soften an opinion into something the listener can confirm or push back on.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Seek agreement or offer a tentative thought
text: Rising ～じゃない？ can ask for agreement, rather than literally denying a statement. ～んじゃない？ often offers an explanatory guess such as “maybe it is…” or “don't you think…?”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～じゃない？・～んじゃない？
text: Before ん, nouns and な-adjectives need な: 休みなんじゃない？ Intonation and context distinguish agreement-seeking from an ordinary negative. These are conversational forms.

formation: Noun or な-adjective + じゃない？ / Plain clause + んじゃない？

examples.ja: このかばん、{便利|べんり}**じゃない？**
examples.romaji: kono kaban, benri janai?
examples.en: This bag is handy, isn't it?

examples.ja: もう{十時|じゅうじ}だよ。{店|みせ}は{閉|し}まっている**んじゃない**？
examples.romaji: mou juuji da yo. mise wa shimatte iru n janai?
examples.en: It's already ten. Isn't the shop closed by now?

examples.ja: この{問題|もんだい}、{簡単|かんたん}**じゃない？**
examples.romaji: kono mondai, kantan janai?
examples.en: Isn't this problem easy?

examples.ja: もうバスが{来|く}る**んじゃない？**
examples.romaji: mou basu ga kuru n janai?
examples.en: Don't you think the bus will be here soon?

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{休|やす}みな**んじゃない？**
examples.romaji: kyou wa yasumi nan janai?
examples.en: Maybe today is a day off?

examples.ja: このシャツ、{似合|にあ}う**んじゃない**？
examples.romaji: kono shatsu, niau n janai?
examples.en: Don't you think this shirt would suit you?

examples.ja: {空|そら}が{暗|くら}いから、{傘|かさ}を{持|も}っていったほうがいい**んじゃない**？
examples.romaji: sora ga kurai kara, kasa o motte itta hou ga ii n janai?
examples.en: The sky is dark, so wouldn't it be better to take an umbrella?

examples.ja: この{道|みち}のほうが{駅|えき}に{近|ちか}い**んじゃない**？
examples.romaji: kono michi no hou ga eki ni chikai n janai?
examples.en: Isn't this road closer to the station?

examples.ja: ～じゃない？・～んじゃない？
examples.romaji: Float a guess and invite agreement
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Wonder aloud in casual conversation
goal: You'll be able to express uncertainty, ask yourself a question, or consider what to do.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Wonder aloud
text: ～かな expresses a casual question to yourself or a softly expressed uncertainty. It can be heard by others, but is less direct than asking them a polite question.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～かな
text: Use 来るかな or 大丈夫かな. The speaker's uncertainty is central. It is usually too casual for a respectful direct inquiry to a customer or teacher.

formation: Plain clause / Noun / な-adjective stem + かな

examples.ja: バスはもうすぐ{来|く}る**かな**。
examples.romaji: basu wa mousugu kuru kana.
examples.en: I wonder if the bus will come soon.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんは、パーティーに{来|く}る**かな**。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san wa, paatii ni kuru kana.
examples.en: I wonder if Tanaka-san will come to the party.

examples.ja: {鍵|かぎ}はどこ**かな**。
examples.romaji: kagi wa doko ka na.
examples.en: I wonder where my key is.

examples.ja: これで{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}**かな**。
examples.romaji: kore de daijoubu ka na.
examples.en: I wonder if this will be all right.

examples.ja: {週末|しゅうまつ}、{天気|てんき}いい**かな**。
examples.romaji: shuumatsu, tenki ii kana.
examples.en: I wonder if the weather will be nice this weekend.

examples.ja: この{服|ふく}、ちょっと{高|たか}い**かな**。
examples.romaji: kono fuku, chotto takai kana.
examples.en: I wonder if these clothes are a bit expensive.

examples.ja: {急|いそ}げば、{電車|でんしゃ}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}う**かな**。
examples.romaji: isogeba, densha ni maniau kana.
examples.en: If I hurry, I wonder if I'll make the train.

examples.ja: ～かな
examples.romaji: Wonder aloud in casual conversation
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Whether something is true or not
goal: You'll be able to place a yes-or-no uncertainty inside a longer sentence.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Embed a yes-or-no question
text: ～かどうか puts “whether or not” inside another sentence. It lets you say you know, check, or are unsure about a yes-or-no issue.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～かどうか
text: Nouns and な-adjectives omit だ before かどうか. Do not use it after a question word such as どこ; that kind of embedded question uses か alone.

formation: Plain clause + かどうか + Main predicate

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{店|みせ}が{開|あ}いている**かどうか**{調|しら}べます。
examples.romaji: ren wa mise ga aite iru ka dou ka shirabemasu.
examples.en: Ren checks whether the shop is open.

examples.ja: ビザが{必要|ひつよう}**かどうか**、{大使館|たいしかん}に{聞|き}きました。
examples.romaji: biza ga hitsuyou ka dou ka, taishikan ni kikimashita.
examples.en: I asked the embassy whether or not I need a visa.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}{行|い}ける**かどうか**{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: ashita ikeru ka dou ka wakarimasen.
examples.en: I do not know whether I can go tomorrow.

examples.ja: これで{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}**かどうか**{確認|かくにん}します。
examples.romaji: kore de daijoubu ka dou ka kakunin shimasu.
examples.en: I will check whether this is all right.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}{晴|は}れる**かどうか**、まだ{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: ashita hareru ka dou ka, mada wakarimasen.
examples.en: We don't know yet whether or not it'll be sunny tomorrow.

examples.ja: この{服|ふく}が{似合|にあ}う**かどうか**、{着|き}てみます。
examples.romaji: kono fuku ga niau ka dou ka, kite mimasu.
examples.en: I'll try these clothes on to see whether or not they suit me.

examples.ja: お{店|みせ}が{今日|きょう}{開|あ}いている**かどうか**、{電話|でんわ}で{聞|き}いてみます。
examples.romaji: omise ga kyou aite iru ka dou ka, denwa de kiite mimasu.
examples.en: I'll call and ask whether or not the shop is open today.

examples.ja: ～かどうか
examples.romaji: Whether something is true or not
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Put an open question inside a sentence
goal: You'll be able to embed questions about who, what, where, when, why, or how in a larger statement.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Embed a question-word clause
text: A question-word clause followed by か can function as the content of knowing, asking, or deciding. It retains the missing information, such as where or when.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Question word + ～か
text: Omit question-final ですか inside the clause. Nouns and な-adjectives normally omit だ. Unlike かどうか, the issue is not simply yes or no.

formation: Question word + plain clause + か + Main predicate

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{鍵|かぎ}がどこにある**か**{分|わ}かりません。
examples.romaji: mei wa kagi ga doko ni aru ka wakarimasen.
examples.en: Mei does not know where the key is.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}にいくらかかる**か**{計算|けいさん}しました。
examples.romaji: ryokou ni ikura kakaru ka keisan shimashita.
examples.en: I worked out how much the trip will cost.

examples.ja: {何時|なんじ}に{出発|しゅっぱつ}する**か**{決|き}めましょう。
examples.romaji: nanji ni shuppatsu suru ka kimemashou.
examples.en: Let's decide what time to leave.

examples.ja: {誰|だれ}が{来|く}る**か**{知|し}っています。
examples.romaji: dare ga kuru ka shitte imasu.
examples.en: I know who is coming.

examples.ja: すみません、{駅|えき}はどこにある**か**{教|おし}えてください。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, eki wa doko ni aru ka oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: Excuse me, could you tell me where the station is?

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}が{何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まる**か**{知|し}っていますか。
examples.romaji: kaigi ga nanji ni hajimaru ka shitte imasu ka.
examples.en: Do you know what time the meeting starts?

examples.ja: {母|はは}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}に{何|なに}をあげる**か**、まだ{決|き}めていません。
examples.romaji: haha no tanjoubi ni nani o ageru ka, mada kimete imasen.
examples.en: I haven't decided yet what to give my mother for her birthday.

examples.ja: Question word + ～か
examples.romaji: Put an open question inside a sentence
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Report what a specific person told you
goal: You'll be able to attribute news or an opinion to the person you heard it from, rather than leaving the source vague.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Report a past message or something heard
text: ～と言っていた reports what someone was saying or said in a relevant past conversation. ～と聞いた reports information you heard, without necessarily identifying the original speaker.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～と言っていた・～と聞いた
text: Noun and な-adjective predicates retain だ inside the quote. Keep the reported message's tense and polarity. Context determines whether past 言っていた refers to repeated speech or a remembered statement.

formation: Plain quoted clause + と言っていた / と言っていました / と聞いた / と聞きました

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{明日|あした}{帰|かえ}る**と{言|い}っていました**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa ashita kaeru to itte imashita.
examples.en: My father said he would return tomorrow.

examples.ja: {駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しいスーパーができる**と{聞|き}きました**。
examples.romaji: ekimae ni atarashii suupaa ga dekiru to kikimashita.
examples.en: I heard a new supermarket is opening in front of the station.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}い**と{聞|き}きました**。
examples.romaji: kono mise wa yasui to kikimashita.
examples.en: I heard that this shop is inexpensive.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{忙|いそが}しい**と{言|い}っていました**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa isogashii to itte imashita.
examples.en: The teacher said they were busy.

examples.ja: {田中|たなか}さんは{明日|あした}{休|やす}む**と{言|い}っていました**。
examples.romaji: tanaka-san wa ashita yasumu to itte imashita.
examples.en: Tanaka-san said that he'd take tomorrow off.

examples.ja: {母|はは}は{週末|しゅうまつ}にこちらへ{来|く}る**と{言|い}っていました**。
examples.romaji: haha wa shuumatsu ni kochira e kuru to itte imashita.
examples.en: My mother said she'd come here on the weekend.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}はテストは{来週|らいしゅう}だ**と{言|い}っていました**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa tesuto wa raishuu da to itte imashita.
examples.en: The teacher said the test is next week.

examples.ja: ～と言っていた・～と聞いた
examples.romaji: Report what a specific person told you
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: A casual let's or I will
goal: You'll be able to form casual suggestions and express a decision to act.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Propose or intend an action
text: The volitional form expresses a proposal such as “let's” or the speaker's intention. It is casual compared with ～ましょう and is used in several later planning patterns.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 1 · Godan
text: Change the final u-row kana to the o-row and add う. The resulting long vowel is part of the volitional ending.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 2 · Ichidan
text: Remove final る and add よう. Do not keep the dictionary-form る.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 3 · Irregular
text: Memorize する→しよう and 来る→来よう (こよう).

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Volitional form (～(よ)う)
text: する becomes しよう and 来る becomes 来よう (こよう). With Group 1 verbs, the final u-row kana changes to the o-row: 行く→行こう. This form expresses intention, not future certainty.

formation: Group 2 without final る + よう
Group 1 o-row stem + う / Group 2 without る + よう
