title: Say what you are thinking of doing
goal: You'll be able to express a current intention or a decision you are considering.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: State your intention
text: Volitional verb + と思います expresses what the speaker intends or is thinking of doing. Use it for a plan the speaker is considering.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～(よ)うと思います
text: Make the volitional form before と思います: 行く → 行こう and 食べる → 食べよう. The ending changes with the verb group.

formation: Verb volitional form (～(よ)う) + と思います

examples.ja: {明日|あした}{図書館|としょかん}に{行|い}**こうと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: ashita toshokan ni ikou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I'm thinking of going to the library tomorrow.

examples.ja: {夏休|なつやす}みに{北海道|ほっかいどう}へ{行|い}**こうと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: natsuyasumi ni hokkaidou e ikou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I'm thinking of going to Hokkaido during the summer vacation.

examples.ja: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{家|いえ}で{休|やす}**もうと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: shuumatsu wa ie de yasumou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I'm thinking of resting at home this weekend.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}の{勉強|べんきょう}を{続|つづ}け**ようと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: nihongo no benkyou o tsuzukeyou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I intend to continue studying Japanese.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}{図書館|としょかん}に{行|い}**こうと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: Volitional + と思います — , intention
examples.en: 行こう is volitional: the speaker is considering this plan.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}{図書館|としょかん}に{行|い}く**と{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: Plain form + と思います — , expectation
examples.en: 行く is plain form: the speaker expects to go but does not state a decision.

examples.ja: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}の{大学|だいがく}を{受|う}け**ようと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: rainen, nihon no daigaku o ukeyou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I'm thinking of taking the entrance exam for a Japanese university next year.

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れたから、{今夜|こんや}は{早|はや}く{寝|ね}**ようと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: tsukareta kara, kon'ya wa hayaku neyou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I'm tired, so I'm thinking of going to bed early tonight.

examples.ja: {母|はは}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}に{花|はな}を{送|おく}**ろうと{思|おも}います**。
examples.romaji: haha no tanjoubi ni hana o okurou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I'm thinking of sending flowers for my mother's birthday.

examples.ja: ～(よ)うと思います
examples.romaji: Say what you are thinking of doing
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: State a scheduled plan
goal: You'll be able to describe an arranged plan or event that is expected to happen.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe a scheduled plan
text: ～予定です presents an action as planned or scheduled. It often sounds more arranged than a thought being considered, though plans can still change.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～予定です
text: Use 出発する予定 and 旅行の予定. A negative plan can use 行かない予定. Do not attach ます directly before 予定.

formation: Verb dictionary form + 予定です / Noun + の予定です

examples.ja: {家族|かぞく}は{明日|あした}{出発|しゅっぱつ}する**{予定|よてい}です**。
examples.romaji: kazoku wa ashita shuppatsu suru yotei desu.
examples.en: The family is scheduled to leave tomorrow.

examples.ja: {飛行機|ひこうき}は{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}に{着|つ}く**{予定|よてい}です**。
examples.romaji: hikouki wa gogo sanji ni tsuku yotei desu.
examples.en: The plane is scheduled to arrive at 3 p.m.

examples.ja: {午後|ごご}は{会議|かいぎ}の**{予定|よてい}です**。
examples.romaji: gogo wa kaigi no yotei desu.
examples.en: A meeting is scheduled for the afternoon.

examples.ja: {来週|らいしゅう}、{祖父|そふ}に{会|あ}う**{予定|よてい}です**。
examples.romaji: raishuu, sofu ni au yotei desu.
examples.en: I plan to see my grandfather next week.

examples.ja: {来週|らいしゅう}の{月曜日|げつようび}に{大阪|おおさか}へ{出張|しゅっちょう}する**{予定|よてい}です**。
examples.romaji: raishuu no getsuyoubi ni oosaka e shucchou suru yotei desu.
examples.en: I'm scheduled to go to Osaka on business next Monday.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{午前中|ごぜんちゅう}は{歯医者|はいしゃ}に{行|い}く**{予定|よてい}です**。
examples.romaji: ashita no gozenchuu wa haisha ni iku yotei desu.
examples.en: Tomorrow morning I'm scheduled to go to the dentist.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{駅|えき}は{来年|らいねん}できる**{予定|よてい}です**。
examples.romaji: atarashii eki wa rainen dekiru yotei desu.
examples.en: The new station is scheduled to open next year.

examples.ja: ～予定です
examples.romaji: State a scheduled plan
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Make a decision yourself
goal: You'll be able to say that you have personally decided to do or not do something.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Make your own decision
text: ～ことにする presents a choice made by the speaker or named decision-maker. It focuses on deciding to adopt an action or not do it.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ことにする
text: Use ことにしました for a decision already made. ～ことにしている can describe a personal rule. It contrasts with ことになる, where the arrangement is presented as decided or resulting without foregrounding your choice.

formation: Verb dictionary form / ない-form + ことにする

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{電車|でんしゃ}で{行|い}く**ことにしました**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa densha de iku koto ni shimashita.
examples.en: My father decided to go by train.

examples.ja: {少|すこ}し{高|たか}いけど、このパソコンを{買|か}う**ことにしました**。
examples.romaji: sukoshi takai kedo, kono pasokon o kau koto ni shimashita.
examples.en: It's a bit expensive, but I've decided to buy this computer.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{外食|がいしょく}しない**ことにしました**。
examples.romaji: kyou wa gaishoku shinai koto ni shimashita.
examples.en: I decided not to eat out today.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{歩|ある}く**ことにしています**。
examples.romaji: mainichi aruku koto ni shite imasu.
examples.en: I make it a rule to walk every day.

examples.ja: {健康|けんこう}のために、{毎朝|まいあさ}{歩|ある}く**ことにしました**。
examples.romaji: kenkou no tame ni, maiasa aruku koto ni shimashita.
examples.en: I've decided to walk every morning for my health.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}なので、{今日|きょう}は{出|で}かけない**ことにしました**。
examples.romaji: ame na node, kyou wa dekakenai koto ni shimashita.
examples.en: It's raining, so I've decided not to go out today.

examples.ja: {来年|らいねん}、{日本|にほん}に{留学|りゅうがく}する**ことにしました**。
examples.romaji: rainen, nihon ni ryuugaku suru koto ni shimashita.
examples.en: I've decided to go and study in Japan next year.

examples.ja: ～ことにする
examples.romaji: Make a decision yourself
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: A decision or outcome comes from circumstances
goal: You'll be able to describe what has been decided by others or what a situation ends up causing.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Announce an arrangement or resulting decision
text: ～ことになる presents an arrangement as decided or as how events have turned out. It backgrounds who made the decision, rather than necessarily claiming it was forced.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ことになる
text: Use ことになりました for an arrangement that has now been settled. The speaker may have participated in deciding; the grammar simply does not foreground that personal choice.

formation: Verb dictionary form / ない-form + ことになる

examples.ja: {来月|らいげつ}、{家族|かぞく}で{旅行|りょこう}する**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: raigetsu, kazoku de ryokou suru koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: It has been decided that our family will travel next month.

examples.ja: {来月|らいげつ}から{大阪|おおさか}の{事務所|じむしょ}で{働|はたら}く**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: raigetsu kara oosaka no jimusho de hataraku koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: It's been decided that I'll work at the Osaka office from next month.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}は{明日|あした}{行|おこな}う**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: kaigi wa ashita okonau koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: The meeting has been arranged for tomorrow.

examples.ja: {今年|ことし}は{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}さない**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: kotoshi wa hikkosanai koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: It has been decided that we will not move this year.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{来月|らいげつ}{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す**ことにしました**。
examples.romaji: ことにしました
examples.en: The speaker foregrounds their own decision to move.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{来月|らいげつ}{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: ことになりました
examples.en: The move is presented as a settled arrangement; the decision-maker stays in the background.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{会議|かいぎ}は{十時|じゅうじ}から{始|はじ}める**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: ashita no kaigi wa juuji kara hajimeru koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: It's been decided that tomorrow's meeting will start at ten.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}の{仕事|しごと}で、{家族|かぞく}でアメリカに{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: chichi no shigoto de, kazoku de amerika ni hikkosu koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: Because of my father's job, our family is going to move to America.

examples.ja: {今年|ことし}の{夏|なつ}、{姉|あね}が{結婚|けっこん}する**ことになりました**。
examples.romaji: kotoshi no natsu, ane ga kekkon suru koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: It's been settled that my older sister will get married this summer.

examples.ja: ～ことになる
examples.romaji: A decision or outcome comes from circumstances
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Something is arranged or established as a rule
goal: You'll be able to describe standing plans, schedules, customs, and rules already in effect.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe an established rule or arrangement
text: ～ことになっています describes a standing rule, schedule, or agreed arrangement. It is what is supposed to happen, even if someone sometimes fails to follow it.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ことになっています
text: The ている form describes the arrangement currently in effect. A personal habit is more naturally ことにしている when the speaker's own decision matters.

formation: Verb dictionary form / ない-form + ことになっています

examples.ja: ここでは{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ**ことになっています**。
examples.romaji: koko dewa kutsu o nugu koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: The rule here is to take off your shoes.

examples.ja: {図書館|としょかん}の{本|ほん}は{二週間|にしゅうかん}で{返|かえ}す**ことになっています**。
examples.romaji: toshokan no hon wa nishuukan de kaesu koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: Library books are supposed to be returned within two weeks.

examples.ja: {九時|くじ}に{集|あつ}まる**ことになっています**。
examples.romaji: kuji ni atsumaru koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: We are supposed to gather at nine.

examples.ja: {教室|きょうしつ}では{食|た}べない**ことになっています**。
examples.romaji: kyoushitsu dewa tabenai koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: The rule is not to eat in the classroom.

examples.ja: この{寮|りょう}では、{夜|よる}{十一時|じゅういちじ}までに{帰|かえ}る**ことになっています**。
examples.romaji: kono ryou de wa, yoru juuichiji made ni kaeru koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: In this dormitory, you're supposed to be back by eleven at night.

examples.ja: この{会社|かいしゃ}では、{朝|あさ}{九時|くじ}までに{来|く}る**ことになっています**。
examples.romaji: kono kaisha de wa, asa kuji made ni kuru koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: At this company, you're supposed to arrive by nine in the morning.

examples.ja: この{学校|がっこう}では、{教室|きょうしつ}に{入|はい}るとき{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ**ことになっています**。
examples.romaji: kono gakkou de wa, kyoushitsu ni hairu toki kutsu o nugu koto ni natte imasu.
examples.en: At this school, you're supposed to take off your shoes when you enter the classroom.

examples.ja: ～ことになっています
examples.romaji: Something is arranged or established as a rule
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Reach a point where something becomes possible or habitual
goal: You'll be able to describe a change in ability, behavior, or a recurring situation over time.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe a change in ability or habit
text: ～ようになる describes reaching a new ability, habit, or condition. It highlights a change from how things were before.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ようになる
text: Potential forms describe gaining ability, while ordinary verbs describe a new habit. Negative ～なくなる is also common for ceasing an action. Do not use ことになる for a naturally developing ability.

formation: Dictionary, potential, or negative verb + ようになる

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{自転車|じてんしゃ}に{乗|の}れる**ようになりました**。
examples.romaji: mei wa jitensha ni noreru you ni narimashita.
examples.en: Mei has become able to ride a bicycle.

examples.ja: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}してから、{毎朝|まいあさ}{駅|えき}まで{歩|ある}く**ようになりました**。
examples.romaji: hikkoshite kara, maiasa eki made aruku you ni narimashita.
examples.en: Since moving, I've gotten into the habit of walking to the station every morning.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}る**ようになりました**。
examples.romaji: maiasa hashiru you ni narimashita.
examples.en: I have started running every morning.

examples.ja: {漢字|かんじ}が{読|よ}める**ようになりたい**です。
examples.romaji: kanji ga yomeru you ni naritai desu.
examples.en: I want to become able to read kanji.

examples.ja: {毎日|まいにち}{練習|れんしゅう}して、{自転車|じてんしゃ}に{乗|の}れる**ようになりました**。
examples.romaji: mainichi renshuu shite, jitensha ni noreru you ni narimashita.
examples.en: After practicing every day, I've become able to ride a bicycle.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}に{来|き}てから、{納豆|なっとう}が{食|た}べられる**ようになりました**。
examples.romaji: nihon ni kite kara, nattou ga taberareru you ni narimashita.
examples.en: Since coming to Japan, I've become able to eat natto.

examples.ja: {最近|さいきん}、{日本語|にほんご}のニュースが{少|すこ}し{分|わ}かる**ようになりました**。
examples.romaji: saikin, nihongo no nyuusu ga sukoshi wakaru you ni narimashita.
examples.en: Recently, I've started to understand Japanese news a little.

examples.ja: ～ようになる
examples.romaji: Reach a point where something becomes possible or habitual
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Make an ongoing effort to do something
goal: You'll be able to say that you deliberately try to build or avoid a habit.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Make an effort to establish a behavior
text: ～ようにする means making an effort or taking care to achieve a behavior or condition. ～ようにしている describes an ongoing practice.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ようにする
text: Use 忘れないようにする for taking care not to forget. It emphasizes effort rather than guaranteeing success; ～ようになる reports the resulting change.

formation: Dictionary or negative verb + ようにする

examples.ja: {父|ちち}は{野菜|やさい}をたくさん{食|た}べる**ようにしています**。
examples.romaji: chichi wa yasai o takusan taberu you ni shite imasu.
examples.en: My father makes a point of eating plenty of vegetables.

examples.ja: {次|つぎ}からは、{宿題|しゅくだい}を{忘|わす}れない**ようにします**。
examples.romaji: tsugi kara wa, shukudai o wasurenai you ni shimasu.
examples.en: From now on, I'll make sure not to forget my homework.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}は{遅|おく}れない**ようにします**。
examples.romaji: ashita wa okurenai you ni shimasu.
examples.en: I will take care not to be late tomorrow.

examples.ja: {野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べる**ようにしています**。
examples.romaji: yasai o taberu you ni shite imasu.
examples.en: I try to make a habit of eating vegetables.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}る**ようにしています**。
examples.romaji: ようにしている
examples.en: Presents running as an ongoing effort, without claiming it always succeeds.

examples.ja: {毎朝|まいあさ}{走|はし}る**ようになりました**。
examples.romaji: ようになった
examples.en: Reports a change from not running regularly to doing so.

examples.ja: {健康|けんこう}のために、{毎日|まいにち}{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べる**ようにしています**。
examples.romaji: kenkou no tame ni, mainichi yasai o taberu you ni shite imasu.
examples.en: I try to eat vegetables every day for my health.

examples.ja: {夜|よる}は{甘|あま}いものを{食|た}べない**ようにしています**。
examples.romaji: yoru wa amai mono o tabenai you ni shite imasu.
examples.en: I try not to eat sweets at night.

examples.ja: {約束|やくそく}の{時間|じかん}に{遅|おく}れない**ようにしてください**。
examples.romaji: yakusoku no jikan ni okurenai you ni shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please make sure you're not late for the appointment.

examples.ja: ～ようにする
examples.romaji: Make an ongoing effort to do something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Describe change that builds over time
goal: You'll be able to say a change happens gradually or that it keeps picking up pace.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe gradual or rapid progress
text: だんだん presents change as gradual. どんどん emphasizes energetic, steady, or rapid forward progress. Both describe a process rather than one isolated event.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use だんだん・どんどん
text: だんだん often occurs with なる. どんどん can describe actions such as reading one book after another. Choose according to the pace and feel of the development.

formation: だんだん / どんどん + Changing or progressing predicate

examples.ja: {空|そら}が**だんだん**{暗|くら}くなってきました。
examples.romaji: sora ga dandan kuraku natte kimashita.
examples.en: The sky has gradually grown darker.

examples.ja: {駅前|えきまえ}には{新|あたら}しいビルが**どんどん**できています。
examples.romaji: ekimae ni wa atarashii biru ga dondon dekite imasu.
examples.en: New buildings are going up one after another in front of the station.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{本|ほん}を**どんどん**{読|よ}んでいます。
examples.romaji: ren wa hon o dondon yonde imasu.
examples.en: Ren is reading one book after another.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}が**だんだん**{分|わ}かるようになりました。
examples.romaji: nihongo ga dandan wakaru you ni narimashita.
examples.en: I gradually became able to understand Japanese.

examples.ja: {十月|じゅうがつ}になって、**だんだん**{寒|さむ}くなってきました。
examples.romaji: juugatsu ni natte, dandan samuku natte kimashita.
examples.en: Now that it's October, it's gradually gotten colder.

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}の{勉強|べんきょう}が**だんだん**おもしろくなってきました。
examples.romaji: nihongo no benkyou ga dandan omoshiroku natte kimashita.
examples.en: Studying Japanese has gradually become more interesting.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{仕事|しごと}にも**だんだん**{慣|な}れてきました。
examples.romaji: atarashii shigoto ni mo dandan narete kimashita.
examples.en: I've gradually gotten used to my new job, too.

examples.ja: だんだん・どんどん
examples.romaji: Describe change that builds over time
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Describe an outcome that finally happens
goal: You'll be able to use やっと for a long-awaited result, often involving effort or relief, and とうとう for an eventual outcome that finally comes about.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Reach an outcome after a long process
text: やっと often conveys relief after difficulty or waiting. とうとう emphasizes that the eventual outcome has finally arrived, whether welcome or unwelcome.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use やっと・とうとう
text: Both can occur with a positive result. とうとう also fits an unwanted final outcome, while やっと usually stresses achieving something awaited or managing to do it.

formation: やっと / とうとう + Outcome

examples.ja: {家族|かぞく}は**やっと**キャンプ{場|じょう}に{着|つ}きました。
examples.romaji: kazoku wa yatto kyanpujou ni tsukimashita.
examples.en: The family finally reached the campsite.

examples.ja: {一時間|いちじかん}{待|ま}って、**やっと**バスが{来|き}ました。
examples.romaji: ichijikan matte, yatto basu ga kimashita.
examples.en: I waited an hour, and the bus finally came.

examples.ja: **やっと**{宿題|しゅくだい}が{終|お}わりました。
examples.romaji: yatto shukudai ga owarimashita.
examples.en: I finally finished my homework.

examples.ja: {古|ふる}い{時計|とけい}が**とうとう**{壊|こわ}れました。
examples.romaji: furui tokei ga toutou kowaremashita.
examples.en: The old clock finally broke.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}まで{走|はし}って、**やっと**{電車|でんしゃ}に{間|ま}に{合|あ}いました。
examples.romaji: eki made hashitte, yatto densha ni maniaimashita.
examples.en: I ran to the station and only just made the train.

examples.ja: **やっと**{宿題|しゅくだい}が{終|お}わった。これで{寝|ね}られる。
examples.romaji: yatto shukudai ga owatta. kore de nerareru.
examples.en: I've finally finished my homework. Now I can go to sleep.

examples.ja: {三日|みっか}{休|やす}んで、{熱|ねつ}が**やっと**{下|さ}がりました。
examples.romaji: mikka yasunde, netsu ga yatto sagarimashita.
examples.en: After three days of rest, my fever has finally come down.

examples.ja: やっと・とうとう
examples.romaji: Describe an outcome that finally happens
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Describe another person's feelings or desires
goal: You'll be able to describe observable signs of someone else's emotions with ～がる and their apparent wishes with ～たがる.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe outward signs of a feeling or desire
text: ～がる presents someone's observable reaction to a feeling. ～たがる describes signs that someone wants to do an action. They are useful when reporting another person's state from behavior.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～がる・～たがる
text: Current reactions commonly use がっている and たがっている. These are Group 1 verbs. Not every adjective accepts がる; use established feelings such as 怖がる. Direct quotations or questions can use ordinary ～たい for another person.

formation: Feeling adjective without い + がる / Verb ます-stem + たがる

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{犬|いぬ}を{怖|こわ}**がっています**。
examples.romaji: mei wa inu o kowagatte imasu.
examples.en: Mei is showing that she is afraid of the dog.

examples.ja: {祖父|そふ}は{孫|まご}に{会|あ}い**たがっています**。
examples.romaji: sofu wa mago ni aitagatte imasu.
examples.en: My grandfather wants to see his grandchildren.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{外|そと}に{行|い}き**たがっています**。
examples.romaji: ren wa soto ni ikitagatte imasu.
examples.en: Ren is showing that he wants to go outside.

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{新|あたら}しい{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{欲|ほ}し**がっています**。
examples.romaji: mei wa atarashii jitensha o hoshigatte imasu.
examples.en: Mei is showing that she wants a new bicycle.

examples.ja: {弟|おとうと}は{歯医者|はいしゃ}を{怖|こわ}**がっています**。
examples.romaji: otouto wa haisha o kowagatte imasu.
examples.en: My younger brother is scared of the dentist.

examples.ja: {娘|むすめ}は{新|あたら}しいゲームを{欲|ほ}し**がっています**。
examples.romaji: musume wa atarashii geemu o hoshigatte imasu.
examples.en: My daughter wants a new game.

examples.ja: {子|こ}どもたちは{早|はや}く{海|うみ}で{泳|およ}ぎ**たがっています**。
examples.romaji: kodomotachi wa hayaku umi de oyogitagatte imasu.
examples.en: The children are eager to swim in the sea.

examples.ja: ～がる・～たがる
examples.romaji: Describe another person's feelings or desires
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Want someone else to do something
goal: You'll be able to express what action you want another person to take or avoid.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Want someone else to act
text: ～てほしい expresses the speaker's wish for another person to do something. The wished-for actor commonly takes に. To report Mei's wish, this example adds ～と思っています. It can also express a wish about a situation.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てほしい
text: Contrast 自分が行きたい, your own desire to go, with someoneに行ってほしい, wanting them to go. It may sound demanding when used directly to a superior; choose request forms appropriately.

formation: Person に + Verb て-form + ほしい

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{蓮|れん}に{手伝|てつだ}**ってほしい**と{思|おも}っています。
examples.romaji: mei wa ren ni tetsudatte hoshii to omotte imasu.
examples.en: Mei wants Ren to help her.

examples.ja: {母|はは}には{長生|ながい}きし**てほしいです**。
examples.romaji: haha ni wa nagaiki shite hoshii desu.
examples.en: I want my mother to live a long life.

examples.ja: もう{少|すこ}しゆっくり{話|はな}し**てほしい**です。
examples.romaji: mou sukoshi yukkuri hanashite hoshii desu.
examples.en: I would like you to speak a little more slowly.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}に{来|き}**てほしい**です。
examples.romaji: tomodachi ni kite hoshii desu.
examples.en: I want my friend to come.

examples.ja: {隣|となり}の{人|ひと}には、{夜|よる}は{静|しず}かにし**てほしいです**。
examples.romaji: tonari no hito ni wa, yoru wa shizuka ni shite hoshii desu.
examples.en: I wish my neighbors would keep quiet at night.

examples.ja: {子|こ}どもには{野菜|やさい}をもっと{食|た}べ**てほしいです**。
examples.romaji: kodomo ni wa yasai o motto tabete hoshii desu.
examples.en: I want my kids to eat more vegetables.

examples.ja: {夫|おっと}には{料理|りょうり}を{手伝|てつだ}っ**てほしい**と{思|おも}っています。
examples.romaji: otto ni wa ryouri o tetsudatte hoshii to omotte imasu.
examples.en: I'd like my husband to help with the cooking.

examples.ja: ～てほしい
examples.romaji: Want someone else to do something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Give background before a request or question
goal: You'll be able to introduce a situation gently and invite the listener to respond or help.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Give background before seeking help
text: ～んですが introduces a situation and leaves room for the listener to respond. It often leads into a request or question; が softens the approach rather than necessarily meaning “but.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～んですが
text: Use a context relevant to the help you need. You may state the request afterward or leave it implied. Nouns and な-adjectives need な before ん.

formation: Plain verb / い-adjective + んですが / Noun or な-adjective + なんですが

examples.ja: {道|みち}が{分|わ}からない**んですが**、{教|おし}えていただけますか。
examples.romaji: michi ga wakaranai n desu ga, oshiete itadakemasu ka.
examples.en: I do not know the way; could you help me?

examples.ja: {日本語|にほんご}がよく{分|わ}からない**んですが**、{英語|えいご}のメニューはありますか。
examples.romaji: nihongo ga yoku wakaranai n desu ga, eigo no menyuu wa arimasu ka.
examples.en: I don't understand Japanese very well. Do you have an English menu?

examples.ja: {予約|よやく}したい**んですが**、{空|あ}いていますか。
examples.romaji: yoyaku shitai n desu ga, aite imasu ka.
examples.en: I would like to reserve a place; is there availability?

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めてな**んですが**、どうすればいいですか。
examples.romaji: hajimete nan desu ga, dou sureba ii desu ka.
examples.en: This is my first time; what should I do?

examples.ja: すみません、{駅|えき}へ{行|い}きたい**んですが**、どのバスに{乗|の}ればいいですか。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, eki e ikitai n desu ga, dono basu ni noreba ii desu ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, I'd like to go to the station. Which bus should I take?

examples.ja: このシャツ、もう{少|すこ}し{大|おお}きいのがほしい**んですが**、ありますか。
examples.romaji: kono shatsu, mou sukoshi ookii no ga hoshii n desu ga, arimasu ka.
examples.en: I'd like this shirt in a slightly bigger size. Do you have one?

examples.ja: {予約|よやく}はしていない**んですが**、{二人|ふたり}{入|はい}れますか。
examples.romaji: yoyaku wa shite inai n desu ga, futari hairemasu ka.
examples.en: We don't have a reservation, but is there room for two?

examples.ja: ～んですが
examples.romaji: Give background before a request or question
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Do an action as a favor for someone
goal: You'll be able to describe doing something that benefits another person from the giver's viewpoint.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Do an action for someone's benefit
text: ～てあげる presents an action as a favor done for someone else. The person doing it is the subject; the sentence looks outward from the helper's side.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てあげる
text: The beneficiary's particle depends on the action; not every sentence needs に. Describing your own act as a favor can sound self-congratulatory, especially directly to a superior. Use the construction with appropriate relationships.

formation: Helper は + beneficiary に + Verb て-form + あげる

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}は{芽衣|めい}の{靴|くつ}ひもを{結|むす}**んであげます**。
examples.romaji: ren wa mei no kutsuhimo o musunde agemasu.
examples.en: Ren ties Mei's shoelaces for her.

examples.ja: {弟|おとうと}の{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{直|なお}し**てあげました**。
examples.romaji: otouto no jitensha o naoshite agemashita.
examples.en: I fixed my younger brother's bicycle for him.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}に{写真|しゃしん}を{送|おく}**ってあげました**。
examples.romaji: tomodachi ni shashin o okutte agemashita.
examples.en: I sent a photograph to my friend as a favor.

examples.ja: {母|はは}の{荷物|にもつ}を{持|も}**ってあげます**。
examples.romaji: haha no nimotsu o motte agemasu.
examples.en: I will carry my mother's luggage for her.

examples.ja: {妹|いもうと}に{算数|さんすう}の{宿題|しゅくだい}を{教|おし}え**てあげました**。
examples.romaji: imouto ni sansuu no shukudai o oshiete agemashita.
examples.en: I helped my younger sister with her math homework.

examples.ja: {道|みち}に{迷|まよ}っている{人|ひと}を{駅|えき}まで{連|つ}れて{行|い}っ**てあげました**。
examples.romaji: michi ni mayotte iru hito o eki made tsurete itte agemashita.
examples.en: I took someone who was lost to the station.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}の{階段|かいだん}で、おばあさんの{荷物|にもつ}を{持|も}っ**てあげました**。
examples.romaji: eki no kaidan de, obaasan no nimotsu o motte agemashita.
examples.en: I carried an elderly woman's bags on the stairs at the station.

examples.ja: ～てあげる
examples.romaji: Do an action as a favor for someone
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Someone kindly does something for me
goal: You'll be able to describe an action another person performs for you or someone close to you.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Receive a favor from someone acting
text: ～てくれる describes someone doing something that benefits the speaker or someone the speaker identifies with. The helper remains the subject of the sentence.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てくれる
text: The beneficiary is often omitted because the speaker's viewpoint supplies it. For a respected helper, ～てくださる is the honorific counterpart. Track perspective rather than translating only the English word “give.”

formation: Helper は/が + Verb て-form + くれる

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}が{宿題|しゅくだい}を{手伝|てつだ}**ってくれました**。
examples.romaji: ren ga shukudai o tetsudatte kuremashita.
examples.en: Ren helped me with my homework.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきたとき、{田中|たなか}さんが{傘|かさ}を{貸|か}し**てくれました**。
examples.romaji: ame ga futte kita toki, tanaka-san ga kasa o kashite kuremashita.
examples.en: When it started to rain, Tanaka-san lent me an umbrella.

examples.ja: {母|はは}が{お弁当|おべんとう}を{作|つく}**ってくれました**。
examples.romaji: haha ga obentou o tsukutte kuremashita.
examples.en: My mother made lunch for me.

examples.ja: {友達|ともだち}が{道|みち}を{教|おし}え**てくれました**。
examples.romaji: tomodachi ga michi o oshiete kuremashita.
examples.en: My friend showed me the way.

examples.ja: {駅員|えきいん}さんが{切符|きっぷ}の{買|か}い{方|かた}を{教|おし}え**てくれました**。
examples.romaji: ekiinsan ga kippu no kaikata o oshiete kuremashita.
examples.en: The station attendant showed me how to buy a ticket.

examples.ja: {友|とも}だちが{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しを{手伝|てつだ}っ**てくれました**。
examples.romaji: tomodachi ga hikkoshi o tetsudatte kuremashita.
examples.en: My friends helped me move.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}だったので、{父|ちち}が{駅|えき}まで{車|くるま}で{送|おく}っ**てくれました**。
examples.romaji: ame datta node, chichi ga eki made kuruma de okutte kuremashita.
examples.en: It was raining, so my father drove me to the station.

examples.ja: ～てくれる
examples.romaji: Someone kindly does something for me
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Receive the benefit of someone's action
goal: You'll be able to say that you arranged for or received help from someone who did an action.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe receiving someone's help
text: ～てもらう puts the recipient of help at the center. The helper is usually marked に, and the main verb describes the action that helper performs.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てもらう
text: 私は先生に教えてもらった means the teacher taught me, not that I taught the teacher. ～てくれる can describe the same favor with the helper as subject; ～てもらう takes the recipient's viewpoint.

formation: Recipient は + helper に + Verb て-form + もらう

examples.ja: {芽衣|めい}は{蓮|れん}に{宿題|しゅくだい}を{手伝|てつだ}**ってもらいました**。
examples.romaji: mei wa ren ni shukudai o tetsudatte moraimashita.
examples.en: Mei got Ren to help her with her homework.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}に{作文|さくぶん}を{直|なお}し**てもらいました**。
examples.romaji: sensei ni sakubun o naoshite moraimashita.
examples.en: I had my teacher correct my essay.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}に{漢字|かんじ}を{教|おし}え**てもらいました**。
examples.romaji: sensei ni kanji o oshiete moraimashita.
examples.en: I received help from the teacher with kanji.

examples.ja: {父|ちち}に{駅|えき}まで{送|おく}**ってもらいます**。
examples.romaji: chichi ni eki made okutte moraimasu.
examples.en: I will have my father take me to the station.

examples.ja: {蓮|れん}が{私|わたし}を{手伝|てつだ}**ってくれました**。
examples.romaji: くれる
examples.en: Ren is the helper and subject; 私 is the person helped.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{蓮|れん}に{手伝|てつだ}**ってもらいました**。
examples.romaji: もらう
examples.en: 私は names the recipient; 蓮 is the helper marked by に.

examples.ja: {友|とも}だちに{駅|えき}まで{車|くるま}で{送|おく}っ**てもらいました**。
examples.romaji: tomodachi ni eki made kuruma de okutte moraimashita.
examples.en: A friend gave me a ride to the station.

examples.ja: {店員|てんいん}さんに{足|あし}のサイズを{測|はか}っ**てもらいました**。
examples.romaji: ten'insan ni ashi no saizu o hakatte moraimashita.
examples.en: I had the shop assistant measure my foot size.

examples.ja: {兄|あに}にパソコンの{使|つか}い{方|かた}を{教|おし}え**てもらいました**。
examples.romaji: ani ni pasokon no tsukaikata o oshiete moraimashita.
examples.en: My older brother taught me how to use the computer.

examples.ja: ～てもらう
examples.romaji: Receive the benefit of someone's action
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

pattern: ～てくれませんか・～てもらえませんか
title: Ask someone politely to help by doing something
goal: You'll be able to make considerate requests by framing the action as a favor.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Ask for a helpful action
text: ～てくれませんか and ～てもらえませんか are requests for someone to do something for you. Their negative-question shape softens the request.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てくれませんか・～てもらえませんか
text: くれませんか asks whether the listener will give the favor. もらえませんか asks whether you can receive it. These are not usually literal questions expecting refusal; more deferential requests can use いただけませんか.

formation: Verb て-form + くれませんか / もらえませんか

examples.ja: この{箱|はこ}を{持|も}**ってくれませんか**。
examples.romaji: kono hako o motte kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Could you carry this box for me?

examples.ja: すみません、もう{少|すこ}しゆっくり{話|はな}し**てもらえませんか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, mou sukoshi yukkuri hanashite moraemasen ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, could I ask you to speak a little more slowly?

examples.ja: {もう一度|もういちど}{説明|せつめい}し**てもらえませんか**。
examples.romaji: mou ichido setsumei shite moraemasen ka.
examples.en: Could you explain it once more for me?

examples.ja: {窓|まど}を{閉|し}め**てくれませんか**。
examples.romaji: mado o shimete kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Could you close the window for me?

examples.ja: すみません、この{荷物|にもつ}を{棚|たな}に{上|あ}げ**てくれませんか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, kono nimotsu o tana ni agete kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, would you put this bag up on the rack for me?

examples.ja: すみません、もう{少|すこ}し{静|しず}かにし**てくれませんか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, mou sukoshi shizuka ni shite kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, would you mind being a little quieter?

examples.ja: {暑|あつ}いですね。{窓|まど}を{開|あ}け**てくれませんか**。
examples.romaji: atsui desu ne. mado o akete kuremasen ka.
examples.en: It's hot, isn't it? Would you open the window for me?

examples.ja: ～てくれませんか・～てもらえませんか
examples.romaji: Ask someone politely to help by doing something
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Thank someone for what they did
goal: You'll be able to name the helpful action you are grateful for when thanking someone.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Thank someone for a specific favor
text: ～てくれてありがとう names the helpful action you are thankful for. くれて frames it as a benefit received from the person you address.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てくれてありがとう
text: Use ありがとうございます for greater politeness. For a respected helper, ～てくださってありがとうございます is more appropriate. Match the action to what the listener actually did.

formation: Verb て-form + くれてありがとう

examples.ja: {手伝|てつだ}**ってくれてありがとう**。
examples.romaji: tetsudatte kurete arigatou.
examples.en: Thank you for helping me.

examples.ja: {話|はなし}を{聞|き}い**てくれてありがとう**。{少|すこ}し{元気|げんき}になったよ。
examples.romaji: hanashi o kiite kurete arigatou. sukoshi genki ni natta yo.
examples.en: Thanks for listening. I feel a bit better now.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{来|き}**てくれてありがとう**。
examples.romaji: kyou wa kite kurete arigatou.
examples.en: Thank you for coming today.

examples.ja: {写真|しゃしん}を{送|おく}**ってくれてありがとうございます**。
examples.romaji: shashin o okutte kurete arigatou gozaimasu.
examples.en: Thank you for sending me the photograph.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}を{覚|おぼ}えてい**てくれてありがとう**。
examples.romaji: watashi no tanjoubi o oboete ite kurete arigatou.
examples.en: Thanks for remembering my birthday.

examples.ja: {遠|とお}いところまで{来|き}**てくれてありがとう**。
examples.romaji: tooi tokoro made kite kurete arigatou.
examples.en: Thanks for coming all this way.

examples.ja: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しを{手伝|てつだ}っ**てくれてありがとう**。{本当|ほんとう}に{助|たす}かったよ。
examples.romaji: hikkoshi o tetsudatte kurete arigatou. hontou ni tasukatta yo.
examples.en: Thanks for helping me move. It really helped.

examples.ja: ～てくれてありがとう
examples.romaji: Thank someone for what they did
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Apologize for an action or situation
goal: You'll be able to say exactly what you are sorry for in a natural apology.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Apologize for an action or omission
text: ～てすみません gives the reason for an apology. ～なくてすみません apologizes for failing to do something.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～てすみません
text: Use 遅れてすみません for being late and 返事をしなくてすみません for not replying. For a completed past situation, すみませんでした is also natural.

formation: Verb て-form / negative ～なくて + すみません

examples.ja: {遅|おく}れ**てすみません**。
examples.romaji: okurete sumimasen.
examples.en: I am sorry I am late.

examples.ja: {昨日|きのう}はパーティーに{行|い}け**なくてすみません**でした。
examples.romaji: kinou wa paatii ni ikenakute sumimasen deshita.
examples.en: I'm sorry I couldn't make it to the party yesterday.

examples.ja: {返事|へんじ}をし**なくてすみませんでした**。
examples.romaji: henji o shinakute sumimasen deshita.
examples.en: I am sorry I did not reply.

examples.ja: {長|なが}く{待|ま}たせ**てすみません**。
examples.romaji: nagaku matasete sumimasen.
examples.en: I am sorry I kept you waiting so long.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}に{遅|おく}れ**てすみません**。{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まっていたんです。
examples.romaji: kaigi ni okurete sumimasen. densha ga tomatte ita n desu.
examples.en: Sorry I'm late for the meeting. The train had stopped.

examples.ja: {返事|へんじ}が{遅|おそ}くなっ**てすみません**。
examples.romaji: henji ga osoku natte sumimasen.
examples.en: Sorry for the late reply.

examples.ja: {長|なが}い{間|あいだ}{連絡|れんらく}し**なくてすみません**。
examples.romaji: nagai aida renraku shinakute sumimasen.
examples.en: Sorry for not being in touch for so long.

examples.ja: ～てすみません
examples.romaji: Apologize for an action or situation
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Give a firm but familiar instruction
goal: You'll be able to recognize and use a command common from parents, teachers, and authority figures.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Give a firm instruction
text: ～なさい is a direct instruction often used by parents or teachers to children. It is less blunt than a bare imperative but is not a general polite request to adults or superiors.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～なさい
text: Use 食べなさい, 書きなさい, しなさい, and 来なさい (きなさい). Remove ます before adding なさい. The speaker must have a suitable relationship or instructional role.

formation: Verb ます-stem + なさい

examples.ja: {手|て}を{洗|あら}い**なさい**。
examples.romaji: te o arainasai.
examples.en: Wash your hands.

examples.ja: {外|そと}は{寒|さむ}いから、コートを{着|き}**なさい**。
examples.romaji: soto wa samui kara, kooto o kinasai.
examples.en: It's cold outside, so put on your coat.

examples.ja: {名前|なまえ}を{書|か}き**なさい**。
examples.romaji: namae o kakinasai.
examples.en: Write your name.

examples.ja: {早|はや}く{寝|ね}**なさい**。
examples.romaji: hayaku nenasai.
examples.en: Go to bed early.

examples.ja: もう{十時|じゅうじ}だから、ゲームをやめ**なさい**。
examples.romaji: mou juuji da kara, geemu o yamenasai.
examples.en: It's already ten o'clock, so stop playing games.

examples.ja: {外|そと}から{帰|かえ}ったら、すぐ{着替|きが}え**なさい**。

title: A direct and forceful command
goal: You'll be able to form and understand strong commands while recognizing when their tone is appropriate.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Recognize a strong command
text: The bare imperative is a forceful command. It occurs in urgent warnings, sports instructions, and some quoted orders. In ordinary requests, choose a softer form appropriate to the relationship.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 1 · Godan
text: Change the final u-row kana to the e-row, without adding る. 待て is a command, while 待てる expresses ability.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 2 · Ichidan
text: Remove final る and add ろ. The alternative よ occurs in literary or formal commands.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 3 · Irregular
text: Memorize する→しろ and 来る→来い (こい). せよ is another formal imperative of する.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Imperative form
text: する becomes しろ and 来る becomes 来い (こい). Group 1 examples include 待て and 止まれ. Do not confuse the e-row imperative with a potential ending in る. Dictionary form + な is a prohibition, a separate formation.

formation: Group 2 without final る + ろ
Group 1 final u-row → e-row / Group 2 without る + ろ

title: Tell or ask someone to do something indirectly
goal: You'll be able to report an instruction or request without quoting the exact words.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Report an instruction indirectly
text: ～ように言う reports telling someone to do or not do something without repeating the exact command. The person receiving the instruction normally takes に.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ように言う
text: Use 来るように言う and 遅れないように言う. This is not the volitional form. Keep separate the person giving the instruction and the person expected to act.

formation: Person に + dictionary or ない-form verb + ように言う

title: Say what was done and who received the action
goal: You'll be able to shift attention from the person acting to the person or thing affected.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe someone receiving an action
text: The passive makes the recipient of an action the subject. It is useful for saying someone was praised, invited, or affected. It can also describe facts without foregrounding an actor.

Passive forms are built according to verb group, as the next steps show. Verbs that take no direct object — such as 泳ぐ or 死ぬ — can also become passive. Because they have no direct object to promote, their affected-person use is the indirect passive in the next lesson.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 1 · Godan
text: Change the final u-row kana to the a-row and add れる. For final う, use わ: 買う→買われる.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 2 · Ichidan
text: Remove final る and add られる. These forms look identical to Group 2 potentials; the sentence roles distinguish them.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 3 · Irregular
text: する becomes される; 来る becomes 来られる (こられる). Conjugate the result as a Group 2 verb.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Passive form (～れる・～られる)
text: う changes to わ before れる: 買う→買われる. する→される and 来る→来られる (こられる). The actor often takes に. Passive verbs conjugate like Group 2 verbs. Not every passive describes suffering.

formation: Group 2 without final る + られる
Group 1 a-row stem + れる / Group 2 without る + られる

title: An event affects someone negatively
goal: You'll be able to describe an action that caused inconvenience, distress, or an unwanted effect.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Show how an event affected someone
text: An indirect passive describes an event from the viewpoint of someone affected by it, often inconveniently. English may naturally use an active sentence plus the effect on that person.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Indirect passive
text: The original object can remain marked を, as in ケーキを食べられた. Intransitive events can also be passive: 雨に降られた. State the affected person or consequence clearly so the viewpoint makes sense.

formation: Affected person + は + Actor or cause + に + Passive verb

examples.en: Mei ate Ren's cake, to his dismay.

examples.en: The baby cried in the middle of the night, and I couldn't get much sleep.

examples.romaji: ame ni furarete, nurete shimaimashita.

examples.romaji: densha no naka de, tonari no hito ni ashi o fumaremashita.
examples.en: On the train, the person next to me stepped on my foot.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}{中|ちゅう}ずっと{雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}ら**れて**、どこにも{行|い}けませんでした。

title: Make or let someone do something
goal: You'll be able to describe causing, requiring, or allowing another person to act.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Make or let someone act
text: The causative describes causing or allowing another person to do something. Context decides whether it means making, having, or letting them act.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 1 · Godan
text: Change the final u-row kana to the a-row and add せる. Final う uses わ: 買う→買わせる.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 2 · Ichidan
text: Remove final る and add させる. The resulting verb expresses causing or allowing the action.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 3 · Irregular
text: する becomes させる; 来る becomes 来させる (こさせる). The causative then conjugates like a Group 2 verb.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Causative form (～せる・～させる)
text: する→させる, 来る→来させる (こさせる), 買う→買わせる. With a transitive action, the person acting usually takes に and the object を. With an intransitive action, を often marks the person; に is also possible depending on agency and context.

formation: Group 2 without final る + させる
Group 1 a-row stem + せる / Group 2 without る + させる

title: Please let me do this
goal: You'll be able to ask permission to take an action while showing that the decision belongs to the listener.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Ask to be allowed to act
text: Causative て-form + ください asks permission for the speaker to perform an action. It often translates as “please let me.”

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～(さ)せてください
text: Make the causative first: 説明する→説明させる→説明させてください. The speaker is normally the person asking to act, not someone requesting that a third person be forced.

formation: Causative verb て-form + ください

examples.ja: {私|わたし}に{手伝|てつだ}わ**せてください**。
examples.romaji: watashi ni tetsudawasete kudasai.
examples.en: Please let me help.

examples.ja: {今日|きょう}は{私|わたし}に{払|はら}わ**せてください**。
examples.romaji: kyou wa watashi ni harawasete kudasai.
examples.en: Please let me pay today.

examples.ja: ここで{少|すこ}し{休|やす}ま**せてください**。

examples.en: Please let me rest here for a while.

examples.en: I have a fever, so please let me go home early today.

examples.ja: その{仕事|しごと}、ぜひ{私|わたし}にやら**せてください**。
examples.romaji: sono shigoto, zehi watashi ni yarasete kudasai.
examples.en: Please let me do that job.

examples.en: I can't decide right away. Please let me think about it a little.

title: Be made to do something
goal: You'll be able to say that someone was forced or pressured to perform an action.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Describe being made to do something
text: The causative-passive puts the person made to act at the center. It often conveys lack of choice or reluctance. The person causing the action commonly takes に.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 1 · Godan
text: Use the full causative ending ～せる, remove its final る, and add られる. Many Group 1 forms also have a shorter ～される form after the a-row stem.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 2 · Ichidan
text: Remove final る and add させられる. Group 2 verbs do not use the common Group 1 shortening.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Group 3 · Irregular
text: する becomes させられる; 来る becomes 来させられる (こさせられる). Keep the person made to act as the topic or subject.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Causative-passive form
text: Examples are 書かせられる, 食べさせられる, させられる, 来させられる. Many Group 1 forms shorten, such as 待たせられる→待たされる. Verbs ending in す normally retain the full form; do not make 話さされる. The result conjugates like Group 2.

formation: Group 2 without final る + させられる
Causative verb without final る + られる

title: Add politeness or respect to words
goal: You'll be able to use common polite prefixes naturally with Japanese and Sino-Japanese words.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Use conventional polite prefixes
text: お～ and ご～ can make conventional expressions polite, respectful, or refined. They appear in everyday words as well as honorific and humble patterns.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use お～・ご～
text: お often accompanies native Japanese words and ご often accompanies Sino-Japanese words, but there are exceptions such as お電話. Learn conventional combinations; do not add a prefix to every noun. お茶 is ordinary polite vocabulary even for your own tea.

formation: お / ご + Conventional noun or expression

examples.ja: **お**{名前|なまえ}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.romaji: onamae o oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: Please tell me your name.

examples.ja: **ご**{家族|かぞく}は{何人|なんにん}ですか。
examples.romaji: gokazoku wa nannin desu ka.
examples.en: How many people are there in your family?

examples.ja: **ご**{住所|じゅうしょ}を{書|か}いてください。
examples.romaji: gojuusho o kaite kudasai.
examples.en: Please write your address.

examples.ja: **お**{茶|ちゃ}をどうぞ。
examples.romaji: ocha o douzo.
examples.en: Please have some tea.

examples.ja: いらっしゃいませ。**お**{飲|の}み{物|もの}は{何|なに}になさいますか。
examples.romaji: irasshaimase. onomimono wa nani ni nasaimasu ka.
examples.en: Welcome. What would you like to drink?

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}、**お**{元気|げんき}ですか。
examples.romaji: sensei, ogenki desu ka.
examples.en: How are you, Professor?

examples.ja: すみません、**お**{手洗|てあら}いはどこですか。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, otearai wa doko desu ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

pattern: ございます・でございます
title: Very polite forms of ある and です
goal: You'll be able to recognize and use extra-polite statements about existence and identity in customer service and formal settings.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Use a formal polite ending
text: ございます is a formal polite counterpart of あります. でございます is a formal polite counterpart of です after a noun or な-adjective. They are common in service encounters and formal introductions.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ございます・でございます
text: Use 部屋がございます for availability and 受付でございます for identification. Neither form is an honorific replacement for a person's いる. Avoid adding でございます directly to an い-adjective.

formation: Thing or availability + ございます / Noun or な-adjective stem + でございます

examples.ja: こちらが{受付|うけつけ}**でございます**。
examples.romaji: kochira ga uketsuke de gozaimasu.
examples.en: This is the reception desk.

examples.ja: お{手洗|てあら}いは{二階|にかい}に**ございます**。
examples.romaji: otearai wa nikai ni gozaimasu.
examples.en: The restroom is on the second floor.

examples.ja: {空|あ}いている{部屋|へや}が**ございます**。
examples.romaji: aite iru heya ga gozaimasu.
examples.en: There is a room available.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{健太|けんた}**でございます**。
examples.romaji: watashi wa kenta de gozaimasu.
examples.en: I am Kenta.

examples.ja: いらっしゃいませ。こちらが{本日|ほんじつ}のメニュー**でございます**。
examples.romaji: irasshaimase. kochira ga honjitsu no menyuu de gozaimasu.
examples.en: Welcome. Here is today's menu.

examples.ja: はい、{山田|やまだ}ホテル**でございます**。
examples.romaji: hai, yamada hoteru de gozaimasu.
examples.en: Hello, Yamada Hotel.

examples.ja: このシャツは、{大|おお}きいサイズも**ございます**よ。
examples.romaji: kono shatsu wa, ookii saizu mo gozaimasu yo.
examples.en: This shirt also comes in a larger size.

title: Ask a careful and polite question
goal: You'll be able to soften a question when speaking to customers, strangers, or people in authority.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Ask a careful question
text: ～でしょうか softens an inquiry or presents a tentative question. It is useful with strangers or in formal settings, and does not always express probability.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～でしょうか
text: Use どちらでしょうか for a careful direction question and 大丈夫でしょうか to check acceptability. Do not insert だ before でしょうか.

formation: Plain clause / Noun / な-adjective stem + でしょうか

examples.ja: {駅|えき}はどちら**でしょうか**。
examples.romaji: eki wa dochira deshou ka.
examples.en: Could you tell me which way the station is?

examples.ja: すみません、この{席|せき}は{空|あ}いている**でしょうか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, kono seki wa aite iru deshou ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, is this seat free?

examples.ja: {今|いま}、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}**でしょうか**。
examples.romaji: ima, daijoubu deshou ka.
examples.en: Would now be all right?

examples.ja: {何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まる**でしょうか**。
examples.romaji: nanji ni hajimaru deshou ka.
examples.en: What time will it begin, I wonder?

examples.ja: すみません、お{手洗|てあら}いはどちら**でしょうか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, otearai wa dochira deshou ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, which way is the restroom?

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{会議|かいぎ}は{何時|なんじ}から**でしょうか**。
examples.romaji: ashita no kaigi wa nanji kara deshou ka.
examples.en: What time does tomorrow's meeting start?

examples.en: Excuse me, can I use this card?

pattern: お～ください・ご～ください
title: Make a respectful request or instruction
goal: You'll be able to ask someone to act politely in customer service, announcements, and formal situations.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Make a respectful instruction
text: お～ください and ご～ください respectfully ask the listener to perform an action. They are common in reception, announcements, and service instructions.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use お～ください・ご～ください
text: Use established forms such as お待ちください and ご記入ください. Some verbs have special forms, such as ご覧ください. Prefix choice is lexical, not a rule that works with every verb.

formation: お + Verb ます-stem + ください / ご + Verbal noun + ください

examples.ja: こちらで**お**{待|ま}ち**ください**。
examples.romaji: kochira de omachi kudasai.
examples.en: Please wait here.

examples.ja: ドアが{閉|し}まります。**ご{注意|ちゅうい}ください**。
examples.romaji: doa ga shimarimasu. gochuui kudasai.
examples.en: The doors are closing. Please be careful.

examples.ja: {少|すこ}し**お**{待|ま}ち**ください**。
examples.romaji: sukoshi omachi kudasai.
examples.en: Please wait a moment.

examples.ja: {お名前|おなまえ}を**ご**{記入|きにゅう}**ください**。
examples.romaji: onamae o gokinyuu kudasai.
examples.en: Please enter your name.

examples.ja: この{写真|しゃしん}を**ご{覧|らん}ください**。
examples.romaji: kono shashin o goran kudasai.
examples.en: Please look at this photograph.

examples.ja: お{名前|なまえ}をお{呼|よ}びするまで、いすに{座|すわ}って**お{待|ま}ちください**。
examples.romaji: onamae o oyobi suru made, isu ni suwatte omachi kudasai.
examples.en: Please take a seat and wait until your name is called.

examples.ja: エレベーターはこちらです。どうぞ**ご{利用|りよう}ください**。
examples.romaji: erebeetaa wa kochira desu. douzo goriyou kudasai.
examples.en: The elevator is this way. Please feel free to use it.

examples.ja: お{荷物|にもつ}はこちらに**お{置|お}きください**。
examples.romaji: onimotsu wa kochira ni ooki kudasai.
examples.en: Please put your bags here.

examples.romaji: Make a respectful request or instruction

title: Respectfully describe another person's action
goal: You'll be able to raise the person performing an action with a general honorific pattern.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Respectfully describe another person's action
text: お～になる and ご～になる raise the person performing an action. They are used for someone you are treating respectfully, not for honoring your own actions.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use お～になる・ご～になる
text: Use established expressions such as お読みになる and ご利用になる. Special honorific verbs are preferred for many common actions. Avoid redundant forms such as お読みになられる.

formation: お + Verb ます-stem + になる / ご + Verbal noun + になる

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{新|あたら}しい{車|くるま}に**お**{乗|の}り**になります**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa atarashii kuruma ni onori ni narimasu.
examples.en: The teacher gets into the new car.

examples.ja: この{本|ほん}は{山田|やまだ}{先生|せんせい}が**お{書|か}きになりました**。
examples.romaji: kono hon wa yamada sensei ga okaki ni narimashita.
examples.en: Professor Yamada wrote this book.

examples.ja: {何時|なんじ}に**お**{帰|かえ}り**になりますか**。
examples.romaji: nanji ni okaeri ni narimasu ka.
examples.en: What time will you go home?

examples.ja: こちらの{部屋|へや}を**ご**{利用|りよう}**になりますか**。
examples.romaji: kochira no heya o goriyou ni narimasu ka.
examples.en: Will you use this room?

examples.ja: {社長|しゃちょう}はもう**お{帰|かえ}りになりました**。
examples.romaji: shachou wa mou okaeri ni narimashita.
examples.en: The company president has already gone home.

examples.ja: {部長|ぶちょう}は{明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}{九時|くじ}に{空港|くうこう}に**お{着|つ}きになります**。

examples.en: The manager will arrive at the airport at nine tomorrow morning.

title: Respectful verbs for common actions
goal: You'll be able to recognize and use special respectful forms for actions such as going, saying, seeing, and eating.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Recognize special respectful verbs
text: Some frequent actions have established honorific replacements. They respectfully describe another person's action rather than merely adding polite ます.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Special honorific verbs
text: 行く/来る/いる→いらっしゃる; 言う→おっしゃる; する→なさる; 食べる/飲む→召し上がる; 見る→ご覧になる; くれる→くださる. Learn the special polite forms いらっしゃいます, おっしゃいます, なさいます, くださいます.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}が**いらっしゃいます**。
examples.romaji: sensei ga irasshaimasu.
examples.en: The teacher is here.

examples.ja: {行|い}く・{来|く}る・いる → **いらっしゃる**
examples.romaji: いらっしゃる respects another person's movement or presence; polite いらっしゃいます.
examples.en: go / come / be

examples.ja: {言|い}う → **おっしゃる**
examples.romaji: おっしゃる respects another person's speech; polite おっしゃいます.
examples.en: say

examples.ja: する → **なさる**
examples.romaji: なさる respects another person's action; polite なさいます.
examples.en: do

examples.ja: {食|た}べる・{飲|の}む → **{召|め}し{上|あ}がる**
examples.romaji: 召し上がる respects the person eating or drinking.
examples.en: eat / drink

examples.ja: {見|み}る → **ご{覧|らん}になる**
examples.romaji: ご覧になる is the established respectful counterpart of 見る.
examples.en: look / watch

examples.ja: くれる → **くださる**
examples.romaji: くださる respects the giver; polite くださいます.
examples.en: give to me / my side

examples.ja: {行|い}く・{来|く}る・いる → **いらっしゃる**
examples.romaji: iku・kuru・iru → irassharu

examples.ja: {言|い}う → **おっしゃる**
examples.romaji: iu → ossharu

examples.ja: する → **なさる**
examples.romaji: suru → nasaru

examples.ja: {食|た}べる・{飲|の}む → **{召|め}し{上|あ}がる**

examples.ja: {見|み}る → **ご{覧|らん}になる**
examples.romaji: miru → goran ni naru

examples.romaji: kureru → kudasaru

examples.en: That is what the teacher said.

examples.romaji: shachou wa ima, kaigishitsu ni irasshaimasu.
examples.en: The company president is in the meeting room now.

title: Show respect with a verb ending
goal: You'll be able to recognize the respectful use of the passive-shaped verb form from context.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Recognize respect expressed with passive-shaped forms
text: ～れる and ～られる can respectfully describe someone's action. The form matches the passive, but context shows that the subject is performing the action and is being respected.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～れる・～られる (honorific)
text: する→される and 来る→来られる. Actor and object roles distinguish honorific from passive; ability context may distinguish potential. Do not combine this mechanically with another honorific such as お読みになる.

formation: Group 1 a-row stem + れる / Group 2 without る + られる

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{黒板|こくばん}に{字|じ}を{書|か}か**れます**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa kokuban ni ji o kakaremasu.
examples.en: The teacher writes characters on the blackboard.

examples.ja: {社長|しゃちょう}は{明日|あした}{大阪|おおさか}へ{行|い}か**れます**。
examples.romaji: shachou wa ashita oosaka e ikaremasu.
examples.en: The company president is going to Osaka tomorrow.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}はこの{本|ほん}を{読|よ}ま**れます**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa kono hon o yomaremasu.
examples.en: The teacher reads this book.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{朝ご飯|あさごはん}を{食|た}べ**られました**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa asagohan o taberaremashita.
examples.en: The teacher ate breakfast.

examples.ja: {何時|なんじ}に{出発|しゅっぱつ}**されますか**。
examples.romaji: nanji ni shuppatsu saremasu ka.
examples.en: What time will you depart?

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{学生|がくせい}を{褒|ほ}め**られました**。
examples.romaji: Honorific ～られる
examples.en: 先生 performs the praise; the ending shows respect for the teacher.

examples.ja: {学生|がくせい}は{先生|せんせい}に{褒|ほ}め**られました**。
examples.romaji: Passive ～られる
examples.en: 学生 receives the praise; 先生に names the person who gave it.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{毎朝|まいあさ}{公園|こうえん}を{散歩|さんぽ}**されます**。
examples.romaji: sensei wa maiasa kouen o sanpo saremasu.
examples.en: The professor takes a walk in the park every morning.

examples.ja: {部長|ぶちょう}はもう{帰|かえ}ら**れました**。
examples.romaji: buchou wa mou kaeraremashita.
examples.en: The manager has already gone home.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}は{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}にどんな{本|ほん}を{読|よ}ま**れます**か。
examples.romaji: sensei wa yasumi no hi ni donna hon o yomaremasu ka.
examples.en: What kind of books do you read on your days off, Professor?

examples.ja: ～れる・～られる (honorific)
examples.romaji: Show respect with a verb ending

title: Humbly describe your action for someone
goal: You'll be able to lower your own action to show respect toward the person it affects.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Humbly present an action for another person
text: お～する and ご～する humbly describe the speaker's or in-group's action directed toward someone being respected. They do not lower the listener's action.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use お～する・ご～する
text: Use established expressions such as お送りします and ご案内します. The respected recipient or destination makes the relationship meaningful. For their action, use an honorific instead.

formation: お + Verb ます-stem + する / ご + Verbal noun + する

examples.ja: {私|わたし}が{お荷物|おにもつ}を**お**{持|も}ち**します**。
examples.romaji: watashi ga onimotsu o omochi shimasu.
examples.en: I will carry your luggage.

examples.ja: {後|あと}でこちらから**お{電話|でんわ}します**。
examples.romaji: ato de kochira kara odenwa shimasu.
examples.en: I'll call you back later.

examples.ja: {駅|えき}まで**ご**{案内|あんない}**します**。
examples.romaji: eki made goannai shimasu.
examples.en: I will guide you to the station.

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}にメールを**お**{送|おく}り**します**。
examples.romaji: sensei ni meeru o ookuri shimasu.
examples.en: I will send the teacher an email.

examples.ja: {重|おも}そうですね。**お{手伝|てつだ}いしましょう**か。
examples.romaji: omosou desu ne. otetsudai shimashou ka.
examples.en: That looks heavy. May I help you?

examples.ja: お{部屋|へや}まで**ご{案内|あんない}します**。
examples.romaji: oheya made goannai shimasu.
examples.en: I'll show you to your room.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{地図|ちず}をメールで**お{送|おく}りします**。
examples.romaji: ashita, chizu o meeru de ookuri shimasu.
examples.en: I'll send you a map by email tomorrow.

examples.ja: お～する・ご～する
examples.romaji: Humbly describe your action for someone

title: Modest verbs for your own actions
goal: You'll be able to recognize and use special humble forms for actions such as going, saying, asking, and seeing.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Use established humble and formal verbs
text: Some common actions use special humble or formal replacements. They describe the speaker's side appropriately when addressing someone respectfully.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use Special humble verbs
text: 伺う means humbly visit or ask; 拝見する means humbly look; いただく means receive or eat/drink humbly. 参る, 申す, いたす, and おる formally present one's own going/coming, speech, doing, and presence. Do not use them to lower a respected customer's action.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}、{先生|せんせい}の{お宅|おたく}に**{伺|うかが}います**。
examples.romaji: ashita, sensei no otaku ni ukagaimasu.
examples.en: I will visit the teacher's home tomorrow.

examples.ja: {訪|たず}ねる・{聞|き}く → **{伺|うかが}う**
examples.romaji: 伺う humbly presents a visit or question directed to a respected person.
examples.en: visit / ask

examples.ja: {見|み}る → **{拝見|はいけん}する**
examples.romaji: 拝見する humbly presents the speaker's looking at something connected to the respected person.
examples.en: look

examples.ja: もらう・{食|た}べる・{飲|の}む → **いただく**
examples.romaji: いただく is the established humble counterpart for these actions.
examples.en: receive / eat / drink

examples.ja: {行|い}く・{来|く}る → **{参|まい}る**
examples.romaji: 参る formally presents one's own movement to the listener.
examples.en: go / come

examples.romaji: 申す formally presents one's own speech or name.
examples.en: say / be named

examples.ja: する → **いたす**
examples.romaji: いたす formally presents one's own action.
examples.en: do

examples.ja: いる → **おる**
examples.romaji: おる formally presents one's own presence.
examples.en: be present

examples.ja: {訪|たず}ねる・{聞|き}く → **{伺|うかが}う**
examples.romaji: tazuneru・kiku → ukagau

examples.ja: {見|み}る → **{拝見|はいけん}する**
examples.romaji: miru → haiken suru

examples.ja: もらう・{食|た}べる・{飲|の}む → **いただく**
examples.romaji: morau・taberu・nomu → itadaku

examples.ja: {行|い}く・{来|く}る → **{参|まい}る**
examples.romaji: iku・kuru → mairu
iu → mousu

examples.ja: する → **いたす**
examples.romaji: suru → itasu

examples.ja: いる → **おる**
examples.romaji: iru → oru

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}を**{拝見|はいけん}しました**。
examples.romaji: shiryou o haiken shimashita.
examples.en: I looked at the materials.

examples.ja: {私|わたし}は{健太|けんた}と**{申|もう}します**。
examples.romaji: watashi wa kenta to moushimasu.
examples.en: My name is Kenta.

examples.ja: {明日|あした}の{午後|ごご}、そちらの{事務所|じむしょ}に**{伺|うかが}います**。
examples.romaji: ashita no gogo, sochira no jimusho ni ukagaimasu.
examples.en: I'll come to your office tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ja: {初|はじ}めまして。ワンと**{申|もう}します**。
examples.romaji: hajimemashite. wan to moushimasu.
examples.en: Nice to meet you. My name is Wang.

examples.ja: お{客|きゃく}{様|さま}、{切符|きっぷ}を**{拝見|はいけん}します**。
examples.romaji: okyakusama, kippu o haiken shimasu.
examples.en: May I see your ticket, please?

title: Could you please do this for me?
goal: You'll be able to make a highly considerate request in formal or unfamiliar situations.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Make a deferential request
text: ～ていただけませんか asks whether the speaker could receive the favor of the listener's action. It is a considerate request suited to strangers, teachers, or formal situations.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～ていただけませんか
text: いただける is the potential of humble いただく. The negative polite question conventionally softens the request; it does not imply that refusal is expected.

formation: Verb て-form + いただけませんか

examples.ja: {もう一度|もういちど}{説明|せつめい}し**ていただけませんか**。
examples.romaji: mou ichido setsumei shite itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please explain it once more?

examples.ja: {先生|せんせい}、{私|わたし}の{作文|さくぶん}を{見|み}**ていただけませんか**。
examples.romaji: sensei, watashi no sakubun o mite itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Professor, would you be willing to look over my essay?

examples.ja: ここに{お名前|おなまえ}を{書|か}い**ていただけませんか**。
examples.romaji: koko ni onamae o kaite itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please write your name here?

examples.ja: {写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}**っていただけませんか**。
examples.romaji: shashin o totte itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please take a photograph for us?

examples.ja: すみません、もう{少|すこ}しゆっくり{話|はな}し**ていただけませんか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, mou sukoshi yukkuri hanashite itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, could you possibly speak a little more slowly?

examples.ja: すみません、この{漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}み{方|かた}を{教|おし}え**ていただけませんか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, kono kanji no yomikata o oshiete itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, could you possibly tell me how to read this kanji?

examples.ja: すみません、{駅|えき}までの{地図|ちず}を{書|か}い**ていただけませんか**。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, eki made no chizu o kaite itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, would you mind drawing me a map to the station?

examples.ja: ～ていただけませんか
examples.romaji: Could you please do this for me?
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.

title: Present alternatives in formal language
goal: You'll be able to connect two choices with a clear written or formal equivalent of or.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Present formal alternatives
text: または connects alternatives in instructions or formal explanations. It means or, allowing a choice according to the surrounding rule.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use または
text: It is more formal than many everyday spoken choices. It does not by itself settle whether choosing both is allowed; the instruction must make that clear when it matters.

formation: Alternative A + または + Alternative B

examples.ja: {現金|げんきん}**または**カードで{払|はら}ってください。
examples.romaji: genkin mata wa kaado de haratte kudasai.
examples.en: Please pay by cash or card.

examples.ja: {答|こた}えはひらがな**または**カタカナで{書|か}いてください。
examples.romaji: kotae wa hiragana matawa katakana de kaite kudasai.
examples.en: Write your answers in hiragana or katakana.

examples.ja: {電話|でんわ}**または**メールで{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.romaji: denwa mata wa meeru de renraku shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please contact us by telephone or email.

examples.ja: {月曜日|げつようび}**または**{火曜日|かようび}に{来|き}てください。
examples.romaji: getsuyoubi mata wa kayoubi ni kite kudasai.
examples.en: Please come on Monday or Tuesday.

examples.ja: {予約|よやく}は{電話|でんわ}**または**メールでお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.romaji: yoyaku wa denwa matawa meeru de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Please make reservations by phone or email.

examples.ja: ご{記入|きにゅう}は{黒|くろ}**または**{青|あお}のペンでお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.romaji: gokinyuu wa kuro matawa ao no pen de onegai shimasu.
examples.en: Please fill this out in black or blue pen.

examples.ja: {入口|いりぐち}でチケット**または**{予約|よやく}のメールをお{見|み}せください。
examples.romaji: iriguchi de chiketto matawa yoyaku no meeru o omise kudasai.
examples.en: Please show your ticket or your booking email at the entrance.

examples.ja: または

title: List casual examples in conversation
goal: You'll be able to give a loose sample of items while signalling that the list is incomplete.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: List examples without exhausting the set
text: ～とか～とか lists representative items or actions, often conversationally. It suggests there may be other examples as well.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use ～とか～とか
text: Nouns can be followed by another particle after the list. Verb lists often end with する. Unlike an exhaustive と list, とか presents examples rather than a complete inventory.

formation: Noun or plain clause + とか + Another example + とか

examples.ja: {休日|きゅうじつ}はキャンプ**とか**バーベキュー**とか**を{楽|たの}しみます。
examples.romaji: kyuujitsu wa kyanpu toka baabekyuu toka o tanoshimimasu.
examples.en: On holidays, we enjoy things such as camping and barbecues.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}では、すし**とか**ラーメン**とか**を{食|た}べたいです。
examples.romaji: nihon de wa, sushi toka raamen toka o tabetai desu.
examples.en: In Japan, I want to eat things like sushi and ramen.

examples.ja: {本|ほん}**とか**{雑誌|ざっし}**とか**を{読|よ}みます。
examples.romaji: hon toka zasshi toka o yomimasu.
examples.en: I read things such as books and magazines.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みは{散歩|さんぽ}する**とか**{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む**とか**します。
examples.romaji: yasumi wa sanpo suru toka hon o yomu toka shimasu.
examples.en: On days off I do things such as take walks and read books.

examples.ja: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{洗濯|せんたく}**とか**{掃除|そうじ}とかをしています。
examples.romaji: shuumatsu wa sentaku toka souji toka o shite imasu.
examples.en: On weekends I do things like laundry and cleaning.

examples.ja: {旅行|りょこう}には、{薬|くすり}**とか**{傘|かさ}とかを{持|も}っていったほうがいいよ。
examples.romaji: ryokou ni wa, kusuri toka kasa toka o motte itta hou ga ii yo.
examples.en: You should take things like medicine and an umbrella on the trip.

examples.ja: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は、{映画|えいが}を{見|み}る**とか**{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}くとかしています。
examples.romaji: yasumi no hi wa, eiga o miru toka kaimono ni iku toka shite imasu.
examples.en: On my days off, I do things like watching movies and going shopping.

examples.ja: ～とか～とか
examples.romaji: List casual examples in conversation

title: Introduce an example
goal: You'll be able to back up a general statement with a concrete case.

sections.label: Why it means that
sections.heading: Make an idea concrete with an example
text: たとえば introduces a specific illustration of a broader statement. The example clarifies the idea without claiming it is the only possibility.

sections.label: How it is built
sections.heading: Form and use たとえば
text: It can introduce a whole sentence or a shorter phrase. Use an example that actually belongs to the stated category. It is not a cause-and-result connector like それで.

formation: General statement + たとえば + Example

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きです。**たとえば**、お{寿司|すし}や{天|てん}ぷらです。
examples.romaji: nihon no ryouri ga suki desu. tatoeba, osushi ya tenpura desu.
examples.en: I like Japanese cuisine. For example, sushi and tempura.

examples.ja: {東京|とうきょう}には{有名|ゆうめい}な{場所|ばしょ}がたくさんあります。**たとえば**、{浅草|あさくさ}や{渋谷|しぶや}です。
examples.romaji: toukyou ni wa yuumei na basho ga takusan arimasu. tatoeba, asakusa ya shibuya desu.
examples.en: Tokyo has many famous places. For example, Asakusa and Shibuya.

examples.ja: {運動|うんどう}をしましょう。**たとえば**、{散歩|さんぽ}はどうですか。
examples.romaji: undou o shimashou. tatoeba, sanpo wa dou desu ka.
examples.en: Let's get some exercise. How about walking, for example?

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{町|まち}に{行|い}きたいです。**たとえば**、{京都|きょうと}です。
examples.romaji: nihon no machi ni ikitai desu. tatoeba, kyouto desu.
examples.en: I want to visit a Japanese city, Kyoto for example.

examples.ja: {日本|にほん}の{冬|ふゆ}の{料理|りょうり}が{好|す}きです。**たとえば**、お{鍋|なべ}です。
examples.romaji: nihon no fuyu no ryouri ga suki desu. tatoeba, onabe desu.
examples.en: I like Japanese winter dishes. For example, hot pot.

examples.ja: {簡単|かんたん}な{運動|うんどう}から{始|はじ}めましょう。**たとえば**、{毎日|まいにち}{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}{歩|ある}くのはどうですか。
examples.romaji: kantan na undou kara hajimemashou. tatoeba, mainichi sanjuppun aruku no wa dou desu ka.
examples.en: Let's start with some easy exercise. For example, how about walking thirty minutes a day?

examples.ja: {体|からだ}にいい{飲|の}み{物|もの}を{飲|の}みましょう。**たとえば**、お{茶|ちゃ}や{水|みず}です。
examples.romaji: karada ni ii nomimono o nomimashou. tatoeba, ocha ya mizu desu.
examples.en: Let's drink things that are good for us. For example, tea and water.

examples.ja: たとえば
examples.romaji: Introduce an example
examples.en: 6 more examples in the grammar path — free for a limited time.
